news.title: Argentina Offers Economic Plan, Hoping to Sidestep Court

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld acknowledges for first time that American troops in Afghanistan might have mistakenly killed or wounded friendly Afghans in raids on two compounds north of Kandahar in January; previously dismissed claims by Afghan villagers that American airstrikes or raids had erred; says US forces may have been fired on first, then returned fire; says incident reflects often confusing situation on ground with uncertain loyalties and imperfect intelligence posing huge challenges for American troops (M)
news.title: Error Possible In Attacks, Rumsfeld Says

news.abstract: Abel Pacheco and Rolando Araya, candidates of Costa Rica's two main parties, will face each other in April runoff after neither manages to secure outright victory in February 3 presidential election (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Costa Rica: Runoff In Presidential Race

news.abstract: Interview with Benjamin Ben-Eliezer, Israel's defense minister and newly elected leader of its labor Party--in theory most powerful left-leaning counterweight inside or outside government to Prime Min Ariel Sharon's rightist Likud; he comments on holding both jobs and clash of values it can create; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli's Dual Job: Chief of Defense, and Dissent

news.abstract: New senate, equally divided between Hutus and Tutsis, is formally installed as part of Burundi's continuing effort to end ethnic strife (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Burundi: Another Step In Peace Effort

news.abstract: Eight-year investigation into web of corruption linked to Elf Aquitaine, former state-owned French oil company, officially ends; implicated more than 40 people, including former minister Charles Pasqua who is presidential candidate; allegations date from before privatization in 1994, era when French government used company as tool of foreign policy, especially in Africa where it had huge investments; investigators say company amassed multimillion-dollar slush fund that was sometimes used to gain influence and win contracts and was siphoned off by politicians and directors (M)
news.title: 8-Year Investigation of Corruption at French Oil Company Ends

news.abstract: Sec of State Colin L Powell tells Senate committee that United States expects to meet Russia's demand for legally binding agreement on reducing nuclear warheads, whether that takes form of treaty approved by Congress or some less formal document; leaves most details unspecified, and officials say they are still being worked out; Sen Chuck Hagel expresses misgivings about Pres Bush's linking of Iraq, Iran and North Korea in 'axis of evil,' and Powell replies that Bush was serious and not using rhetorical flourish (M)
news.title: POWELL SAYS U.S. PLANS TO WORK OUT BINDING ARMS PACT

news.abstract: Italian Senate votes to let exiled male heirs of Vittorio Emanuele III back into country (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Royal Exiles Win Round 1

news.abstract: Celebration of Queen Elizabeth II's 50th year on British throne gets off to inauspicious start, and there are fears that it might become rerun of botched millennium celebrations; British public has become less deferential to monarchy and less appreciative of royal family since 1977, when queen had triumphant Silver Jubilee; photo (M)
news.title: London Journal; Uneasy Heads in the Palace: Will Jubilee Year Flop?

news.abstract: Didier Schuller is extradited to Paris, where he is expected to give testimony to support longstanding allegations of large-scale illicit funding scheme when city's mayor was Jacques Chirac, now president of France; people in Chirac's Rally for the Republic Party, accuse Socialist government of timing extradition to undermine Chirac's re-election chances; polls have only recently and only slightly turned in favor of Chirac's likely challenger, Prime Min Lionel Jospin, Socialist leader; photo (M)
news.title: Fugitive, Returning to France, Jolts Presidential Campaign

news.abstract: US intelligence officials say CIA has no evidence that Iraq has engaged in terrorist operations against United States in nearly a decade and is also convinced that Pres Saddam Hussein has not provided chemical or biological weapons to Al Qaeda or related terrorist groups; say agency believes meeting in Prague between Mohamed Atta, leader of hijacking teams of Sept 11, and Iraqi intelligence officer does not provide sufficient evidence of Iraqi involvement; say agency's greatest concern with Iraq is its continuing development of chemical and biological weapons (M)
news.title: Terror Acts By Baghdad Have Waned, U.S. Aides Say

news.abstract: French Foreign Min Hubert Vedrine openly criticizes Washington's approach to terrorism as 'simplistic' and scores United States for conducting foreign policy without consulting its allies; remarks seen as sign of frustration with Pres Bush's worldview as described in his State of Union address; Vedrine, in interview on France's Inter radio, suggests Europeans must speak out more and more because they face US that acts 'unilaterally' based only on its own interests; Secretary of State Colin L Powell rejects criticism, saying it is far from truth; Vedrine's comments may be harshest yet, but other European leaders are also beginning to distance themselves from Washington; even British Prime Min Tony Blair has warned against military strike on Iraq unless clear connection is found between it and Sept 11 attacks; photo (M)
news.title: French Minister Calls U.S. Policy 'Simplistic'

news.abstract: President Bush has decided to apply the Geneva Convention to Taliban fighters, the White House announced today.
news.title: Geneva Convention to Be Applied to Captured Taliban Fighters

news.abstract: France's highest appeals court upholds three-month jail term for Jose Bove for his ransacking of MacDonald's restaurant site in Millau in 1999 to protest American trade policy (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Sentence For Big Mac Attacker

news.abstract: Pres Fidel Castro of Cuba has muted his hostile remarks about Washington and offered to cooperate with Bush administration's war on terrorism in wake of Sept 11 attacks; within hours of attacks, he offered medical help as well as intelligence on movement of terrorists; Castro has not criticized United States decision to detain Taliban and Al Qaeda prisoners at American military base at Guantanamo Bay; his warmer tone appears to be part of effort to avoid deterioration in relations with Washington as Cuba faces its own economic crisis; photo (M)
news.title: Cuba, Too, Felt the Sept. 11 Shock Waves, With a More Genial Castro Offering Help

news.abstract: German unemployment figures rise sharply in Jan, above psychologically important four milion total; new figure is political blow to Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, who said four years ago that if his governement could not hold number below 3.5 million by next election, which is scheduled for Sept 22, it would not deserve to be re-elected; adding to Schroder's woes is budding scandal about falsification of job-creation figures by state employment offices (M)
news.title: German Unemployment Is Growing Problem for Schröder

news.abstract: Officials estimate that as of yesterday, 3,067 people had died, or were missing and presumed dead, as a result of the attacks on Sept. 11, not including 19 hijackers.    AT THE WORLD TRADE CENTER  2,843 dead or missing, with 147 dead on two hijacked planes  199 missing  711 death certificates issued by medical examiner's office  1,933 death certificates issued at request of families in cases in which remains have not been identified
news.title: Dead and Missing

news.abstract: Pakistani and American officials say Ahmed Omar Sheikh, Islamic fundamentalist, is chief suspect in abduction of American journalist Daniel Pearl; cite 45-page account of kidnapping plan that Sheikh wrote 7 years ago after being jailed for kidnapping of three Britons and an American; that plan bears striking resemblances to Pearl's kidnapping; Rhys Partridge, one of Britons held captive by Sheikh, says he displayed mixture of intelligence, irrationality and intensity that led him, Partridge, to become convinced that Sheikh was psychopath (M)
news.title: Confession in 1994 Case Evokes Pearl Abduction

news.abstract: Mountains of discarded refrigerators in Britain are visible side effect of new European law that requires discarded appliances to be taken to special plants where environmentally harmful, ozone-depleting chlorofluorocarbons are extracted from insulation foam; Britain neglected to build plants, and this oversight has brought charges of incompetence from Conservative opposition and round of finger-pointing between defensive Labor government and European Union; photo (M)
news.title: St. Merryn Journal; Europe Decrees. British Bristle. Iceboxes Heaved.

news.abstract: Economic and Social Research Institute reports one in three Irish children born in 2000 were born to unmarried parents, up from one in 20 in 1980 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ireland: Rise In Unwed Parents

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel tells Pres Bush that 'Israel is committed to peace' and that he expects to see Palestinian state at end of Middle East peace process; two hold 45-minute meeting at White House, at which Bush says United States will keep up pressure on Yasir Arafat to crack down on violence; American and Israeli officials say Sharon's words about Palestinian state, made with American president at his side, are sign of his willingness to move toward negotiations with Palestinians, and reflects slight warming in his hard-line appraoch (M)
news.title: Sharon Tells Bush He Expects Creation of Palestinian State

news.abstract: International Committee of Red Cross says it differs with United States on how to decide whether to grant prisoner of war status to captives in Afghanistan; says person captured in international conflict is presumed to be prisoner of war unless competent tribunal decides otherwise (S)
news.title: Agency Differs With U.S. Over P.O.W.'s

news.abstract: korea: north korea cancels trip by 4 experts fro
news.title: North Korea Cancels Trip By 4 Experts From the U.S.

news.abstract: Group of Arab youths stab to death Israeli woman, 24, who was walking in park between Jewish and Arab areas of Jerusalem; police report catching four of masked Palestinians spotted running away; say one died at scene, without being shot or wounded; plan autopsy; thousands of supporters of Islamic group Hamas rally, Gaza Strip; watch performers act out rocket attack on Jewish settlement; Hamas leader Dr Abdel Aziz Rantisi speaks in first public appearance since he agreed with Palestinian Authority to submit to house arrest in Dec; deal, together with limited cease-fire set by Hamas, seems to have collapsed; Rantisi says suicide attacks will continue; Palestinian leadership again calls for cease-fire; map; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Woman Stabbed to Death in a Wave of Violence

news.abstract: Reaching back more than a decade to find common ground for their countries' future relationship, the leaders of Afghanistan and Pakistan agreed at a meeting that ''misunderstandings and misperceptions'' of the past should be left behind.    Article, Page A8.
news.title: Afghan-Pakistan Talks

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  Germany appeared close to blocking an unprecedented censure of its ballooning deficit that would deal an election-year humiliation to Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, officials said Friday.
news.title: Key Allies Oppose Deficit Warning : Berlin Looks Set To Escape Rebuke

news.abstract: Cambodians feel betrayed and abandoned after United Nations gives up effort to create international tribunal to try former leaders of Khmer Rouge; UN ended nearly five years of negotiations over makeup and procedures of tribunal, worn down by stubbornness of Cambodian government; this leaves government to proceed on its own with trials that both Cambodian and foreign analysts say will not meet international standards of fairness and impartiality and are likely to spare most major figures; Khmer Rouge, led by late Pol Pot, were responsible for deaths of more than million people when they held power from 1975 to 1979 (M)
news.title: Khmer Rouge Trials Won't Be Fair, Critics Say

news.abstract: Accidental explosion in arms depot in Lagos, Nigeria, comes after months of rising lawlessness and focuses anger on elected government that is widely seen as ineffective, uncaring and dangerously fragile; more than 1,000 people died, trampled on and drowned in canal as tens of thousands were fleeing city; government's response to Lagos disaster has hardened Nigerians' low opinion of their leaders; Pres Olusegun Obasanjo, in visit to military barracks near arms depot, expresses little sympathy for victims and refuses peoples' request to visit munitions dumps; when Vice Pres Atiku Abubakar visits barracks, his car is stoned and he is forced to flee; photo; map (M)
news.title: Blast Further Erodes Nigerians' Confidence

news.abstract: SYDNEY, Australia, Feb. 9 — Australia wants firmer penalties and longer jail sentences for convicted spies and traitors, but broad legislation proposed after Sept. 11 for that purpose could also imprison public sector whistle-blowers and journalists who expose scandals, not state secrets, civil libertarians and legal experts contend.
news.title: Security Bill for Australia Is Too Broad, Critics Say

news.abstract: Pres Vladimir V Putin's campaign to get Russians to exercise more fails to move average citizen, but politicians are scrambling to fulfill his will; mayor of Saransk takes his entire government on biathlon-style jaunt, and governor of St Petersburg orders his aides to prepare fitness program for all 6,000 government workers; this has provoked debate about national character, wisdom of imposing change from above and even president's commitment to democracy; critics wonder whether Putin and country are breaking Soviet mold or simply reverting to it; Izvestia columnist says 'habit to obey is in our blood'; photo (M)
news.title: When Putin Says 'Exercise!' Russia Treads a Beaten Path

news.abstract: Hundreds of young Afghan women take exam to attend Kabul University, idea that was anathema to former Taliban rulers; university faces many problems; Dr Aziz Ahmad Rahmand, professor of Afghan history, recalling Taliban repression, says he is thrilled that new day is dawning for education in his country; photos (M)
news.title: For Women in Kabul, This Test Is Welcome

news.abstract: British government struggles to quell fears about common childhood vaccine that increasing numbers of parents believe may be linked to autism, despite strong official assurances to contrary; government says so-called MMR vaccine, administered in two doses, is perfectly safe; vaccine has mostly wiped out three potentially deadly diseases, measles, mumps and rubella; Prime Min Tony Blair is under pressure from press and parents' groups to say whether his 20-month-old son, Leo, has had vaccine; Blair strongly implies that child has been or will be inoculated; growing numbers of parents decide not to allow their children to be inoculated, citing anecdotal evidence from parents of autistic children as well as several studies that suggest links between MMR and autism; meanwhile, measles has been diagnosed in 11 children in London, where only 75 percent of eligible toddlers have been immunized as opposed to 90.5 percent in United States (M)
news.title: Britain Tries To Quell Fear Over Vaccine For Children

news.abstract: SALT LAKE CITY:—  A year ago, at the World Ski Championships in Austria, an American named Daron Rahlves upstaged his hosts to win the opening men's race. On Sunday, in the first race of Ralves's home Olympics, the Austrians returned the favor.
news.title: From the Austrian Wunderteam, a suprise

news.abstract: Drug abuse in Saudi Arabia is serious enough problem that rulers are beginning to deal with it in very un-Saudi way: openly; government treats drug trafficking as criminal activity, but it has begun to regard drug, alcohol and nicotine dependence as treatable illnesses; drugs have increasingly become source of entertainment and escape in country that bans movie theaters, concert halls, discotheques and dating, and where 65 percent of population is under age of 25; country now has four drug treatment centers where patients are offered group therapy, physical therapy and biofeedback; photos (M)
news.title: Rehabilitation Joins Retribution in Saudi Drug War

news.abstract: Slobodan Milosevic, former president of Yugoslavia who goes on trial Feb 12, is first head of state ever to be tried for war crimes; is essentially accused of leading genocidal, criminal enterprise to 'cleanse' land he believed belonged to ethnic Serbs of other ethnic groups in three wars in Croatia, Kosovo and Bosnia; he proclaims his innocence, saying he wanted only to keep Yugoslavia whole; even those who loathe Milosevic worry that proceedings may look like victors' justice, and wonder whether prosecutor Carla Del Ponte can deliver evidence that draws direct line between Milosevic and bodies that have been uncovered in mass graves in Bosnia and elsewhere; trial is expected to last two years; beyond trial itself is question of what it means for people of what was once much larger Yugoslavia; photos; timeline; map (L)
news.title: Trial of Milosevic Will Peel Layers of Balkan Guilt, Too

news.abstract: Government of Iran shutters offices in Tehran of Afghan warlord Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, indicating he might be asked to leave; Hekmatyar's criticism of interim government in Kabul, plus his veiled threats to foreign forces stationed there, are at odds with Iran's own stated policy of helping to create stable government next door; his expulsion would also serve as yet another signal to Washington of Iran's good intentions; photo (M)
news.title: Tehran Shuts Offices of Afghan Hard-Liner as Calls to Expel Him Increase

news.abstract: Severe mid-January winter storm in mountains of central Mexico devastated two of country's largest monarch butterfly colonies; record 74 percent to 80 percent, or between 220 million and 270 million, butterflies died; researchers say loss is not expected to threaten species; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Storm in Mexico Devastates Monarch Butterfly Colonies

news.abstract: The Pentagon today sought to fend off continued questions about a missile attack by a C.I.A. drone in Afghanistan, and faced a number of questions about the agency's role in the war on terrorism.
news.title: Pentagon Faces More Questions on Afghan Raid, Plus C.I.A. Role

news.abstract: Article describes workings of International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (S)
news.title: Tribunal: How It Works

news.abstract: United Nations Secretary Gen Kofi Annan nominates James T Morris, an American, as executive director of World Food Program; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | World: United Nations: U.S. Nominee

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  Without warning, a phalanx of riot police and plainclothes officers descended on a school for about 200 young children in a lush oil palm estate in the southern Malaysian state of Johor, adjacent to Singapore. The raid, on Jan. 3, led to the closure of the Islamic school, or madrasa, which Malaysian authorities say was linked to a group of Muslim extremists.
news.title: Asians take a closer look at Islamic schools

news.abstract: Residents of 12-story apartment block on edge of industrial city of Ryazan, 130 miles southeast of Moscow, recall mysterious incident in Sept 1999, in which Russian intelligence agents planted what appeared to be huge bomb that, had it exploded, would have killed hundreds of people; official account is that it was extremely ill-considered civil defense drill, but incident occurred in wake of apartment bombings that did kill more than 300 people; Russian oligarch Boris A Berezovsky says he will show documentary film proving federal agents were involved in explosions, with Ryazan dummy bomb as evidence, but his claims are also doubted; photo (M)
news.title: Russian Tycoon's Bombshell: Can It Be?

news.abstract: Senior Afghan official Yunus Qanooni accuses elements in Pakistan's intelligence service of helping Osama bin Laden and Mullah Mohammad Omar evade capture (S)
news.title: Afghan Official Says Pakistanis Helped bin Laden Evade Capture

news.abstract: World Briefing
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Coldly brutal death of Wilson Pacheco, 26-year-old illegal immigrant from Ecuador who was beaten by nightclub bouncers and thrown into Barcelona harbor in January, has many Spaniards asking whether their society is as racially tolerant as they have believed (M)
news.title: Brutal Death Of Immigrant Shakes Faith Of Spaniards

news.abstract: UN says global ban on child soldiers has gone into effect; treaty bars recruitment of children under 18 by armies and militias, practice that affects estimated 300,000 children (S)
news.title: World Briefing | World: Ban On Young Soldiers

news.abstract: Secretary General Kofi Annan of United Nations meets privately with Pres Bush and members of Senate to prod them to give more for new global fund to combat AIDS epidemic; reportedly asks United States to set example for other countries by increasing international AIDS spending by 50 percent each year for next four years; Bush's budget proposal for 2003 asks for $900 million in international spending for AIDS prevention and treatment; pledge is not increase over this year and advocates and lawmakers say it is not enough (M)
news.title: Annan Asks U.S. for More Money for AIDS Fund

news.abstract: Excerpts from angry exchange between Slobodan Milosevic and Richard May, presiding judge at International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia (M)
news.title: From Serb, One More Protest About His Trial

news.abstract: Israeli foreign minister Shimon Peres draws up new peace plan calling for cease-fire with Palestinians, immediate recognition of initial Palestinian state on limited turf and yearlong negotiation over what final state would look like; he negotiated new plan with speaker of Palestinian parliament, known as Abu Ala; Peres faces solitary quest to sell plan to Prime Min Ariel Sharon, who resisted his negotiating in first place, to his party, which is under new, more hawkish leadership, and to Israelis, most of whom have given up on Yasir Arafat, Palestinian leader; Sharon has criticized peace plan, but he has not yet rejected it; photo (M)
news.title: Peres Offers New Peace Plan to Arafat and Sharon

news.abstract: Police in Pakistan report that arrest and interrogation of Ahmed Omar Sheikh, chief suspect in kidnapping of American journalist Daniel Pearl, has produced no solid evidence on Pearl's whereabouts or whether he is still alive; Gen Perez Musharraf, in visit to Washington, says he is 'reasonably sure' that Pearl is still alive, and that he regards abduction as retaliation by Muslim extremists to his efforts to crack down on terror; it is unclear whether police found Sheikh or whether he turned himself in as part of arrangement for freeing of relatives and colleagues who have been detained in case; photo (M)
news.title: Hunt for U.S. Reporter Leading to Dead Ends

news.abstract: Traudl Junge, private secretary to Hitler who was last surviving witness to Nazi leader's final moments in his Berlin bunker, dies at age 82 (S)
news.title: Traudl Junge, 82, Hitler's Private Secretary

news.abstract: Health Ministry of Brazil orders tobacco companies to display on cigarette packs photos showing effects of smoking; Brazil has been tightening regulations on tobacco industry since 1995, banning cigarette advertisements at sporting and cultural events and forbidding smoking in enclosed areas (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Brazil: An Effort To Make Smokers Think Twice

news.abstract: Many Italians hope British Prime Min Tony Blair's upcoming visit will help end Italy's current isolation within Europe, 'reinvent' Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi and reposition Italy in new alliance with Britain and Spain on economic and European policy (M)
news.title: Italians Hope Blair Visit Helps Berlusconi's European Image

news.abstract: For the first time, Palestinians destroyed an Israeli tank, planting a mine that punched through its belly and killed at least three soldiers.    The attack followed an Israeli incursion into three Gaza towns. That, in turn, was a reponse to the Palestinian firing of rockets into Israel.
news.title: Mine Wrecks Tank; 3 Israeli Soldiers Die

news.abstract: European Union gives tepid welcome to Pres Bush's new proposals, strictly voluntary, to address climate change (M)
news.title: Europeans Give Bush Plan on Climate Change a Tepid Reception

news.abstract: Palestinian militants destroy Israeli tank for first time, using mine underneath that kills at least three soldiers and lightly wounds fourth; tank was responding to coordinated attack on settlers' convoy in Gaza; Hamas and Fatah faction claim responsibility; Israel sees escalation to conventional warfare; Israeli raids in Gaza and West Bank and killings of several Palestinians also noted (S)
news.title: Arabs Deploy New Explosive Against Tank; 3 Israelis Die

news.abstract: Efren Reyes of Philippines may be world's best pool player and biggest money winner in that sport; he spent his best pool years--between 18 and 24--in lucrative obscurity before becoming famous; he is now 47; in space of eight days last Nov he won two of biggest billiards championships in world, in Warsaw and Tokyo; photo (M)
news.title: Oh, This Shark Has Missing Teeth, Dear

news.abstract: Having an offshore bank account may sound exotic and racy and not quite on the upand-up, but it can be a useful — and legitimate — financial planning tool for expatriates, providing tax savings and convenience.
news.title: Banking offshore : Even for a middle roller, it can make sense

news.abstract: Vatican announces that it will not make available documents on Pope Pius XII's controversial World War II pontificate for at least three more years; Jewish leaders and scholars express disappointment; some scholars theorize that Vatican is trying to get out in front of wave of criticism of Pius XII expected after release of new Costa Gavras film Amen, movie adaption of Rolf Hochhuth's play The Deputy, in which Pius is shown refusing to act on information about Holocaust; Pope John Paul II, only one with authority to open archives, has decided to start with release of selected documents on ties between Vatican and Germany from 1922 to 1939 (M)
news.title: Vatican to Hold Off Opening Pope Pius XII Wartime Archives

news.abstract: Fire and riots tear through Yari's Wood, Britain's showcase holding center for asylum seekers in what police say appears to be attempted mass escape by some of its 380 inmates; six people are reported injured; 20 asylum seekers, thought to be from Eastern Europe, escape, but 10 of them are recaptured; incident seen as severe challenge to Prime Min Tony Blair's government, which has sought to accelerate deportations and gathered those it plans to expel at centers like Yari's Wood; growing influx of migrants from developing countries and Eastern Europe has inspired political duel between Labor government and opposition Conservatives, with each side accusing other of being soft on economic fugitives seeking sanctuary as political refugees; photo (M)
news.title: Asylum Seekers Set Fires at Detention Center in Britain

news.abstract: Slobodan Milosevic says he will call present and past world leaders, including former Pres Bill Clinton, to stand during his war crimes trial at Hague; says he will personally cross-examine witnesses, including those who were raped, tortured or had their families killed, purportedly by Serbs; International War Crimes Tribunal must manage defendant who seems likley to represent himself with full-bore focus during trial that may last two years; Milosevic outlines his defense during defiant speech lasting over four hours; photo (M)
news.title: Milosevic Vows a Parade of Witnesses, Including Clinton

news.abstract: Arab experts say tentative proposal from Crown Prince Abdullah of Saudi Arabia for ending Middle East violencethrough longstanding land-for-peace formula would only serve to convince Israel that inflexibility toward ending its occupation works (M)
news.title: Arab Experts Fault Saudi's Idea Based on Land-for-Peace Trade

news.abstract: South Africa shakes off decades of apartheid-era isolation and stretches beyond its borders in powerful explosion of trade and investment that fellow Africans are watching with awe and admiration, but also unease at prospect of ceding so much control to outsiders; development underscores metamorphosis since apartheid ended in 1994 as former pariah state seems poised to dominate continent that once shunned its products and leaders; economic expansion is accompanied by growing political influence; many people praise country's championing of new partnerships among African nations they hope will reduce economic dependency on former colonial rulers, but there are also cries of outrage from politicians and businessmen who view rapid expansion as new form of colonialism; map; charts; photo (L)
news.title: Awe and Unease as South Africa Stretches Out

news.abstract: Focus on sharp increase in street crime in London, where officials say pedestrians are more likely to be mugged than in New York; visit by former New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, well known for tough line against crime, has focused government's attention on problem and sent embarrassed officials scrambling for ideas on how to solve it; street crimes increased 40.3 percent in London in past year; Home Sec David Blunkett gives police officials six months to achieve steep reduction in violent street crime and two years to make heavy inroads into problem of crime in general (M)
news.title: As Crime Rises, London Looks To New York For Lessons

news.abstract: Thousands unexpectedly line up outside National Library in Canberra, Australia, to view exhibition of rare books, letters, manuscripts, writers' possessions and other literary treasures borrowed from 42 collections in 24 countries; exhibit is part of celebration of library's centennial (M)
news.title: Library Treasures on International Loan Delight Australians

news.abstract: Suicide bomber detonates explosive package in outdoor food court of West Bank settlement of Karnei Shomron, killing himself and two Israelis and injuring 30 others; bombing follows already deadly day in West Bank and Gaza Strip; Palestinian militants are testing new tactics in stepped-up exchange of attack and retaliation and Israeli Army is searching for new ways to strike back; Israeli soldiers in Gaza kill three Palestinians in gun battle; leader of Hamas in West Bank city of Jenin dies in explosion that Palestinians say is Israeli assassination; Palestinian militants fire rockets into Israeli Army base in northern Gaza Strip, damaging building; Hamas militants fire rockets from Gaza into Israel, injuring no one but drawing new warnings of retaliation for what Israeli officials consider marked escalation in fighting; photo (M)
news.title: West Bank Suicide Bombing Kills 2 Israelis and Hurts 30

news.abstract: Ani Pachen, celebrated as warrior nun who led her Tibetan clan in armed rebellion against Chinese invaders until she was captured and spent 21 years as prisoner, dies at 68 or 69; photo (M)
news.title: Ani Pachen, Warrior Nun In Tibet Jail 21 Years, Dies

news.abstract: An explosion at a brake-pad factory near Mexico City killed four plant workers and injured seven others, the police reported Sunday.
news.title: 4 Die in Explosion at Brake Plant in Mexico

news.abstract: Bush administration, frustrated that Indonesia has not cracked down on terrorist threat, urges officials to hunt for Indonesian cleric, Riudan Isamuddin or Hambali, who is believed to be Al Qaeda point man in Southeast Asia; US believes he led plot to blow up US Embassy in Singapore; Indonesians also say they do not have enough evidence to arest second cleric, Abu Bakar Baasyir, alleged conduit of money (M)
news.title: Finding a Tepid Ally in the War on Terror, U.S. Presses Indonesia to Arrest 2 Clerics

news.abstract: Special Peruvian government commission, 15 months after fall of autocratic government of Pres Alberto K Fujimori, opens window into 20 years of state-sponsored repression and rebel terror that tore country apart; Truth and Reconciliation Commission is beginning probe of killings and disappearances of thousands of people, many from province of Ayacucho; is interviewing relatives of victims and disinterring remains; will collect testimony in private and will hold public hearings, first in Latin America, where victims of violence and public officials can give their accounts; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Where the Bodies Are Buried in Peru

news.abstract: Canada has overhauled security policy since Sept 11 terrorist attacks, tightening coordination with US on military, intelligence and law enforcement matters, and easing traditional concerns with civil liberties; government may now intercept e-mail and more than 750 Canadian troops are engaged in Afghanistan; photo; 72-hour detentions without warrant are permitted in terrorism cases and national security budgets are increased; shift aims to reassure US that Canada is not sanctuary for terrorists exploiting liberal refugee policies and porous border, but also reflects economic shock of long border-crossing delays; coordinated policies explained (M)
news.title: Canada Alters Security Policies to Ease Concerns of U.S.

news.abstract: Peru's Supreme Court upholds 20-year prison term for Lori Berenson, American convicted in June 2001 of collaborating with Tupac Amaru Marxist rebel group in its war against Peruvian government; she was arrested in 1995 and sentenced to life in prison by military junta, but sentence was overturned; was retried by new three-judge panel; can seek pardon from Pres Alejandro Toledo (S)
news.title: Berenson Loses Peruvian Appeal Of Her 20-Year Prison Sentence

news.abstract: Prosecutors at Slobodan Milosevic's war crimes trial in the Hague move swiftly to show that ousted Yugoslav leader knew or should have known of actions of his underlings, did nothing and therefore bears responsibility for any atrocities they committed; testimony of first witness former Kosovo Communist leader Mahmat Bakalli described; Bakalli says he warned Milosevic early in conflict about police abuses (M)
news.title: A Witness Says Milosevic Knew Early About Abuses in Kosovo

news.abstract: US forces apparently open new phase in war in Afghanistan with bombing raids Afghan commanders around Kabul say were aimed at clashing militia forces rather than at Taliban or Al Qaeda; US Central Command reports warplanes dropped precision-guided bombs when 'enemy troops' attacked forces loyal to eight-week-old Kabul government near southeastern city of Khost; bombing raids place US for first time in position of using American air power in defense of government of Hamid Karzai, pro-American leader of new administration; US policy since fall of Taliban has been to offer strong political and economic support to Karzai government, which recently announced it would request American air strikes if needed to end clashes between armed factions that control much of Afghanistan outside Kabul; map (M)
news.title: In a Shift, U.S. Uses Airstrikes To Help Kabul

news.abstract: Families of 26-year-old Australian man and a pair of young British citizens captured with fighters for Al Qaeda and Taliban in Afghanistan and flown to American military base in Cuba will file suit in federal court, Washington, DC, demanding their release; lawyers say clients David Hicks, Asif Iqbal and Shafiq Rasul are not terrorists and that their detention is fundamental violation of due process guarantees of Constitution; photo (M)
news.title: Suit to Be Filed on Behalf Of Three Detainees in Cuba

news.abstract: Pres Bush strongly reaffirms role of American military in Asia during speech to Japanese Parliament; declares next 100 years will be 'Pacific Century;' says US will stop aggression against South Korea, show American power and purpose in support of Philippines, maintain its commitments to Taiwan and press forward with missile defense system; powerfully endorses economic reforms of Prime Min Junichiro Koizumi; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Affirms U.S. Role in Asia in New 'Pacific Century'

news.abstract: Efforts by Swedish newspaper group, Metro International, to distribute free newspapers in France is met by violence from members of printing trades chapters of General Workers Confederation, union alliance allied with Communist Party; vendors have been assaulted, printing plants vandalized, trucks attacked and stacks of newspapers dumped into gutters; union officials want government to halt all distribution of free papers until it can study effects on economy (M)
news.title: In Paris, Read All About It if You Can

news.abstract: A blazing train jammed with holiday travelers sped through Egypt today, killing more than 370 passengers.
news.title: Hundreds Killed in Train Fire in Egypt

news.abstract: George Bogdanich, American filmmaker, protests unauthorized use of part of his documentary, Yugoslavia: The Avoidable War, by former Serbian leader Slobodan Milosevic at his war crimes trial in the Hague; film examines responsibility for breakup of Yugoslavia, and is particularly critical of Western support for armed separatists in Slovenia and Croatia (S)
news.title: Use of Film By Milosevic Draws Protest

news.abstract: In a plan approved by President Bush, a temporary wartime effort to shape information and coordinate messages will be expanded into a permanent office of global diplomacy, intended to spread a positive image of the United States.       Article, Page A11.
news.title: Office Promoting U.S.

news.abstract: Palestinian gunmen stage audacious attack at West Bank outpost killing six Israeli soldiers and escaping, stunning army already reeling from deaths of seven soldiers since February 14; attack is most lethal against Israeli soldiers in West Bank and Gaza in more than 16 months of fighting; follows dizzying 24 hours of shooting, shelling, bombing and rocket attacks that have claimed lives of at least 16 people; attack on checkpoint at Ein Ariq west of Ramallah described; Israeli forces stage reprisal; attack Yasir Arafat's official compound in Gaza City, killing at least four members of his elite guard; photos (M)
news.title: Mideast Death Toll Rapidly Rises As Violent Recriminations Spiral

news.abstract: Following is the statement by Peter R. Kann, publisher of The Wall Street Journal, and Paul E. Steiger, managing editor of The Wall Street Journal on the death of reporter Daniel Pearl:.
news.title: Text of Statement From The Wall Street Journal

news.abstract: Pres Bush is told by American intelligence agencies that China has continued to supply missile technology to Iran and Pakistan, two countries that are also North Korea's primary missile customers; Bush has repeatedly called North Korea 'evil,' citing its missile sales, but aides say Bush's tone about China's continued sales of missile parts and technology will be more muted; more than year after taking office, Bush administration remains deeply divided about how to deal with China--as economic and counterterrorism partner or as strategic competitor (M)
news.title: China Is Treated More Gently Than North Korea for Same Sin

news.abstract: People killed last month in a raid in Afghanistan were not Taliban or Al Qaeda members, the defense secretary said today.
news.title: Rumsfeld Defends Raid in Which 12 Were Killed

news.abstract: World Briefing
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Slobodan Milosevic, acting as his own lawyer at his war crimes trial, cross-examines Agim Zeqiri, who says Serb troops massacred his wife and five children in Kosovo in 1999; Zeqiri testifies with his back turned to Milosevic; denies under questioning that Kosovo Liberation Army, armed Albanian guerrilla group, had been in his small village on last day he saw his family; insists that only Yugoslav forces were there, burning down houses and shooting civilians; Milosevic does not ask questions disputing that civilians were killed; rather, he implies that attack was justified by presence of Kosovo guerrillas, which Zeqiri denies over and over again (M)
news.title: Milosevic Cannily Cross-Examines Kosovo Massacre Survivor

news.abstract: President Bush's decision this month to reverse himself and apply the Geneva Conventions to the Afghan war came after the Pentagon and State Department lined up against the administration's top lawyers, senior administration officials now say.    Senior officials also disclosed for the first time that NATO allies were so concerned with Mr. Bush's initial decision to reject the conventions that Britain and France warned they might not turn over Taliban and Al Qaeda fighters captured by their troops in Afghanistan unless Mr. Bush pledged to honor the treaties.
news.title: Behind-the-Scenes Clash Led Bush to Reverse Himself on Applying Geneva Conventions

news.abstract: North Korea today rejected President Bush's plea for dialogue during his visit last week.
news.title: North Korea Rejects Bush's Plea for Dialogue

news.abstract: Colombian Air Force planes bombed rebel camps and clandestine airstrips today as thousands of troops prepared to retake a huge rebel-held zone in an offensive that may well  mark the end of a tortuous three-year peace effort.    The operation began just hours after President Andrés Pastrana, in an emotional nationwide address on Wednesday night, angrily broke off talks while accusing the rebels of hijacking a domestic airliner in order to kidnap a senior senator who was on board. The president said the Marxist guerrilla group, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, was guilty of ''extreme wickedness and cruelty,'' demonstrating that his legendary patience with the rebels had been spent.
news.title: Colombia Attacks Rebel Zone as Leader's Patience Snaps

news.abstract: Nepal's Parliament votes to extend state of emergency imposed in November to battle Maoist rebellion that has spread across nation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Nepal: State Of Emergency Extended

news.abstract: Court in Karlsruhe, Germany, rejects appeal by former SS officer Anton Malloth, who is serving life sentence for role in atrocities at Theresienstadt concentration camp during World War II (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Nazi Loses Court Appeal

news.abstract: Bodies of three American servicemen killed in crash of Army Special Operations helicopter off Philippine coast arrive in Okinawa, Japan, as rescue crews search for other seven (S)
news.title: Briefly Noted; CRASH VICTIMS

news.abstract: South Korean intelligence service reports 20 more defectors from North Korea, bringing total this year to 74; total of 583 Koreans defected last year (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: More Defectors From North

news.abstract: World Briefing
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Prime Min Ranil Wickremesinghe of Sri Lanka signs formal cease-fire agreement with Tamil leader Velupillai Prabhakaran that is expected to lead to first peace talks between warring parties in seven years; truce brings promise of respite from 18-year-old ethnic conflict that has claimed more than 60,000 lives; Norway, which brokered deal, will lead international mission to monitor cease-fire on ground; Prime Min Jan Petersen of Norway hails accord as bold step toward peace, but also seeks to discourage unrealistic hopes of quick resolution to one of world's most intractable civil wars (M)
news.title: Truce Accord In Sri Lanka Could Herald Peace Talks

news.abstract: Chief suspect in Daniel Pearl case, Ahmed Omar Sheikh, tells investigators that Pearl was killed in late Jan as part of plot that was to have included attack on United States Consulate in Karachi; Sheikh's claims are among clues being weighed by American and Pakistani authorities still pursuing others thought to be involved in Pearl's killing; his gruesome beheading was recorded on videotape made available to American investigators in Karachi by Pakistani journalist who covers Islamic militants; American officials praise Pakistan for its aggressive pursuit of Pearl's killers, and Pres Pervez Musharraf vows that killing would not deter him and his government from acting against terrorists; Pearl was reporter for Wall Street Journal; photo (M)
news.title: Suspect Says Reporter Was Slain In January as Part of Wider Plot

news.abstract: Sgt Michael Oxman, Israeli soldier killed with five comrades when Palestinian gunmen attacked West Bank outpost, is buried with full honors in non-Jewish part of military cemetery; Ukrainian immigrant considered himself Jew, like his father, but does not qualify as such under Jewish law because his mother is not Jewish (M)
news.title: Soldier's Burial As a Non-Jew Adds to the List Of Israel's Pain

news.abstract: Nigerians are growing disenchanted with democracy as government's positive steps are being eclipsed by unmet promises, uncontrolled violence and string of disasters; spasms of violence are expected to grow more frequent as politicians position themselves for 2003 presidential vote; over 10,000 people are believed to have been killed in ethnic and religious clashes since military rule ended in 1999; photos (M)
news.title: Nigeria Grows Disenchanted With Democracy

news.abstract: sydney de haan, 83, creator o
news.title: Sydney De Haan, 83, Creator Of the Budget Package Tour

news.abstract: Analysis of Pres Bush's Asian trip as damage control mission aimed at reassuring leaders of Japan, South Korea and China shaken by his 'axis of evil' speech that he is more interested in peace than war with Iraq, Iran and North Korea; national security adviser Condoleezza Rice hold Bush's strategy is to define problem bluntly and then follow up with diplomacy and restraint; he spent most of his time shoring up Asian alliances he needs in next phase of anti-terrorism drive (M)
news.title: Damage Control

news.abstract: Yemeni Pres Ali Abdullah Saleh, although eager to prove his antiterrorist credentials to United States, is unable to produce two terrorism suspects US seeks without cooperation of tribal sheiks over whom his weak central government has little power; most of these warlords say they are on president's side and will hand over any terrorism suspects, but deny having seen them; Sheik Muhammad al Shayef comments, interview; photo (M)
news.title: Warlord Web Thwarts Terror Fight in Yemen

news.abstract: Western regional group of countries on United Nations Human Rights Commission seeks way to avoid repeat of embarrassing surprise 10 months ago, when United States lost its seat on panel; proposed formula would allot each Western state fixed number of years on commission over next 20 years; question now is how many years should be allotted to each country; everyone agrees US should have most, but that is where consensus ends; Amb Thorsteinn Ingolfsson of Iceland has unenviable task of rotating 20 seats among 29 nations for 20 years, based on size, merit and history of countries (M)
news.title: At U.N., Debating Who Gets the Right to Debate Human Rights

news.abstract: A report that the Saudi ruler is prepared to normalize relations with Israel if it makes peace with the Palestinians has brought a glimmer of hope to the land.
news.title: Saudi Proposals Bring a Bit of Hope to a Despairing Israel

news.abstract: Officials have begun talks on arrangements that could lead to the extradition of Ahmed Omar Sheikh, the chief suspect in the murder of Daniel Pearl.
news.title: U.S., in Pakistan Talks, Seeking Transfer of Suspect in Pearl Case

news.abstract: Amjed Hussain Farooqi, top fugitive being sought in Daniel Pearl case, is identified and described by Pakistani officials as man closely linked to web of Muslim militants in Afghanistan and Kashmir, reflecting view of Pakistani authorities that Pearl's killing was much more than isolated act; Farooqi is said to be former bodyguard for founder of banned group Army of Muhammad; Farooqi is suspected of picking up Pearl in Karachi and taking him to his death (M)
news.title: Suspect Linked to Regional Militants

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld says Pentagon may eliminate new office intended to influence public opinion and policy makers overseas; proposals from Office of Strategic Influence have caused uproar in Congress and elsewhere in government; Rumsfeld reiterates earlier assurance that military would not be permitted to tell lies to promote American policies or views, but says disclosures about new office's potential activities may have doomed its credibility (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Says He May Drop New Office Of Influence

news.abstract: Corn exports from United States to Mexico have risen sharply in last decade because of North American Free Trade Agreement, and this development may doom growing of corn as way of life for family farmers in Manzanillo, Mex; in US, corn growers receive billions of dollars yearly in subsidies from Congress, much of it going to huge agribusiness operations; that policy fuels huge surpluses and pushes corn prices down; in Mexico, Nafta did away with many traditional subsidies and generous price supports; some contend it is doing away with small farmers; about 90 percent of Mexico's corn farmers work fields of five acres or less; their survival instincts are driving them farther and farther up Mexico's mountainsides as they strive to grow enough to get by; Mexican legislators who want Mexico to protect its corn have no luck swaying Pres Vicente Fox; photo; graph (M)
news.title: Manzanillo Journal; In Corn's Cradle, U.S. Imports Bury Family Farms

news.abstract: Over last two weeks 160 American Special Forces soldiers have arrived in Basilan, small island in Philippines, as part of 'military training exercise' to help Philippine Army track down and defeat Abu Sayyaf, terrorist organization that specializes in kidnapping; group is currently holding American missionaries Martin and Gracia Burnham and Filipino nurse Ediborah Yap; photo (M)
news.title: Special Forces' Sweltering Paradise

news.abstract: EUROPE.
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Morgan Tsvangirai, who is running against Pres Robert Mugabe of Zimbabwe in upcoming election, is charged with treason in what authorities describe as plot to assassinate Mugabe; Tsvangirai is questioned and released by police; he denies accusations and his election coordinator claims charge constitutes government effort to sully his reputation before election, which is scheduled for Mar 9 and 10; incident highlights rising tensions as country braces for its most hotly contested presidential election; Mugabe, 78, has run Zimbabwe since white rule ended in 1980; opposition backers say his supporters use political disinformation and violence against them; groups of election observers from two southern African groups are stoned by rowdy supporters of Mugabe; photo (M)
news.title: Zimbabwe Candidate Charged With Treason

news.abstract: American-brokered security talks resumed between Israelis and Palestinians in Tel Aviv today against a backdrop of swelling hopes raised by a Saudi initiative.
news.title: Buoyed by Saudi Peace Proposal, Israelis and Arabs Resume Talks

news.abstract: Pres Bush, thrusting himself into Mideast peace effort, calls Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah and praises his proposal for Israel to withdraw completely from West Bank and Gaza in return for full normalization of relations with all Arab countries; others in administration are less enthusiastic, undertain how Prime Min Ariel Sharon will view long-term plan at time of intensifying violence; Javier Solana of European Union reports Sharon says idea is interesting; also discusses concept with Yasir Arafat, who sends team to Tel Aviv to discuss curbing violence; some Israeli ministers are heartened by what seems to be first concrete peace signal in 17 months of unmitigated violence (M)
news.title: BUSH WELCOMES SAUDI'S PROPOSAL ON MIDEAST PEACE

news.abstract: Hungarian Prime Min Viktor Orban calls for repeal of decrees issued by Edvard Benes, Czechoslovakia's postwar president, allowing for expulsion of millions of Germans and Hungarians from Czechoslovakia; Orban says repeal should be condition of European Union membership for Czech Republic and Slovakia, but demand infuriates two countries and puts pressure on partnership with Hungary and Poland (M)
news.title: Czech Decrees, Dating to 40's, Divide Europe

news.abstract: Prosecutors at war crimes trial at The Hague move to clamp down on Slobodan Milosevic's lengthy cross-examinations, saying grillings could deter future witnesses from testifying against him (S)
news.title: Milosevic Grills Witnesses Too Harshly, His Prosecutors Complain

news.abstract: US considers sending 'sizable' number of Special Operations forces to former Soviet republic of Georgia to help train its military in counterterrorism tactics; aim is to prepare Georgian troops to combat foreign fighters who are operating in mountainous region and may have links to Osama bin Laden's network; new front in war against terrorism would build on operations in Afghanistan and involve 100-200 Special Operations forces who would not take part in direct combat but would defend themselves against attack (M)
news.title: U.S. MAY SEND G.I.'S TO EX-SOVIET AREA

news.abstract: Zimbabwe Pres Robert Mugabe presides at campaign rally of supporters and assails opponent Morgan Tsvangirai as front man for whites; photo (M)
news.title: In Zimbabwe, Mugabe Runs Against an Old Rival: Colonialism

news.abstract: Thailand, one of freest and most open societies in Asia, issues rare expulsion order against two foreign correspondents, arousing cries of dismay and anger from local and foreign press; action is taken against Far Eastern Economic Review correspondents Shawn Crispin and Rodney Tasker; magazine denies any wrongdoing and appeals order; expulsion order cites brief article in magazine referring to frictions between Prime Min Thaksin Shinawatra and royal palace (M)
news.title: Thai Government Orders Expulsion of 2 Foreign Correspondents

news.abstract: United Nations officials investigate claims of sexual abuse of young girls in refugee camps in West Africa; Secretary Gen Kofi Annan vows action will be taken against violators (S)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: Annan Vows Action On Sex Abuses

news.abstract: Calling it "very strong," Yasir Arafat said today that a Saudi Arabian peace proposal's chances for success depended on immediate American support.
news.title: Arafat Says Saudi Plan Needs U.S. Backing

news.abstract: BRUSSELS:—  When he presides over the first session of the "Convention on the Future of Europe" on Thursday, Valery Giscard d'Estaing will return to the center of the European political stage after 20 years in the wings.
news.title: But ex-president's past looms large : Giscard's new role at heart of Europe

news.abstract: Dozens of Afghan and Arab fighters are thought to be hiding in Pankisi Gorge, 40-mile-long slash of rock and forest in Caucasus Mountains of Georgia, possibly plotting terrorist strikes in Russia, Europe and United States; Russian and American officials want to bring fight against global terrorism to that area, but Pres Eduard Shevardnadze's government is reluctant to act while estimated 8,000 Chechen refugees and 1,500 Chechen rebels are also taking shelter there; fear is that any military operation in gorge would endanger civilians and risk bringing Russia's war in Chechnya to Georgia; area has long served as no man's land of crime, drug trafficking and hostage taking on border between Georgia and Russia; Russia has long pressed Georgia to crush Chechen rebels on its territory, or at least drive them back into Chechnya; Georgia wants United States to provide military hardware before Georgian troops are sent against hardened fighters of gorge; US and Russia are reluctant to provide such heavy weapons, concerned that they would not be used in gorge but to inflame conflicts in breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia; photos; maps (L)
news.title: In Caucasus Gorge, a Haven for Muslim Militants

news.abstract: Congo's two main rebel groups agree to let political parties select delegates to talks on country's political future (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Congo: Agreement Could Let Talks Resume

news.abstract: South Korea's Park Geun Hye considers running in next presidential election; would be first woman to do so; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Gearing Up For Presidential Bid?

news.abstract: Argentina's 23 provincial governors sign accord with President Eduardo Duhalde requiring them to reduce budget deficits; accord paves way for austerity budget, International Monetary Fund condition for new aid (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Argentina: Clearing An I.M.F. Hurdle

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder cancels visit to Prague, avoiding involvement in dispute between Czechs and Hungarians stemming from end of World War II over citizenship and land rights (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: More Fallout From 1945

news.abstract: Israeli troops for first time battle their way into two refugee camps in Jenin on West Bank, killing at least 11 Palestinians and losing one soldier in some of fiercest fighting of 17-month conflict; hospital officials say dozens of Palestinians are wounded; Israeli government says it wants to deny Palestinian militants havens to manufacture explosives and plan attacks; militants promise reprisals, particularly for attack on Balata Refugee Camp, stronghold of Yasir Arafat's Fatah faction; gunmen then open fire on Gilo, Jewish neighborhood of Jerusalem occupied in 1967 war; new violence comes as Palestinian officials and Arab leaders praise initiative floated by Saudi Arabia to resolve deepening impasse; photos (M)
news.title: Israeli Troops Raid Arab Camps, Killing 11 in West Bank Fighting

news.abstract: NAPLES—  Noodles and pizza have spread from Naples throughout the world. Could Neapolitan neo-grunge also be exported?
news.title: Reinventing grunge, Naples-style

news.abstract: Pres Bush has approved plans to send as many as 100 troops, mostly Special Forces, to train Yemeni military to fight terrorists, specifically Al Qaeda fighters hiding in country; increasingly broad campaign stirs Democratic complaints that administration demands virually unlimited funds without answering to Congress; latest operations aim to crush isolated but potent Islamic insurgents; Special Forces would be limited to training and equipping nations requesting help, but not calling in air strikes; Americans will be discouraged from even firing weapons except in self-defense; Yemen is key center of support for Osama bin Laden, home to well-armed tribal forces, at least 20 senior Qaeda officials and scores of fighters trained in Afghanistan (M)
news.title: U.S. Broadens Terror Fight, Readying Troops for Yemen

news.abstract: UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan and international law experts strongly defend UN war crimes tribunals for Balkans and Rwanda, in response to US envoy Pierre-Richard Prosper's testimony to Congress casting doubt on tribunals' integrity and professionalism; South Africa Justice Richard Goldstone, first chief prosecutor, criticizes Bush administration position that tribunals should wind up work by 2007-2008; experts concede management problems at Rwanda tribunal, but not at Balkan proceedings in The Hague (M)
news.title: Experts Dispute Bush Aide's Criticism of War Crimes Panels

news.abstract: Cuban police arrest 21 asylum seekers holed up inside Mexican Embassy after crashing bus through gates; Mexican officials request raid after concluding young men are economic, not political, refugees (S)
news.title: Cuba Arrests Asylum Seekers in Mexican Embassy

news.abstract: LONDON—  London has come to a pretty pass when the parties upstage the catwalk shows. So frantic was the social whirl surrounding London Fashion Week that many a fashion editor bypassed the catwalk shows altogether.
news.title: For glamorous dressing, the city's nightclubs steal the show : In London, forget the catwalks

news.abstract: Pentagon announces death of American soldier in Afghanistan, bringing number of American service members killed by hostile fire while engaged in war on terrorism to two (S)
news.title: Previous U.S. Deaths

news.abstract: Israeli army says its soldiers have found six makeshift rockets and stores of bomb-making chemicals at refugee camps in Balata and Jenin on West Bank; soldiers continue to occupy many cinder-black homes on third day of two raids that Israel says has left 30 Palestinians dead; Palestinians in both camps accuse soldiers of firing at random, killing several civilians and terrifying residents; most Palestinian gunmen have deserted both camps but gunfire still rings out periodically (M)
news.title: Israelis Say Arms Are Found In Search of 2 Refugee Camps

news.abstract: Officials in suburb of Beijing cut off electricity for small Christian-run home for aged and threaten to shut off water supply unless home is disbanded; they are alarmed by unauthorized church services there; religious activities outside China's official church are illegal, but so called house church services such as ones in home for aged are widespread, sometimes tolerated and sometimes not (M)
news.title: China Punishes a Christian Home for the Aged

news.abstract: Three former Rwandan news media executives stand accused of genocide and incitement to genocide through their use of radio broadcasts and newspapers; their trial before United Nations war crimes tribunal will examine scope of role played by news media in massacre of more than 800,000 people in Rwanda in 1994; this is first time group of journalists stand accused before international tribunal on such grave charges since 1946, when Julius Streicher, Nazi publisher of anti-Semitic weekly Der Sturmer, appeared before Nuremberg judges; prosecutors in Rwanda case are drawing stark parallels between Der Sturmer's vitriolic campaigns against Jews before World War II and actions of some Rwandan media before and during 1994 slaughter of Tutsi; legal specialists believe outcome of current trial may set crucial precedent for future international cases; photos (M)
news.title: Trial Centers on Role of Press During Rwanda Massacre

news.abstract: Federal authorities want to create DNA databank of terrorism suspects by analyzing blood samples from thousands of captured fighters of Al Qaeda and Taliban being held in Afghanistan and at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba; FBI authorities say they are frustrated by their inability to identify vast majority of detainees, and worried that many of them will be released before government is certain who they are; say information from proposed DNA database could also play role in some current investigations, including case of Richard Reid, accused of trying to blow up trans-Atlantic flight with explosives hidden in his shoes; say DNA might help them trace source of hairs found in Reid's shoes and possibly identify accomplice; DNA database proposal is being reviewed by Justice Dept; Congressional approval would be required; civil liberties groups are likely to fight such attempts to expand use of DNA profiling (M)
news.title: U.S. Seeks DNA Of All Captives In Afghan War

news.abstract: Mistaken belief that dozens of children died from doses of vitamin A halts public health drive in Assam, India, that international experts say is essential to save tens of thousands of children from dying of variety of diseases; decision by national government to halt campaign underscores politics and suspicion that can surround even best-intended efforts at foreign assistance in India; even though public health officials say none of deaths was caused by vitamin A, government has turned matter over to committee of experts who will recommend strategy in coming weeks, which will include decision on whether campaign should be restarted or ended for good; photos; map (M)
news.title: Fear Stalls Health Push In India

news.abstract: News analysis of outlook for US diplomacy in Middle East as Israeli-Palestinian violence intensifies; unrelenting violence seems all but certain to bolster Bush administration's position that meaningful engagement will have to wait; has left Bush administration stymied and efforts at meaningful diplomacy stalled (M)
news.title: Frozen by Violence: An American Mission Waits for Its Opening

news.abstract: Suicide bombing in Orthodox section of East Jerusalem that left nine Israelis dead is seen by many yeshiva students as painful reprimand from God and as part of chain of violence dating back to biblical times (M)
news.title: For Israelis, New Tragedy Is a Challenge Sent by God

news.abstract: The Formula One auto-racing circuit is a high-speed crossroads of death and danger, big bucks and big stakes, where leaders of nations and big business hobnob with, promote and cheer for young men whose only skill is driving very fast machines that look more like rockets than cars.
news.title: High speed, high society : Formula One swerves through a downturn

news.abstract: Special relationship forged between US and Philippines during World War II, which soured in early 1990's, is revived in aftermath of September 11 terrorist attacks; most visible sign of revival is arrival of American troops to work with Filipino soldiers to defeat Abu Sayyaf terrorists holding two Americans hostage; two nations are discussing treaty that would give US right to store weapons, permanent overflight rights for combat aircraft and right to set up camps in archipelago for short periods; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. and Philippine Governments Revive Old Relationship

news.abstract: Haitian Pres Jean-Bertrand Aristide selects Senator Yvon Neptune as prime minister to replace Jean-Marie Cherestal, who resigned amid complaints of corruption; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Haiti: New Prime Minister

news.abstract: Far Eastern Economic Review apologizes for recent article about Thailand's government and monarchy; police weigh lifting expulsion orders for two of magazine's reporters (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Thailand: Under Pressure, Magazine Apologizes

news.abstract: Seven American soldiers are killed in some of fiercest fighting of five-month war in Afghanistan as US ground forces take lead in large-scale combat operation for first time; die in incidents involving two helicopters, one hit by rocket-propelled grenade, while attempting to drop off reconaissance teams during heavy fighting in nearly inaccessible mountains near Gardez in east; deaths, along with that of Special Forces soldier day earlier, bring total casualties to eight killed and approximately 40 wounded since start of operation on March 2 to wipe out pocket of hard-core Al Qaeda fighters; operation involving approximately 2000 allied troops described; commander Gen Tommy R Franks comments; Pres Bush voices sadness over loss of American servicemen, but says he is determined to fulfill mission troops were sent to perform and to make sure US is free from further attack; photos; map; diagram (M)
news.title: 7 AMERICANS DIE DURING RAID ON AFGHANISTAN MOUNTAINS

news.abstract: American and Canadian law enforcement officials say illegal production in US of popular stimulants like methamphetamine reflects lax regulations in Canada for chemical ingredients; say Canada has become as result leading supply route for raw ingredients to US where substances are more tightly controlled; US Customs Service has seized in last 11 months more than 110 million tablets of decongestants that contain primary ingredients for making methamphetamine or 'speed' (M)
news.title: U.S. Moves to Close Canadian Drug Route for Illegal Stimulant

news.abstract: Japanese Foreign Ministry admits Parliament member Muneo Suzuki exerted improper influence over ministry's policies and bidding for government contracts (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: More Trouble At Foreign Ministry

news.abstract: Indian probers seek to learn what spurred Muslim mob to set fire to train loaded with Hindu activists, Godhra, burning alive 58 people, mostly women and children, and sparking reprisal attacks on Muslims across Gujarat state; Godhra remains under tight curfew; city's Muslim mayor, two Muslim city council members and 38 Muslims who live along railway tracks have been arrested; police in Ahmedabad reportedly charge local Hindu politicians and World Hindu Council leaders encouraged reprisals; Godhra has history of Muslim-Hindu violence and open mutual contempt and mistrust; map; photo (M)
news.title: After Deadly Firestorm, India Officials Ask Why

news.abstract: WASHINGTON:—  American officials expressed caution and doubts Tuesday about reports that a large ring of Israelis spies had been broken up last year in the United States, where some of them allegedly had come in pursuit of Al Qaeda militants.
news.title: U.S. cool to report of Israeli spy ring

news.abstract: Egyptian Pres Hosni Mubarak urges United States to intervene to stop mounting bloodshed between Israelis and Palestinians, speech, Washington; Pres Bush gives no sign that US will step up its role; says he and Mubarak view situation 'with great alarm,' joint news conference; calls Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah's peace proposal positive development; lauds Mubarak's offer to broker meeting between Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon; photo (M)
news.title: Mubarak Urges U.S. Role in Stopping Mideast Bloodshed

news.abstract: Chinese Prime Min Zhu Rongji calls for renewed assault on official corruption and for bolstering farm incomes, televised State of Nation speech opening annual Parliament session; highlights threats to prosperity and social stability he says dog transition to market economy; hails 2001 achievements, including 7.3 percent economic growth rate (M)
news.title: Chinese Hear From Premier On Threats To Economy

news.abstract: Conflict in Zanzibar, Tanzania, spurred by dual roles as Islamic society and tourist spot has intensified as segment of its Muslim community pushes hardline religious view; anti-alcohol teachings in local mosques have spurred series of bombings at local bars, none regular tourist haunts, tarnishing island's image as tranquil resort; map; photos (M)
news.title: Zanzibar Journal; Tourists and Islam Mingle, Not Always Cozily

news.abstract: Belgian court sets May 15 for hearing on whether case can proceed against Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon for 1982 massacre of Palestinians in two Lebanese refugee camps (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Belgium: Date Set For Sharon Hearing

news.abstract: Commanders call in more American troops and helicopters to counter attempts by Taliban and Al Qaeda to bolster Islamic fighters struggling to hold on to their mountaintop redoubts; 300 more troops are called to battle, for total of 1,200 American combat soldiers; 21 more helicopters are also added; American and Afghan commanders say up to 500 new fighters have joined Taliban and Qaeda force of 200 men; there is growing sense that battle could be climactic moment of conflict that may decide whether Taliban and Al Qaeda meet their end as fighting force in Afghanistan; American commanders say US-led bombing attacks and ground assaults may have already killed as many as 400 hostile fighters of total of 800; photos; map; chart (L)
news.title: U.S. ADDS TROOPS AND HELICOPTERS IN AFGHAN BATTLE

news.abstract: Bush administration decides to terminate its unequivocal support for Prime Min Ariel Sharon's hard-line strategy and declares that his approach will likely fail; administration officials are alarmed by Sharon's recent comment that Palestinians must be 'hit hard' because they will only negotiate after they are beaten; officials decide to respond strongly to Sharon, lest he interpret Washington's silence as implicit permission to intensify conflict or declare all-out war; Secretary of State Colin Powell's comments to House subcommittee asking Israel to take 'hard look' at its policies are sharpest criticism to date of Sharon's tough policy; Sharon quickly responds that he, like Pres Bush, is simply fighting terrorism (M)
news.title: Bush Officials End Support Of Sharon's Tough Stance

news.abstract: Twenty-one Muslim boys and girls burned to death by raging Hindu mobs and unclaimed in city mortuary--perhaps because all relatives died also--are buried in Ahmedabad in Gujarat state; Muslim disillusionment is heightened by government decision on compensation to families; families of Hindu victims of train attack by Muslims will receive twice as much as families of Muslim victims of Hindu attacks in reprisal; government calls train attack terrorism, and later rioting Hindu-Muslim violence; Muslims are angry at police force that failed to protect them and at state chief minister who blamed Muslims for provoking mob violence directed at them; photo; map (M)
news.title: Ahmedabad Journal; In India, a Child's Life Is Cheap Indeed

news.abstract: Analysis: Defense Sec Donald H Rumseld seeks to differentiate between disastrous American raid in Mogadishu, Somalia, in 1993 that led to deaths of 18 American soldiers, and recent military events in Afghanistan, when Navy Seal fell out of helicopter and died, perhaps at hands of enemy, and six commandos were killed and dozen wounded before his body was retrieved; there are similarities, including significant underestimation of enemy's will to mobilize and fight; but contrasts are more striking; this time Pentagon has clear purpose: destruction of Al Qaeda and Taliban government; it also has broad support of American public; still, Pentagon's willingness to accept casualties is far from clear (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld's Burden: Stilling Echoes of the Grisly Raid in Somalia

news.abstract: Man enters restaurant in Jerusalem wearing heavy jacket on warm, sunny afternoon, attracting attention of owner, waiter and security guard; man is found to be wearing bomb with detonator switch in his hand; incident leaves restaurant workers and patrons jumpy but grateful; photo (M)
news.title: Coat, Backpack, Sweat: Close Call in Israeli Cafe

news.abstract: Morgan Tsvangirai, opposition presidential candidate in Zimbabwe, says he hopes to be alive to play role in government; has faced three assassination attempts since standing up to government five years ago as leader of country's largest trade union; one of Pres Robert Mugabe's aides said publicly that week that he would support military coup if Tsvangirai wins election; thousands of people have put their hopes in him; he is first politician to build formidable coalition of blacks and whites powerful enough to challenge Mugabe; photo (M)
news.title: Zimbabwe President's Rival Vows to Prevail at the Polls

news.abstract: Chinese and American paleontologists find fossils of feathered, flightless dinosaur, slightly bigger than pheasant, that they say should settle once and for all that feathers originated before birds or flight; discovery of 125-million-year-old dinosaur in China is reported in journal Nature; scientists suspect feathers evolved for some purpose other than flight, perhaps for warmth, and only later and with other physical changes were they used to help takeoffs (M)
news.title: Scientists Discover a Dinosaur Clad in Flightless Feathers

news.abstract: Japan weighs whether to salvage ship that sank in gun battle in East China Sea (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: A Warning From China

news.abstract: PARIS—  With skirts whirling, fur from Mohican boots flying and colors vibrating along with the 1980s dance music, John Galliano finally got Dior products out on the runway. His joyous show brought pep and energy to the opening day of the Paris autumn/winter 2002 shows Thursday and proved why Dior's latest figures are as hot as its designer's clothes.
news.title: The Collections / Paris : Dior's magpie magnificence

news.abstract: PARIS—  With a burst of color, one of the city's oldest shopping destinations, Old England, has been recently redone, turning it into one of Paris's most modern shopping venues.
news.title: Corner of England in Paris gets a colorful makeover

news.abstract: PARIS—  The powerful shows that have hit the runways — Bang! Bang! Bang! — in the first two days of the autumn/winter 2002 have a collective thread. Designers are going back to their roots.
news.title: The Collections / Paris : Forward-looking designers go back to their roots

news.abstract: Lawmakers in Macedonia pass amnesty for ethnic Albanian guerrillas, in move hailed by both sides as vital step to solidify tenuous peace; law does not cover possible crimes investigated by international tribunal in The Hague, which is said to be looking into incidents involving both Macedonians and Albanians (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Macedonia: Amnesty For Rebels Approved

news.abstract: Senior Pakistani officials say government will expel thousands of Arab, Afghan and other foreign students now studying at religious schools across country, out of concern that their presence might be step toward possible militant activities; plan would also bar new enrollment of foreign students altogether; plan stems from promise made by Gen Pervez Musharraf in Jan to deport foreign students at madrassas who lacked valid visas; in past, Pakistan's government allowed madrassas to operate virtually unregulated; madrassas served as principal base for Islamic scholars who became leaders of Taliban movement in Afghanistan and fighters against American-led forces there; government also intends to release at least 800 of 2,000 Pakistani militants arrested in Jan as part of crackdown against extremist Muslim groups, provided they vow to abstain from violence and outlawed groups (M)
news.title: Pakistan Prepares to Expel Foreign Religious Students

news.abstract: African diplomats converge on Harare to observe Zimbabwe's presidential election; Pres Robert Mugabe, fiery nationalist who nurtured and inspired generation of black leaders, is now old man with tarnished image, his popularity waning and his power seemingly slipping through his fingers; whether or not he wins re-election, emergence of formidable black opposition party in Zimbawe is already sending jitters all across southern Africa, where leaders are wrestling with similar strains: disaffected young people, voter apathy and mounting complaints about unemployment, poverty and empty stomachs; opposition party leaders in Zimbabwe say leaders of neighboring countries fear political challenges at home, and so are reluctant to condemn Zimbabwe's government attacks on opposition; photos (M)
news.title: Zimbabwe Vote Heralds a Shift in Southern Africa
