news.abstract: Mexican authorities announce arrest of Benjamin Arellano Felix, chief of nation's most powerful and violent drug gang; Asa Hutchinson, head of United States Drug Enforcement Administration, hails arrest as 'incredible victory'; Mexican authorities say that under interrogation, Arellano Felix confirmed death of his brother Ramon, cartel's notorious enforcer; say death of one brother and capture of another represent one of biggest breakthroughs for law enforcement in Mexico's long history of drug wars (M)
news.title: Drug Kingpin, Long Sought, Is Captured By Mexicans

news.abstract: International Conference on Eradication of Dracunculiasis, commonly known as Guinea worm disease, draws hundreds of scientists, politicians and others to Khartoum, Sudan; Guinea worm disese occurs in just 13 countries around world and could be eradicated altogether if it were not for Sudan, country with more cases than any other; health experts note that Sudan has 80 percent of world's reported Guinea worm cases, virtually all of them in war-ravaged south where clinics are rarity and aerial bombardments by government troops are commonplace; 18-year-long war in Sudan has made impossible inoculations, treatments and health education campaigns that are imperative in controlling any disease; photo; map showing cases of Guinea worm disease worldwide (M)
news.title: Sudan's War Bars Cure For Disease Eradicated In Other Parts of Africa

news.abstract: Palestinian terror attacks in Jerusalem and in Netanya kill at least 14 Israelis, underscoring enormous challenges facing America's renewed peacemaking efforts; in Jerusalem, suicide bomber walks into popular cafe and sets off bomb, killing 11 people and wounding 50 others; militant Islamic group Hamas claims responsibility and says bomber lived in refugee camp in Hebron; in Netanya, two men attack popular promenade, hurling grenade into hotel lobby and opening fire with automatic rifles until police officers shoot them dead; three people are killed, including baby and Israeli-Arab man, and 24 others are injured; Aksa Martyrs Brigades, which is associated with Yasir Arafat's Fatah organization, claims responsibility for attack and says attackers came from refugee camp in Nablus; Israeli helicopters fire missiles at Arafat's seaside office building in Gaza City, detroying it; photos; maps showing locations of Israeli and Palestinian deaths in last week (L)
news.title: 14 Israelis Killed in Two Terror Attacks

news.abstract: Switzerland votes to join United Nations, but narrow margin of victory is expected to hobble any more such overtures for near future; exceptionally high voter turnout underlines divisions between urban centers that favor membership and rural heartland areas that are opposed (S)
news.title: Slim Edge Mars Vote by Swiss To Join U.N.

news.abstract: Esther Afua Ocloo, who pioneered small loans for women, dies at age 83; photo (M)
news.title: Esther Ocloo, 83, Pioneer in Microloans to Help Women Become Entrepreneurs, Dies

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  Why spend money on nice underwear, when nobody sees it? That used to be the reasoning of Asian consumers who went in for utilitarian styles in basic colors. But today women are discarding their boring beige bras and panties and donning more feminine lace-embellished styles in pretty pastel colors.
news.title: Trendy and sophisticated styles replace boring beige bras and panties : Asia brightens up its lingerie, discreetly

news.abstract: American commanders, while not declaring victory, cautiously declare crux of battle against Al Qaeda ad Taliban fighters in much of Shah-i-Kot Valley in Afghanistan effectively is over; order about 400 soldiers back to base but say say fresh troops may be rotated into battle to eliminate remnants of enemy; Joint Chiefs of Staff Chmn Gen Richard B Myers says remaining Al Qaeda and Taliban fighters are widely dispersed; hints battle has opened way to eventual end of American combat operations in Afghanistan; jubilant returning soldiers from 10th Mountain Division in Fort Drum, NY, express confidence battle will mark decisive moment in successful war; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Saying Battle Is Reaching End, U.S. Sends Troops Back to Base

news.abstract: Shah-i-Kot, collection of mountain villages in eastern Afghanistan that is scene of fierce fighting between US-led forces and those of Al Qaeda and Taliban, is dealt double blow; residents were forced to leave by Taliban who favored it as place to make last stand; was home to mujahedeen base in 1980's during war against Russians, and is considered hallowed ground; is currently being destroyed by bombs dropped by US warplanes; photo (M)
news.title: Taliban and War Deliver a Double Blow to Villagers

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Fashion's flirtation with architecture has led to a new generation of over-the-top boutiques. But the design elite is still struggling to embrace the shop-til-you-drop movement.
news.title: Architects fear boutique craze is going too far

news.abstract: Sec of State Colin L Powell says there is no cause for international alarm over secret Pentagon policy review that identifies countries like Iran, Iraq and North Korea as potential targets for future American nuclear attacks; Powell's remarks are echoed by Joint Chiefs of Staff chairman Gen Richard B Myers and other top foreign policy and national security aides to help calm fears among European groups and Middle Eastern leaders that disclosure of administration's ambitious nuclear plans suggest that American nuclear attack is imminent as part of war on terrorism; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. Tries To Explain New Policy For A-Bomb

news.abstract: Police in Harare, Zimbabwe, arrest Welshman Ncube, an opposition leader, and detain four American diplomats observing presidential election, which ended after court denied opposition request to extend vote after third day of sometimes chaotic balloting; developments draw strong protest from US State Department, which calls it 'totally unacceptable;' photo (M)
news.title: Official Arrested as Zimbabwe Election Ends

news.abstract: LONDON—  I wanted to created something that was pure, yet totally luxurious," says the young British designer Russell Sage of the transparent twists of glass jewelry he created for his recent autumn 2002 London show. Known for using delicate fabrics such as antique French and Gainsborough silks, this season Sage is concerned with the more exclusive aspects of fashion. "Now it's time to concentrate on luxury and quality," he says.
news.title: In London, putting touch of whimsy into jewelry

news.abstract: India's Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee, facing anger over failure of governing party in Gujarat State to prevent killing of hundreds of Muslims by Hindu mobs, assures Parliament he will keep peace in another potential flash point: northern Indian city of Ayodyha; militant Hindus who belong to group affiliated with Vajpayee's Hindu nationalist Bhatariya Janata Party say they will hold ceremony in Ayodhya on March 15 as part of campaign to build temple on site of 16th-century mosque they helped tear down nine years ago; photo (M)
news.title: India Seeks to Head Off Any New Violence

news.abstract: American soldiers returning from combat against Al Qaeda and Taliban fighters in Shah-i-Kot mountains of Afghanistan give first-hand accounts of battle; say enemy appears vanquished, but is willing to fight to death; photo (M)
news.title: With Relief and Sarcasm, Soldiers Recall Whizzing Bullets Fired by 'Wimps'

news.abstract: New Afghan government risks sanctions from donor nations, especially US, since any aid may depend on destruction of poppy fields, which are sources of most of heroin found on streets of Europe and America; government, however, will also face opposition from farmers who depend on poppy cultivation for living; plight of poppy farmers in Sangin in Helmand Province, where opium markets thrived under Taliban but are now outlawed, and where fields may be eradicated discussed; maps; photos (M)
news.title: A Village at Source of Heroin Trade Fears the Eradication of Its Poppies

news.abstract: General Assembly has slashed operating budget of United Nations by $75 million over two years; thermostats are lowered to save heating costs, leaving many meeting rooms too cold to sit in without coat and gloves (M)
news.title: U.N. Shivers In a Season Of Cost Cuts That Pinch

news.abstract: UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan tells Israel to end 'illegal occupation' of Palestinian lands, as Israeli forces carry out fiercest assault since areas were captured in 1967 war; 31 Palestinians are killed as troops pursue armed Palestinians and round up young men in hunt for terrorists; photos; map; six Israelis are killed when gunmen disguised as Israeli soldiers open fire on bus and cars near Lebanon border; violence comes as Vice Pres Cheney begins tour of 11 nations to rally Arab support against Iraq, and further undermines prospects for Gen Anthony C Zinni's cease-fire mission; Israeli tanks enter Ramallah amid boom of Palestinian grenades and clatter of Israeli machine guns; Annan statement condemns Palestinian terrorist attacks on innocent civilians as 'morally repugnant'; says Israel has right to live in peace within secure recognized borders, but must end occupation, bombings, unnecessary lethal force and daily humiliations of ordinary Palestinians; tells Palestinians they have right to state but must stop terrorism that makes Israelis believe their very existence, not occupation, is target; Israeli official likens Israeli raids to US attack in Afghanistan, which Annan supported as self-defense (M)
news.title: U.N. Chief Tells Israel It Must End 'Illegal Occupation'

news.abstract: Vice Pres Dick Cheney is in Amman, beginning most difficult phase of his 12-day mission to elicit allied support for possible military campaign against Iraq; he encounters immediate opposition from King Abdullah II; Jordanian officials issue statement saying king is urging that Bush administration dispute with Iraq be resolved through dialogue and peaceful means; strong comments from king's officials, and decision to make them public, reflect concern that American offensive against Iraq would open another front in region already racked by instability; Jordan's large Palestinian population and extensive trade with Iraq have long fed Jordanian reluctance to support Washington's stance toward Baghdad; photo (M)
news.title: Cheney, in Jordan, Meets Opposition to Military Move in Iraq

news.abstract: Dr Roy Porter, British author, commentator and historian, dies at age 55 (M)
news.title: Roy Porter, 55, Historian, 'A One-Man Book Factory'

news.abstract: Taiwan has weathered lurid and tacky scandals in recent months; pirated copies of video depicting single female politician in tryst with married lover flooded island in Dec; since then, Taiwan's news media has ladled out almost-daily dollops of love and lust among politicians; this is far cry from two years ago, when newspapers were full of thoughtful analysis about relations with China; photo (M)
news.title: Taipei Journal; In Taiwan, a Scandal a Day Keeps the Blues Away

news.abstract: About 3,000 Taliban prisoners, captured in Kunduz, have been living in miserable conditions in Afghan jail for last four months; Americans interviewed them and took worst of lot to Gunatanamo naval base in Cuba; Uzbek government took about 10 of its citizens; warden freed about 250, most of them either very old or very sick, before recent Muslim holiday; remaining prisoners, all of them Afghan or Pakistani, appear to be largely forgotten; 800 Pakistanis face especially uncertain future; 3,000 men are living in 40 cells in prison, in Shibarghan, Afghanistan, designed to hold about 800; there is little food and hardly any medical aid or medicine; exactly how many prisoners have died remains mystery; photo (M)
news.title: Marooned Taliban Count Out Grim Hours in an Afghan Jail

news.abstract: Relative peace in town of Shlomi, Israel, on Lebanon border, has been shattered by two Arab gunmen who kill six Israelis near town; it is most serious attack in area since Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon in May 2000; attack is claimed by Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, linked to mainstream Palestinian group Al Fatah; Israeli military officials say it could have been work of Hezbollah; photos (M)
news.title: Fatal Attack Shatters Israeli Border Town's Calm

news.abstract: Hundreds of immigrants try to board trains to go from France to England but are stymied by increased security at Channel Tunnel; virtually all freight service to Britain through tunnel is suspended (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Migrants Stifle Channel Traffic

news.abstract: American military officials acknowledge that Taliban and Al Qaeda death tolls they announce nearly every day are just estimates; say that listing Qaeda fighter as 'confirmed dead' does not necessarily mean that military has a body; still, estimates exist, despite assertions of Pentagon officials that they are not in body-count business; photo (M)
news.title: Taliban and Qaeda Death Toll In Mountain Battle Is a Mystery

news.abstract: American firebombing of Tokyo during World War II, which killed estimated 100,000 people and devastated 16 square miles of city, has left surprisingly few traces in popular memory of Japanese, or Americans; it occurred 57 years ago this week, in one horrific night, when 1,665 tons of napalm-filled bombs were dropped; apart from atomic bomb victims, little is done to honor Japan's civilian dead, partly because this might raise questions about Japanese leaders druing war and partly because of avid pursuit of friendship with America; one survivor, Hiroshi Hoshino, is banding together with other survivors to devote himself to preserving memory of people killed in Mar 10, 1954 bombings; photos (M)
news.title: Tokyo Journal; 100,000 People Perished, but Who Remembers?

news.abstract: John Nkomo, home affairs minister in Zimbabwe, acknowledges that next few months will be challenging; United States and Britain have assailed re-election of Pres Robert Mugabe as illegitimate and threaten to toughen sanctions against government's top leaders; western officials, who have already cut off most aid to Zimbabwe, vow to keep their pocketbooks shut; in past decade, poverty rate has climbed from 40 to 75 percent; photo (M)
news.title: Zimbabwe Moderate Offers Assurances to Opposition

news.abstract: Fear and stress on both sides in Mideast is being felt even by household pets; Jerusalem veterinarian has taken to prescribing Valium for pet dogs so nervous from days and nights pierced by gunfire, explosions and sirens that they shake and will not eat; psychic shakiness of some pets is sign of how fear, and coping with it, has become stitched into daily life; in Ramallah, families sleep in basements, order their children not to go outside, and stretch out groceries to last until crossfire dies away; people on both sides are sick of living in fear, and that is chief resource for Anthony C Zinni, Bush administration envoy who arrived in hopes of arranging cease-fire; but along with fear has come anger, and that is Zinni's foremost obstacle; photos (M)
news.title: On Both Sides in the Mideast, Fear and Stress Are Building

news.abstract: Dr Leonid M Ozernoy, Soviet-born astrophysicist and dissident whose campaign to emigrate to United States in 1980's drew international attention, dies at age 62 (M)
news.title: Leonid Ozernoy, 62, Dissident And Soviet-Era Astrophysicist

news.abstract: Bush administration officials say Secretary of State Colin L Powell delivered blunt private demand to Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel on Mar 12 to withdraw from Palestinian-controlled areas to help American efforts to broker cease-fire, and that Amb Daniel C Kurtzer followed up with oral message to Sharon on following day, before American envoy Anthony C Zinni arrived in Jerusalem; Sharon has announced that army will begin staged withdrawal from Ramallah, but State Dept spokesman responds by saying US expects 'complete withdrawal' from all Palestinian-controlled areas; these demands, plus Pres Bush's stern reprimand to Israel on Mar 13, mark distinct policy shift after months of giving Israel virtual green light to move against Palestinians while blaming only Yasir Arafat for violence; Israelis say Sharon wants to avoid any confrontation with Washington, especially given rifts in his own government; photo; map (M)
news.title: U.S. SAYS POWELL DEMANDED PULLOUT BY ISRAELI FORCES

news.abstract: Hemophiliacs infected with virus that causes AIDS by blood products provided by Irish state-run health services in 1980's in begin legal case to overturn 1991 compensation package and get more reparations (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ireland: Blood Victims Seek More Compensation

news.abstract: US is likely to regain seat on UN Human Rights Commission, now that Italy and Spain reportedly agree to step aside (S)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: U.S. May Regain Human Rights Seat

news.abstract: Treasury Sec Paul H O'Neill, in off-the-record comment following speech before Council on Foreign Relations in New York, says that he opposes Bush administration's recent decision to impose tariffs on imported steel and that move will cost more jobs in US than it will save; reiterates long-held position that imposing tariffs risks nation's interests as world's leader in promoting free trade (M)
news.title: TREASURY'S CHIEF IS SAID TO FAULT STEEL TARIFF MOVE

news.abstract: The World Cup of soccer kicks off in South Korea and Japan less than 80 days from now. But instead of keeping their eyes on the ball, instead of harmonizing efforts to manage and secure the games, soccer's overlords are betraying the sport they should serve.
news.title: A corruption scandal looms over global tournament : Soccer chiefs play political game

news.abstract: Vice Pres Cheney signals that Bush administration is determined to confront Iraq despite Arab objections, and says US goal after Afghanistan is to stop terrorism and prevent rogue states from developing weapons of mass destruction; speaks aboard aircraft carrier John C Stennis in Arabian Sea; photo (M)
news.title: Cheney Says Next Goal In U.S. War on Terror Is to Block Access to Arms

news.abstract: Serbian politics twist into chaos as US diplomat, John David Neighbor, is arrested and charged with espionage, along with senior Serb official, Momcilo Perisic; Neighbor is seized in restaurant and driven away with bag over his head, and held incommunicado for 15 hours; US expresses outrage (S)
news.title: In Serbia, Politics in Turmoil As U.S. Diplomat Is Detained

news.abstract: United States and its allies intensify their search for Taliban and Qaeda leaders in waters off Pakistan and Iran, convinced that American-led offensive in eastern Afghanistan has eliminated major terrorist haven and forced Taliban and Qaeda commanders to flee (M)
news.title: Coalition Widens Its Ocean Manhunt

news.abstract: Yugoslav Pres Vojislav Kostunica defends arrests of American diplomat John David Neighbor and senior Serbian government official Momcilo Perisic for espionage; local news media report men are suspected of leaking documents that could help convict former leader Slobodan Milosevic in his trial for war crimes at The Hague; Kostunica's statement will likely deepen his rift with Prime Min Zoran Djindjic, who has called arrests 'scandal'; Perisic has been released and Neighbor, who has diplomatic immunity, was released earlier; officials at American Embassy are outraged at arrest of Neighbor (M)
news.title: Yugoslav Chief Defends Arrest Of American For Espionage

news.abstract: United Nations Human Rights Commission is set to begin annual review of abuses worldwide amid concerns that international commitment to human rights is being eroded by war against terrorism; human rights campaigners have accused United States, Russia, China and other countries of adopting security measures that jeopardize basic rights (M)
news.title: U.N. to Open Rights Review With U.S. On Sidelines

news.abstract: International effort led by United States to expand area where aid workers can operate safety in Sudan's civil war, one of Africa's longest, bears fruit with word that aid may soon be flowing to thousands of civilians isolated in rugged mountain region (M)
news.title: Sudanese Foes Give Consent For Relief Aid For Civilians

news.abstract: Doctors who are members of Pakistan's Shiite religious minority are targets of violence, victims of sectarian violence that has surged in Pakistan in last six weeks; attackers' real target appears to be government of Gen Pervez Musharraf; they are angry about his decision to side with United States in war against Taliban and his domestic policy of getting tough on terrorists at home; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistan Seethes as the Militants Lash Out

news.abstract: Assassination of Archbishop Isaias Duarte Cancino of Cali, Colombia, after officiating over group wedding in poor neighborhood, stuns country already deep in conflict; Colombian law enforcement officials hint rebels are most likely responsible, while church officials say narcotics traffickers may have killed him; his excommunication of rebels for kidnapping civilians and his castigation of drug-tainted candidates in recent congressional elections noted; his involvement in country's civil war and his help in arranging secret meetings between government officials and outlawed rightist paramilitary group responsible for thousands of killings discussed; government offers $483,000 reward for information leading to arrest of killers; thousands show up at Cali's cathedral to pay respects; he is mourned by Pope John Paul II, who issues statement lauding him as generous and valiant pastor; photo (M)
news.title: Rebels or Drug Rings Suspected in Colombian Prelate's Killing

news.abstract: Pres Bush and world leaders from 57 other nations will gather, Monterrey, Mex, to rethink strategy to help speed economic growth in developing countries, which are much poorer than at end of cold war despite fast economic integration of 1990's; Bush administration has promised to increase US foreign aid budget by 15% per year, or $5 billion over three years in first real expansion in more than decade, but administration as well as European leaders and poverty experts are deeply divided about wha
news.title: World Leaders Rethinking Strategy on Aid to Poor

news.abstract: Two terrorist attacks in Israel and heavy gunfire in Bethlehem mark fourth day of shuttle diplomacy by US envoy Gen Anthony C Zinni, who appears to make substantive headway toward brokering cease-fire between Israelis and Palestinians; Zinni holds separate meetings in West Bank and Gaza to work out security arrangements for Israeli withdrawal from all Palestinian-controlled areas; reportedly meets with Yasir Arafat in Ramallah; Israeli forces withdraw from most Palestinian areas invaded in large-scale military operations over past two weeks; remain in and around Bethlehem and on fringes of other areas; gunman opens fire in Kfar Saba killing 18-year-old Isreali high school student and wounding several other people before he is shot dead; suicide bomber sets off explosive near bus stop in northern Jerusalem, wounding woman; map; photo (M)
news.title: Hopes Rise for a Mideast Truce, Despite Attacks

news.abstract: News analysis; Israel's chief concern in conflict with Palestinians is security, hence Bush administration's proposed cease-fire is not just means but end in itself; Palestinians' chief goal is progress toward state, hence cease-fire looks increasingly like obstacle; basic asymmetry explains why Yasir Arafat has for months demanded political negotiations along with security talks, and why he may be starting to get his way; photos (M)
news.title: Arafat's Edge: Violence, And Time, on His Side

news.abstract: American and Afghan officials warn that pockets of Taliban and Al Qaeda fighters remain in southeastern Afghanistan, along border with Pakistan, and that new military operations are needed to defeat them; American commanders ease away from earlier estimates that recent 11-day battle in mountains could prove decisive engagement of five-month-old war; now feel that as many as 1,000 fighters thought to be surrounded during first encounter in Shah-i-Kot may have slipped away, setting scene for further American-led assaults; Russian defense minister, Sergei B Ivanov, citing bitter experience of Soviet occupation troops in Afghanistan in 1980's, says US must be prepared to spend years flushing out fighters; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Planning New Operations to Root Out Scattered Afghan Holdouts

news.abstract: Most of the people killed or wounded in a church attack in Pakistan on Sunday were foreigners, but a principal target was Pakistan's government. News Analysis, Page A14.
news.title: Pakistan's Leaders as Target

news.abstract: Text of UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan's letter to Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel condemning Israel for waging what he says seems to be all-out conventional war on Palestinian civilians (M)
news.title: Kofi Annan's Blunt Words Criticizing Israeli Tactics

news.abstract: Survey published by Peace Now movement says that 34 new Israeli settlement sites have been built in West Bank since Prime Min Ariel Sharon was elected more than year ago (S)
news.title: 34 New West Bank Settlements Spotted

news.abstract: Afghanistan's tribal elite, who lived in exile while Soviets, warring mujahedeen and Taliban exerted control over country, converge on Kandahar to await return of exiled King Mohammad Zahir Shah, who left Afghanistan in 1973; scions of noble, mostly Pashtun, families, they are also courtiers to king whose lineages ensure they will be welcomed back as demigods; believe only 87-year-old monarch can unite Afghans, giving country new and peaceful order; photos (M)
news.title: Exiles Wait for Return Of King to Kandahar

news.abstract: News analysis; while most of people killed or wounded in grenade attack on Protestant church in Islamabad, Pakistan, were foreigners there is little question that principal target was government of Pres Pervez Musharraf, who has become one of point men in Bush administration's war on terrorism; question arises over whether he can survive, not just politically but even physically; photo (M)
news.title: Cloud Over Pakistan: Is Musharraf's Life Safe?

news.abstract: Following are excerpts from the interview Monday at the Elysee Palace with President Jacques Chirac. The excerpts were transcribed and translated by Chirac's staff. The interview was conducted by the executive editor of the International Herald Tribune, David Ignatius, and its senior correspondent, John Vinocur.
news.title: Q&A / Jacques Chirac : What message for the globalization talks?'Liberty, equality, fraternity'

news.abstract: Bush administration officials say that US will refuse to certify that North Korea is complying with its commitments under 1994 accord under which it was to freeze its nuclear activities in exchange for foreign aid; Pres Bush will nevertheless inform Congress that he has also decided to continue fulfilling America's obligations under accord; position appears to be intended to satisfy conservative critics of agreement, who say North Korea may be continuing to develop nuclear weapons at hidden underground sites, while enabling administration to avoid breach with Japan and Soouth Korea, which strongly support accord (M)
news.title: U.S. to Report North Korea Is Not Meeting A-Pact Terms

news.abstract: Bush administration publicly calls for resignation of Jose Bustani as director general of Organization for Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, international organization charged with stopping spread of chemical weapons; says he has mismanaged organization, undertaken ill-considered initiatives and demoralized its technical staff; has sought Bustani's resignation through quiet diplomacy for several weeks to no avail (M)
news.title: White House Wants Chief of Chemical Arms Group to Resign

news.abstract: Marco Biagi, economist and top adviser to Italy's labor minister, Roberto Maroni, is shot dead by two gunmen outside his home in Bologna, and police believe killing is political assassination; Biagi has been helping center-right government draft proposed changes to Italy's labor law, changes that would make it easier to fire workers; photos (M)
news.title: Adviser for Italian Labor Reform Is Killed

news.abstract: Four Indonesian army officers go on trial in Jakarta on charges of failing to prevent militia forces linked to army from massacring 27 people at Roman Catholic church in Suai, East Timor, in Sept 1999; this is first such trial of military defendants, and it shows that despite little interest among public, Indonesia finally feels that it must stand by promise made in 2000 to establish special court to try those accused of responsibility for killing of civilians before and after 1999 vote for East Timor's independence; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesia Begins Trials of Military in East Timor Abuses

news.abstract: Car bomb explodes near American Embassy in Lima, Peru, killing at least 8 people and wounding 40, just three days before Pres Bush is due to arrive for talks; no one claims responsibility; State Dept official says no American citizens were hurt in explosion; photos (M)
news.title: 8 Die in Blast Outside U.S. Embassy in Peru

news.abstract: Palestinian suicide bomber tears intercity bus into twisted metal, killing seven Israelis in Umm El-Fahm, Israel; despite attack, Israeli and Palestinian negotiators meet with American mediator Anthony C Zinni to try to hammer out cease-fire; Palestinians are demanding immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces to positions they held before violence broke out in Sept 2000; Israelis demand that their withdrawal occur only after Palestinians crack down on terror and illegal weapons; radical group Islamic Jihad claims responsibility for latest suicide bombing; photo (M)
news.title: Suicide Bomber Kills 7, but Envoy Presses On

news.abstract: American forces in Afghanistan might cross border into Pakistan to capture or kill Al Qaeda and Taliban fighters thought to have found sanctuary there; Maj Gen Franklin L Hagenbeck, commander of American forces, says such an effort would be 'last resort' carried out with approval of Pakistani leaders; American troops are attacked from several directions just 20 miles from border with Pakistan, near Khost; Hagenbeck says it is not clear whether Americans were caught in fighting between Afghan factions or had come under attack from Taliban or Al Qaeda fighters; one American soldier is injured; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. MIGHT PURSUE QAEDA AND TALIBAN TO PAKISTAN LAIRS

news.abstract: Two immigrants believed to be Kurds are killed and one seriously wounded while trying to sneak into Greece through minefield; thousands of economic and political refugees try to enter Europe through Greece (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Greece: Immigrants Killed In Minefield

news.abstract: World Health Orgn releases its first list of manufacturers of safe AIDS drugs, move that could help bring down price of AIDS medicines for poor countries; list includes Cipla Ltd, large Indian producer of generics, and three smaller European ones; decision represents setback for pharmaceutical multinationals who want only patent-holders to decide what discounts to offer on their most expensive and profitable products (M)
news.title: New List of Safe AIDS Drugs, Despite Industry Lobby

news.abstract: India's upper house of Parliament rejects anti-terrorism bill favored by ruling Hindu nationalists; opponents fear law, which would let suspects be detained for 30 days without appearing in court, would be used against Muslims (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Anti-Terror Bill Rejected

news.abstract: So you thought the Winter Games were over. In Nuuk, Greenland, and Iqaluit, Canada, the opening ceremony took place only Sunday.
news.title: Some tough competition heats up the Arctic Winter Games : Now starring in the knuckle hop

news.abstract: LONDON:—  They're small, nearly valueless — and a nuisance to millions of Europeans.
news.title: Euro quandary:It's no small change

news.abstract: New York Times correspondent Serge Schemamann describes latest suicide bombing in Jerusalem, which he witnessed first-hand; describes noise of explosion, followed by people screaming and running, some people laying on ground injured; says carnage and debris were everywhere; notes that Israeli reaction to suicide bombings is invariably to erase their traces as quickly as possible, as if to say they will not give in to this; says Israelis are living in fear, and wonders how much more they can take (M)
news.title: Up Close, Too Close, to a Suicide Bombing

news.abstract: British government shies away from promised ban on fox hunting in face of divided Parliament and anger from country's influential countyside; pledges final action on revised proposal in fall (S)
news.title: Fox Hunters In England Win a Reprieve

news.abstract: United States and Russia narow differences in two days of talks in Geneva on pact to reduce nuclear arms, but differences remain on how warheads will be counted and whether they will be destroyed or stored when taken out of operation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Progress Reported In Talks With U.S.

news.abstract: British High Court judge, Dame Elizabeth Butler-Sloss, rules that paralzyed woman has right to die and that it is her decision rather than her doctors' whether life-support machine should be shut off; woman, 43-year-old former social worker, appealed to court after doctors at hospital where she is in intensive care say ethics blocks them from following her wishes to end her life; woman has needed ventilator to remain alive since ruptured blood vessel in her neck year ago left her unable to breathe unaided (M)
news.title: Paralyzed Woman Has Right To Die, a British Judge Rules

news.abstract: Pres Bush calls for 'new compact' for global development by insisting that rich nations give foreign aid to poor nations only if poor nations undertake broad range of political, legal and economic reforms, speech to conference on global aid to developing world, Monterrey, Mexico; photo; 171 nations sign 'Monterrey Consensus,' accord committing them to goals of doubling development to poor and halving world poverty by 2015 (M)
news.title: Bush, in Monterrey, Speaks of Conditional Global Aid

news.abstract: Gen Pervez Musharraf, Pakistan leader, plans to stay in power for at least another five years by holding referendum on matter, probably in May; photo of Musharraf with Vice Premier Wu Bangguo of China (M)
news.title: Pakistan Chief Said to Plan A Vote to Extend His Rule

news.abstract: Bush administration is convinced that Ahmed Omar Sheikh, militant accused of killing Daniel Pearl, will eventually be handed over to United States even if Pakistani government follows through with its plan to try him for crime in Pakistan; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Confident of Suspect's Extradition From Pakistan

news.abstract: Riots in India that have laid bare simmering hostilities between Hindu majority and Muslim minority have also left secular Indians fearing for future and shaken friendships across divide; Akbar Divecha, retired Muslim judge in Ahmedabab who was rescued by his Hindu friend, Sanjay Shah, discuss shrinking space for secularism in their country (M)
news.title: Riots Shake Friendships And Faiths In India

news.abstract: Former Belarus Pres Stanislav Shushkevich is suffering inventive punishment at hands of current Pres Aleksandr Lukashenko, political enemy who is refusing to have Shushkevich's pension indexed for inflation; Shushkevich says inflation has left monthly pension worth about $1.80, enough for four loaves of excellent brown bread or bottle of vodka, but not both (M)
news.title: Ex-Leader of Belarus Challenges a Punishment by Pension

news.abstract: Sec Gen Kofi Annan releases report on increasing security at UN offices around world (S)
news.title: U.N. Reviews Plans to Protect Its Offices Around the World

news.abstract: Salvadorans await Pres Bush's visit in hopes that US, which lavished money on country during 12-year civil war, will reward peace and political loyalty with economic aid; photo; Central Americans are coming to realise that region is unlikely to regain importance it held during cold war; former US national security official Robert A Pastor says this is moment, when countries have fragile democracies, that US could have most decisive impact on their long-term security (M)
news.title: Central America Waiting To Reap Beneifts of Peace

news.abstract: China's most influential liberal newspaper, Southern Weekend, reportedly cancels article on misuse of funds at large government-backed charity, Project Hope, which helps poor children stay in school; government pressure suspected (M)
news.title: Under Pressure, Chinese Newspaper Pulls Exposé on a Charity

news.abstract: Tribal leaders from treacherous mountainous areas along Pakistan's border with Afghanistan warn US military not to carry out threat to enter region in pursuit of Al Qaeda fighters: some regard US as enemy and say their people will sacrifice their lives to keep American soldiers off their land; say no foreigner may enter tribal lands without permission and that warning must be taken seriously; war in Afghanistan is seen dragging on indefinitely if tribal areas, which share porous 450-mile border with Afghanistan, become safe haven for Taliban and Al Qaeda fighters to rest and regroup; maps (M)
news.title: Tribal Leaders in Pakistan Warn the U.S. to Keep Out

news.abstract: Vice Pres Dick Cheney says it is important that Yasir Arafat attend upcoming Arab summit in Beirut, development that would require Prime Minister Ariel Sharon of Israel to lift travel ban; says he has no immediate plans to meet with Arafat because of failure to meet US condition that he take steps to establish cease-fire and stop terrorist attacks against Israel; Sharon weighs Cheney's appeal; says Arafat has given no orders to halt attacks; US officials hope Beirut meeting will endorse Saudi peace plan calling for Israel to withdraw from territory it has occupied since 1967 in return for full normalization of relations with Arab nations; fear meeting could turn into cascade of criticism of Israel and US if Israel does not allow Arafat to attend; Saudi and other Arab leaders also urge Cheney to help Arafat attend Beirut meeting (M)
news.title: U.S. PRODS ISRAEL TO ALLOW ARAFAT TO GO TO SUMMIT

news.abstract: News analysis; Vice Pres Dick Cheney has presented Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon with dilemma: let Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat escape his siege and attend summit of Arab leaders in Beirut, or risk having Israel look as if it sabotaged Arab bid for peace in Middle East; has asked Sharon to put aside conditions he set for Arafat to travel and let his old nemesis score at least short-term political victory at his expense (M)
news.title: For Sharon, a Painful Choice

news.abstract: Philippine troops clash several times in last week with Muslim rebels holding American missionary couple Martin and Graciela Burnham hostage, leading to suggestions that attempt to rescue couple from remote jungle island of Basilan may be imminent; map (M)
news.title: Philippine Clashes May Point to Attempt to Rescue American Hostages From Rebels

news.abstract: 1.4 million Arabs who live inside Israel as full citizens of state are increasingly isolated as tensions rise between Israelis and Palestinians; many have grown increasingly angry and some have become violent, causing alarm within Israeli government; two sides seem to be growing further apart; several Israeli Arab members of Parliament, reflecting views of constituents, are making statements Jewish colleagues consider treasonous; recent public opinion survey indicates many Israeli Jews view Arabs as dangerous fifth column--an enemy from within; some Israeli-Arab residents of Umm al Fahm comment; map; photo (M)
news.title: Anger and Isolation Roil Israeli Arabs

news.abstract: Central American leaders sign accord to guarantee investment and allow service companies to operate freely in region; say they have made significant advances toward regional economic integration (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Central American Unity

news.abstract: Dr Cesar Milstein, who shared 1984 Nobel Prize in Medicine for revolutionary technique to produce antibodies that latch onto specific proteins, dies at age 74; photo (M)
news.title: César Milstein, 74, Who Won Joint Nobel Prize in Medicine

news.abstract: Ugandan officials armed with automatic weapons patrol Lake Victoria in search of crocodiles so aggressive they frequently overturn small boats and have eaten some 43 people in last six months (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Uganda: Crocodiles Kill 43 People

news.abstract: Some 100 demonstrators rally outside Chinese Embassy, Seoul, South Korea, protesting roundup of North Koreans who fled across border into China; Dr Norbert Vollertsen, who wages international effort to publicize harsh conditions in North Korea, is detained briefly after scuffle with police (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Support For North Koreans

news.abstract: South African judge affirms government most distribute AIDS drug nevirapine at public hospitals while it appeals ruling that it make drug available; drug cuts risk of transmission of HIV from pregnant mothers to their unborn babies (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: South Africa: Government Must Offer AIDS Drug

news.abstract: Negotiators meeting in Geneva to draft global treaty curbing tobacco use wrap up fourth round of talks without progress (S)
news.title: World Briefing | World: No Progress On Tobacco Curbs

news.abstract: Rival groups of ethnic Albanian guerrillas wage fierce nighttime battle, killing two fighters and wounding five bystanders (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Macedonia: Guerrillas Fight Each Other

news.abstract: Committee to Protect Journalists reports 37 journalists were slain worldwide as direct result of their work in 2001, up from 24 in 2000; says at least 24 were apparently victims of governments or their sympathizers who objected to reporters' work; says number of journalists in prison jumped to 118 from 81 in 2001 (M)
news.title: Killings of Journalists Rose In 2001 From the Year Before

news.abstract: Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat says he will not attend Arab League summit meeting in Beirut after Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon says he wants right to bar him from returning to West Bank; decision is setback for Bush administration; casts doubt on Saudi peace plan; efforts of United States envoy Gen Anthony C Zinni to mediate Israeli-Palestinian cease-fire also seems stalled; suspicious vehicle halted by Israeli security forces explodes, killing both men inside, before it can reach apparent target, crowded Jerusalem shopping mall; two members of unarmed international monitoring force are ambushed and shot dead, near Hebron; survivor says uniformed Palestinian opened fire on them; security in Israel is extraordinary in advance of Passover; photo (M)
news.title: ARAFAT SAYS FEAR OF EXILE WILL KEEP HIM FROM MEETING

news.abstract: Earthquake and its aftershocks raze Nahrin, densely-populated city in remote northeast Afghanistan that had been filling up with refugees returning home, and several villages; kill up to 2,000 people, injure 4,000 and leave up to 10,000 people homeless; Afghan government and aid agencies scurry to send aid to hard-to-reach mountain area; maps; photos (M)
news.title: TOLL IN THOUSANDS POSSIBLE AS QUAKE HITS AFGHAN TOWN

news.abstract: Jews across New York region welcome in Passover, but with forbidding chill of anger and frustration over latest suicide bombing in Israel; many of those attending Seders say latest bloodshed in Israel, coming after months of almost daily violence, has cast pall over their gatherings, prompting feelings of doubt and guilt over events in Middle East; photo (M)
news.title: Emotions Swirl at Passover Gatherings

news.abstract: Team of Russian journalists win right to continue broadcasting on national television after being shut off airwaves in January in bankruptcy proceedings they say were rigged; government commission votes unanimously to award five-year broadcasting license to Media-Sotsium, nonprofit group that includes former Russian Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov, business magnate Arkady Volsky and some of country's most critical journalists; supporters are doubtful about how much control journalists wil have over how station will be run (M)
news.title: Nonstate TV In Russia Wins License To Broadcast

news.abstract: Kamel Hossain, United Nations's special representative on human rights in Afghanistan, urges significant expansion of international security force there, warning that failing to do this could torpedo efforts to create democratic institutions in war-devastated country; his recommendation runs counter to view of United States and France, which have expressed opposition to expanding 4,800-member International Security Assistance Force (M)
news.title: U.N. Official Calls for a Much Larger International Force in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Tokyo High Court rejects appeal for government compensation for 150,000 civilians and military personnel held prisoner in Asia during World War II; ruling is latest in string of setbacks for people seeking compensation from Japan for war-related atrocities (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: War Prisoners Lose Compensation Bid

news.abstract: PARIS:—  The Valentino fashion house was sold Wednesday, after six months on the block, at a discount that signals the bursting of a seven-year bubble of rising prices for luxury companies — and the end of a feeding frenzy of acquisitions in the luxury market.
news.title: Valentino sale reveals sour market for high-end firms : Luxury has gone out of fashion

news.abstract: Federal health officials, even with more abundant supplies of smallpox vaccine expected by end of year, say they still will not recommend mass vaccination to prepare for possible terrorist attack; but they leave themselves plenty of room to change course, saying repeatedly that issue is still open for public discussion; Health and Human Services Sec Tommy Thompson and Dr Anthony S Fauci, head of National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, say that vaccine has significant risks and likelihood of terrorists' using smallpox is considered low; diagram shows how vaccine is dispensed; photo (M)
news.title: A Nation Challenged: The Vaccine; Officials See No Grounds For a Mass Smallpox Effort

news.abstract: Pakistani human rights organization issues report painting bleak picture of respect for human dignity there, particularly for women and children; says women have 'almost no rights' and are bound to follow wishes of male family members, that nearly half country's children are malnourished, that physical and sexual abuse of children is 'rampant' and that young boys are smuggled to Middle East to serve as jockeys in camel races; report expands conventional definition of human rights, looking at social and economic conditions, including health and education; State Dept's annual human rights report had similarly critical assessment of Pakistan, although it took note of fact that Pakistani press is able to publish 'relatively freely' (M)
news.title: Pakistani Group Offers Bleak View of Pakistan's Rights Record

news.abstract: LONDON:—  With armies of accountants in offices from Tokyo to Toronto, Arthur Andersen created the model for the globalization of a fragmented industry. Now it is suffering in part because of its success.
news.title: Model of globalization at risk of losing international clout : At Andersen, success backfires

news.abstract: United Nations Security Council has taken up issue of Israel and its relations with neigbors many times through years; examples of how council has called on Israel and its neighbors to settle half century of conflict (M)
news.title: Mideast Turmoil; U.N. and the Middle East: Many Calls for Peace

news.abstract: a new batch of old smallpox vaccine*
news.title: A Nation Challenged: The Drug Makers; A New Batch of Old Smallpox Vaccine

news.abstract: US to shut about half of military bases in South Korea over next decade, but will not reduce number of troops from current 37,000; Gen Thomas A Schwartz explains; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: U.S. To Close Bases

news.abstract: Excerpts from Sec Colin Powell's news conference on latest violence in Middle East (S)
news.title: In Powell's Words, a Plea to Both Sides

news.abstract: First American soldier killed in assault on Al Qaeda and Taliban forces in eastern Afghanistan this month may have died from fire from US warplane, not enemy mortar blasts as initially thought; Gen Tommy Franks announces investigation into death of Special Forces soldier Stanley L Harriman; also reports US now has more than 7,000 troops in Afghanistan, and releases reports on ten incidents of American and allied troops reportedly killed by coalition fire, and of attacks on possible civilian sites (M)
news.title: Strike by a U.S. Plane, Rather Than Enemy Fire, May Have Killed a G.I.

news.abstract: Article explains range of ideologies and allegiances of Palestinian factions involved in terrorism against Israel, and sources of their financing; four major groups are Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad and Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine; chart on numbers of people killed and modes of attack, including suicide bombings (M)
news.title: In the Arabs' Struggle Against Israel, There Are Many Players

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II is forced by ill health to severely curtail participation in Holy Week ceremonies at Vatican (S)
news.title: Pope Is Forced To Curtail Usual Role In Holy Week

news.abstract: Reports of capture of top Al Qaeda commander, Abu Zubaydah, noted (S)
news.title: A Top Qaeda Aide May Be Held Captive

news.abstract: US troops will likely remain in Philippines longer than six months announced when they were dispatched to train Filipino military in counterterrorism and help rescue two American missionary hostages; heart of training by 160 Special Operations forces on Basilan has yet to begin (S)
news.title: U.S. Antiterror Forces May Extend Stay on Philippines Island

news.abstract: US involvement in Angola from 1970's reviewed (M)
news.title: From Old Files, a New Story Of U.S. Role in Angolan War

news.abstract: US joins other UN Security Council members in resolution calling on Israel to withdraw troops from Ramallah and other Palestinian cities (M)
news.title: U.S. Joins Council Vote Telling Israel To Withdraw

news.abstract: UN Security Council authorizes new mission for Afghanistan that will leave most of responsibility for rebuilding with Afghan government (S)
news.title: U.N. Opens Rebuilding Effort, With Limits, in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Suicide bomber from Islamic group Hamas blows self up in restaurant in Haifa, Israel, killing self and 14 others and wounding more than 40; attack is among deadliest of 18-month intifada and shocks both Arabs and Jews; Arab-owned Matza restaurant was one of rare places in Israel where Jews felt they could find refuge in company of Arabs; dead include Israeli Arabs; suicide bomber also strikes station for paramedics in settlement of Efrat, south of Bethlehem; kills self and wounds four medics; photos; maps (M)
news.title: Bomber Strikes Jews and Arabs At Rare Refuge

news.abstract: American officials say man believed to be Abu Zubaydah, chief of operations of Osama bin Laden's Al Qaeda terrorist network, was seriously wounded when captured recently in Pakistan and is in US custody; say US is more certain than ever of his identity; capture would represent major accomplishment in American campaign against terrorism, especially since Zubaydah is believed to have taken control of effort to rebuild Al Qaeda network (M)
news.title: New Confidence U.S. Has a Qaeda Leader

news.abstract: Once bustling city of Ramallah--commercial, political and intellectual capital of Palestinian West Bank--has become ghost town, quiet except for invading Israeli tanks and armored personnel carriers; soldiers have all but taken over city on third day of siege of Yasir Arafat's compound; siege of city by Israeli forces described; photo (M)
news.title: Residents Cower in Vibrant Ramallah, Now a Ghost Town Occupied by Israelis

news.abstract: Leaders of Canada's separatist Parti Quebecois now say they have no intention of calling referendum to declare province's independence from Canada any time in foreseeable future; will refocus on holding on to its control of province's government; is moderating image by building bridges with English-speaking population and pressing central government for greater share of federal spending; shift reflects sharp decline in party's popularity over last several months; recent polls suggest it will have tough time beating back challenge by Liberal Party in next elections, expected within year; its narrow defeat in divisive separatist referendums in 1980 and 1995 recalled (M)
news.title: Separatist Leaders in Quebec Shift Their Focus to Stability

news.abstract: News analysis of Pakistan government's firm cooperation with US in war against terrorism; few countries have done as much; government's willingness to take on strident nationalists and Islamic extremists and recent decision to allow FBI and CIA to conduct raid with Pakistani police in Islamabad for Al Qaeda suspects discussed; while Bush administration has recognized contributions of Gen Pervez Musharraf, it has been slow to deliver on promises of economic aid and other assistance to impoverished country; without some tangible benefits, there is question of how long Musharraf government can continue to mobilize public opinion behind its antiterrorism policies (M)
news.title: Pakistan's Bold Alliance: U.S. Ties Holding Firm

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, April 2 - Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said on Tuesday he would let Palestinian President Yasser Arafat leave his besieged headquarters in the West Bank city of Ramallah only on condition it was a "one-way ticket."
news.title: Sharon Says Arafat Can Leave Ramallah on a "One-Way Ticket"

news.abstract: Rising tide of anti-Semitic incidents in France prompts sharp government reaction, with Prime Min Lionel Jospin vowing harsh action after synagogue in Marseilles is destroyed by arson in addition to three others set ablaze over Easter-Passover weekend; he meets with Jewish community leaders; says 1,100 extra police officers will be deployed to guard country's synagogues and Jewish schools; anti-Semitic attacks have soared in past year, reflecting growing radicalization and anger of France's large Muslim population, numbering about five million, as violence in Middle East increases and as Israel applies growing military pressure on Palestinians; photos (M)
news.title: France Vows Harsh Action After More Synagogues Burn

news.abstract: Bush administration, after year of lobbying by energy industry, is seeking ouster of Dr Robert T Watson, chief scientist at World Bank and highly regarded climate expert who has for nearly six years directed international panel of hundreds of experts assessing global warming; he is outspoken advocate of idea that human actions, mainly burning of fossil fuels, are contributing to global warming and must be changed to avert environmental upheavals; his term is expiring and State Department has chosen not to renominate him to head panel (M)
news.title: Dispute Arises Over a Push To Change Climate Panel

news.abstract: Peta Thornycroft, correspondent for Daily Telegraph of London, is freed in Zimbabwe after being detained on charges of working in country illegally (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Zimbabwe: Court Frees Journalist

news.abstract: Afghanistan's desolate and remote border region, formed where eastern Afghan province of Khost meets Pakistan, is under intense scrutiny following persistent reports that Al Qaeda and Taliban forces are regrouping to mount guerrilla attacks from sanctuaries across border in Pakistan; recent arrests of suspected Al Qaeda members in areas under tribal control on Pakistani side of border, carried out by Pakistani authorities, give credence to reports that large numbers of fugitive fighters have fled where Americans are unable as yet to reach them; rugged frontier that stretches from legendary Khyber Pass to Quetta is famous for smuggling routes, but gave sanctuary in 1980's to mujahedeen fighters who traveled back and forth across border to stage attacks on Soviet forces; frustrated American officials hint they may reach across frontier to carry out military strikes; Pakistani leaders, who have sent 12,000 troops to border areas, indicate if any military action is needed they will undertake it themselves; photos; maps (M)
news.title: Qaeda and Taliban May Ply Pakistan's Porous Frontier

news.abstract: Sammy Abu Samhadanah, who commands Gaza Strip militia allied with Yasir Arafat, plots strategy if Israel expands military action from West Bank; Israeli security official says Gaza is not of as much concern because recent suicide attacks have been carried out by Palestinians from West Bank (M)
news.title: Gazans Await Israeli Attack Despite Lack Of a Buildup

news.abstract: US State Department meets with industry lobbyists unhappy about international science panel assessing climate change, and then announces support for Indian engineer Dr Rajendra K Pachauri to become panel's new chairman; current chairman Dr Robert T Watson has long pressed for aggressive action to curb heat-trapping gases (S)
news.title: U.S. to Back Scientist From India To Replace Global Warming Expert

news.abstract: PARIS:—  The rise of crime in France, a vast concern that may well decide the outcome of the presidential election next month, is one of the areas of French life where everybody senses the extent of the problem, but politicians shut up about the deepest nature of the causes.
news.title: NEWS Analysis : Candidates skirt facts on crime in France

news.abstract: Macedonian and ethnic Albanian police patrols resume in two villages that have been strongholds of Albanian guerrillas (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Macedonia: Former Enemies Cooperate

news.abstract: Defense Secretary Donald H. Rumsfeld rejected suggestions today that Abu Zubaydah might be tortured to get information.
news.title: Rumsfeld Says Captured Qaeda Leader Won't Be Tortured

news.abstract: President Bush said today he was sending Secretary of State Colin L. Powell to the Middle East next week.
news.title: Bush Says U.S. Is to Assume Stronger Role in Ending Violence

news.abstract: Leaders of African countries entangled in Congo civil war meet in Zambia (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Congo: Summit Meeting On Civil War

news.abstract: Egypt downgrades its relations with Israel in pointed warning that intensifying war against Palestinian Authority of Yasir Arafat is ratcheting up Arab resentment to dangerous levels; Egypt is Israel's largest and most important peace partner; it says it is suspending 'all contacts' with Israeli Government but would keep open diplomatic channel to deal with crisis in West Bank; decision falls short of formally breaking ties, and seems intended as much to placate rising frustration among Egyptian public as to signal anger over widening Israeli military campaign; sixth day of demonstrations at Cairo University pits students demanding expulsion of Israeli Amb Gideon Ben-Ami against riot police; Palestinian leaders are pressing King Abdullah II of Jordan to downgrade his kingdom's ties to Israel as well; photo (M)
news.title: Swamped by Protests, Egypt Cuts Nearly All Ties to Israel

news.abstract: Afghan security officials say they arrested hundreds of political opponents who were conspiring to mount bombing campaign against government of Hamid Karzai and against former king Mohammad Zahir Shah; Karzai advisers says plot appears to have been aimed at toppling government or destabilizing his regime; say conspiracy is linked to Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, longtime warlord known for his anti-Western views and ruthlessness on battlefield; he was last seen in Pakistan and Iran; with details of alleged plot so sketchy, roundup of well-known opponents of Karzai's government seems certain to prompt suspicions that government fabricated threat to crush its opponents; wave of arrests illustrates fragility of American-backed effort to foster democracy in country with long tradition of cutthroat and tyrannical politics; photo (M)
news.title: AFGHANS ROUND UP HUNDREDS IN PLOT AGAINST LEADERS

news.abstract: American-style sushi is being served with great success at restaurants in Japan, sushi's country of origin; this culinary cross-fertilization illustrates high-speed ricochet of American and other influences across Pacific; not long ago most Americans considered sushi to be far too exotic; photos; map (M)
news.title: Tokyo Journal; Sushi Comes Home, With Cream Cheese and Chili

news.abstract: Pres Bush thrusts his administration into central role in Middle East crisis, demanding that Israel withdraw from West Bank and telling Arab nations and Yasir Arafat that they must actively oppose terrorism if they hope to create Palestinian state, speech in Rose Garden; says he will send Secretary of State Colin L Powell to region next week; Bush aides say speech sets president on course of acting as central mediator in peace effort, role he previously sought to avoid; say he decided to intervene more directly because he fears that long-term allies in region like Egypt and Jordan are facing destabilizing protests over Israeli-Palestinian conflict; senior aide to Yasir Arafat says Arafat accepts Bush's remarks 'without conditions'; in Israel, Prime Min Ariel Sharon says military operation in West Bank will continue and that he will refuse to negotiate before terror is subdued; Bush's speech seeks to strike far more delicate balance than he has in comments of recent weeks, when he seemed to be giving Israel virtual green light to defend itself however it deems necessary; Bush now says Israeli settlement activity in occupied territories must stop and occupation must end; he calls on Israel to show respect for dignity of Palestinian people; Bush spares no one--not Israel, Palestinians or Arab nations--in his criticism or his challenges; photos (L)
news.title: BUSH DEMANDS ISRAELI PULLOUT; INSISTS ARAFAT OPPOSE TERROR; POWELL WILL GO TO THE MIDEAST

news.abstract: Asia North KOREA: Public Enemy NO. 1 ; MYANMAR: Freedom, Some Day, For Dissident; INDIA: Accusations Of Brutality ; NEPAL: State Of Emergency Eased.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Indian Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee visits riot-torn state of Gujarat and pleads for end to violence that has pitted Muslims against Hindus and left at least 815 people dead; speaks angrily about fact that some people have been burned to death; says he is shamed by taint of such violence; many Muslims are disappointed that he did not chastise Narendra Modi, Hindu nationalist chief minister in state who has been accused of turning blind eye to horrendous rampages against Muslims during first days of violence; photo (M)
news.title: Angry and Ashamed, Indian Prime Minister Tours Riot-Torn State

news.abstract: Gen Wiranto, commander of Indonesian Army when militias backed by military rampaged through East Timor three years ago, killing more than 100 people, says he was not responsible for 'the incident'; blames United Nations and East Timorese police for violence that followed referendum in which majority of East Timorese voted for independence; independent commission in Indonesia and UN panel concluded two years ago that military, which opposed independence, supported militias; Wiranto appears as witness, not defendant, at trial on human rights abuses by military in East Timor; five mid-level military officers as well as police officers and civilian leaders are defendants; trial has direct bearing on Indonesia's relations with US, where Congressional restrictions are placed on American aid to Indonesian military because of human rights abuses in East Timor (M)
news.title: Indonesia General Denies Responsibility for East Timor Killings

news.abstract: Europe SPAIN: Europe-asia Meeting On Migrants; FRANCE: Ruling On Diana's Death Upheld.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Police in Northern Ireland make three arrests and charge Irish Republican Army was behind break-in at Special Branch headquarters in which intelligence data about undercover operations and informants was stolen; Sinn Fein, IRA's political wing, scores arrests as 'smoke screen' to hide security service role in theft (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Northern Ireland: I.R.A. Accused In Break-In

news.abstract: Bomb is found and defused at entrance to Jewish cemetery, Strasbourg, France; police arrest five people in connection with firebomb thrown at suburban Paris synagogue; say three people suspected of hurling firebombs at Montpellier synagogue have confessed; police action seems to reflect urgency felt by Prime Min Lionel Jospin's government in face of complaints that there has not been enough public outcry over anti-Semitic attacks; judicial officials probe arson charges against at least dozen men who crashed two cars through gates of Lyon synagogue and set them on fire; 21 prominent French Jews publicly denounce Israel's occupation of Palestinian West Bank cities; photo (M)
news.title: Bomb Is Defused at Entrance to Jewish Cemetery in France

news.abstract: Residents of Bremen, German
news.title: Germans of One Mind About Two Rivals: Dubious

news.abstract: United States officials say Pentagon has ordered cut in naval forces committed to war in Afghanistan in sign that peak fighting there has passed and that military is adjusting its troops for long-term global war on terrorism; say US will withdraw one of two aircraft carriers and half of 4,000 marines aboard ships from northern Arabian Sea; other signs that military prepares for long haul in Afghanistan noted; photo (M)
news.title: Pentagon to Cut Navy Role in Afghan War

news.abstract: Africa NIGERIA: Court Sides With Government On Oil; SUDAN: Cease-fire Monitors.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Israeli forces and Palestinian militants intensify their fighting in Nablus and Jenin on West Bank; Israeli officials interpret Pres Bush's latest demand that Israel withdraw from West Bank without delay as providing them sufficient scope to continue operation, at least until Sec of State Colin L Powell arrives in Israel on truce-seeking mission; photos (M)
news.title: Israel Presses On With Attacks, Focusing on Northern West Bank

news.abstract: Edmund Stoiber makes malaise of German economy his core issue in campaign to unseat Chancellor Gerhard Schroder in Sept 22 elections; Stoiber, candidate of Christian Democratic Union and his own Christian Social Union, gives interview with American journalists in advance of visit to Washington in which he tries to show his familiarity with foreign policy, urges even closer relationship with US and works to undercut any idea that he is provincial xenophobe, while defending restrictions on immigration; his perception as dour bureaucrat and 'Bavarian pit bull' puts him at disadvantage with the personable, telegenic Schroder; photo (M)
news.title: For Dogged German Challenger, It's Still About the Economy

news.abstract: US trade representative, Robert B Zoellick, tours high-tech plants in Indonesia to show that countries of Southeast Asia can stand up to looming economic force of China through trade cooperation; US hopes to right what it sees as unhealthy imbalance between China and smaller countries to south by urging them to reduce trade barriers among themselves to attract more outside investment (M)
news.title: U.S. Envoy Campaigns For Trade Pacts On Asian Trip

news.abstract: Excerpts from news conference held by Pres Bush and Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain in Crawford, Tex; photos (M)
news.title: Allies Discuss Terrorism and the Middle East: Bush and Blair on Policy

news.abstract: Palestinian governor of Bethlehem, Muhammad Madani, vows that neither he nor any of other Palestinians holed up inside Church of Nativity will leave until Israeli troops end their five-day siege; an archbishop, two nuns and two female Palestinian church employees leave church, which holds about 150 Palestinians, 40 priests and other church employees; Israelis say they have no intention of firing on church or harming anyone inside -- as long as any wanted gunmen inside are turned over to them; photo (M)
news.title: Vowing to Stay at a Holy Site As Troops and Impasse Linger

news.abstract: Victims of bombing in Afghanistan hand in petitions from 400 families at American Embassy in Kabul, part of growing movement to demand compensation from US for loss of families and homes; represent some of possibly thousands of civilians who suffered in campaign against Taliban and Al Qaeda; Global Exchange, human rights organization supporting victims and their claims, estimates about 2,000 families may have suffered losses in bombings; photo (M)
news.title: Shattered Afghan Families Demand U.S. Compensation

news.abstract: Still a Standoff in Diplomacy, Too
news.title: Still a Standoff in Diplomacy, Too

news.abstract: News analysis; Arab anger and demonstrations across Middle East do not represent immediate threat to moderate governments that have served as America's principal friends and allies in region, but unrelenting siege by Israeli forces in occupied West Bank and at Ramallah headquarters of Yasir Arafat may be radicalizing politics of region and creating threat to peace and recognition of Jewish state by rising generation of Arabs (M)
news.title: Popular Arab Anger: A Long-Term Threat to the Foundations of Peace

news.abstract: Voters in Hungary hand slim but unexpected defeat to governing center-right leaders in first round of parliamentary elections, setting stage for even tougher final round of voting in two weeks; reject outright place in Parliament for far-right Freedom and Justice Party, whose possible voice in future government was major question of campaign; photo (M)
news.title: Hungary Socialists Win Narrowly in Early Parliamentary Vote

news.abstract: Following is the text of a speech by Ariel Sharon to a special session of the Israeli Parliament, as provided by the Prime Minister's Office.
news.title: Text of Speech by Sharon to Israeli Parliament

news.abstract: After 13 Israeli soldiers were killed in Jenin, Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said today that Israel's military offensive in the West Bank would continue.
news.title: 13 Israeli Soldiers Killed; Sharon Says Offensive Will Go On

news.abstract: Pentagon prepares to increase its commitment to global war on terror by readying new troops for deployment to Yemen and Philippines; logistics assessment team already in Yemen is paving way for arrival of as many as 150 American troops; initial group of 50 to 70 soldiers will be sent by end of month, and will consist predominantly of Special Forces troops; will also include seaport and airport security specialists; training by Navy and Coast Guard of Yemeni forces that patrol 1,500-mile-long coast noted; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld says there are no plans to resume port calls in Yemeni port of Aden, where terrorists bombed destroyer Cole 16 months ago killing 16 American sailors; presence of about 575 American troops in Philippines advising and training local troops to combat Abu Sayyaf rebels on Basilan island noted; Rumsfeld says he is awaiting final proposal from military advisers for deployment of additional troops, mostly engineers and civilian affairs specialists (S)
news.title: U.S. to Send More G.I.'s to Yemen and Philippines

news.abstract: International commission charged with disarming Irish Republican Army says organization has for second time removed batch of weapons, ammunition and explosives from its illegal arsenal (M)
news.title: I.R.A.'s Illegal Arsenal Reduced In a 2nd Act of Disarmament

news.abstract: Afghanistan's defense minister Muhammad Fahim escapes apparent assassination attempt unhurt as bomb explodes in crowd lining streets of Jalalabad to welcome him for visit; four people are killed and 18 are wounded; attack is seen as latest incident in organized effort to undermine American-backed government of Hamid Karzai, which took office in December (M)
news.title: Bomb Kills 4 In Jalalabad But Minister Is Uninjured

news.abstract: Secretary of State Colin L. Powell said he intended to meet with Yasir Arafat this weekend. Mr. Powell plans to meet with Mr. Sharon in Jerusalem on Friday.
news.title: Powell Affirms That He Intends to Meet Arafat

news.abstract: Parliaments of Serbia and Montenegro approve plan to remodel Yugoslavia as new state called Serbia and Montenegro (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Yugoslavia: Restructuring Plan Advances

news.abstract: Greed and corruption are allowing Mexican fishing fleets to drain Gulf of California, decimating every important species and leaving impoverished local fishermen with meager catches; photos; American and Japanese ships were first to exploit waters as many governments pour subsidies into commercial fishing fleets, causing fisheries to collapse around world; Gulf of California is world's youngest sea, created when San Andreas fault split Mexico millions of years ago and let Pacific pour in; waters are home home to 875 species of fish and 30 species of marine mammal, which have been killed indiscriminately for years (M)
news.title: In Mexico, Greed Kills Fish by the Seaful

news.abstract: Focus of French presidential election is likely to remain on law and order following death of police officer in Vannes; gunman apparently furious over driving incident sprayed bullets into police station (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Policeman Killed In 'Road Rage'

news.abstract: Pakistan Pres Pervez Musharraf opens one-man campaign to remain in office for five years, delivering crisp, rousing speech at huge organized rally in Islamabad; Musharraf is exempt from ban on public rallies because he has no political party and is ostensibly not waging political campaign (M)
news.title: Musharraf Makes Debut On the Stump

news.abstract: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon vowed to continue Israel's military sweep through the West Bank after a Palestinian suicide bomber attacked an Israeli bus today.
news.title: In New Rebuff to U.S., Sharon Presses Military Sweep

news.abstract: United Nations food convoy that was heavily damaged on Nov 10 during American airstrike in Afghanistan was unmarked and had not coordinated its travel with US-led coalition forces, according to investigation by Central Command; convoy was en route to city of Bamian and struck by two bombs that were dropped in effort to block Taliban and Al Qaeda forces; no United Nations employees were hurt in incident; two reports are also released on Afghan detainees who claimed they had been beaten while in custody, but report says injuries are consistent with force necessary to secure them (M)
news.title: Convoy Struck in November Found to Lack U.N. Markings

news.abstract: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, impoverished former Soviet republics of Central Asia, are undergoing surge of repression and corruption just as they are attracting new world attention as United States allies in its war on terrorism; authoritarian turn in region is problem for US, which relies on republics' support for military operations in Afghanistan; Bush administration has criticized human rights records of several governments but has been careful not to undermine them; several nations crack down harder than usual on political opponents, even as World Economic Forum's Eurasian Summit attracts hundreds of Western business executives and government officials to Kazakhstan (M)
news.title: Spotlight on Central Asia Is Finding Repression, Too

news.abstract: Thousands of Afghan refugees begin trek home across country's eastern border after poppy farmers, at government's behest, call off protest that had blocked refugees' passage; however, fighting at western border and confusing situation in east highlights tenuous hold that interim government headed by Hamid Karzai exerts over fractious and war-torn country; poppy farmers can earn much more by taking crops to market than government is willing to pay them to destroy harvest although there is confusion about amount government would pay; photo (M)
news.title: Afghan Refugees Allowed to Pass After Poppy Farmers End Protest

news.abstract: WEST BANK -- After a suicide bombing in Haifa that killed eight people, four of them soldiers, Ariel Sharon vowed that Israel would continue with its military sweep. He made the declaration to soldiers near Jenin, a day ahead of Colin L. Powell's arrival, asserting that the United States should not ''put any pressures upon us'' to withdraw.    Defense Minister Benjamin Ben-Eliezer said Israel would not interfere with Secretary Powell's plans to visit Yasir Arafat. ''As long as Powell wants to see Arafat he can see him,'' Mr. Ben-Eliezer said, adding, ''We are not preventing him to see Arafat.''
news.title: Fresh Attacks, And Sniper Fire

news.abstract: Egyptian students demonstrate, Alexandria, against Israel, United States support for Israel, and Egyptian government's violence against and arrest of protesters; crowd, fearful of police, begins to disperse within hours; photo (M)
news.title: Egyptians Protest Against Israel and U.S., but Fear Takes Edge Off Bravado

news.abstract: King Gyanendra of Nepal signs antiterrorist law passed by Parliament as security forces fight Maoist rebels trying to overthrow constitutional monarchy; king has eased state of emergency that had imposed restrictions on political parties and press (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Nepal: King Signs Antiterror Law

news.abstract: The Bush administration signaled that Colin L. Powell might cancel his meeting with Yasir Arafat unless he denounced terrorism.
news.title: White House Hints Powell May Cancel Meeting With Arafat

news.abstract: ISRAEL: Secretary of State Colin L. Powell arrived, planning a ''very long conversation'' with Prime Minister Ariel Sharon over his flouting of American demands for a prompt Israeli withdrawal from West Bank cities and towns.    WEST BANK: Israeli forces withdrew from several Palestinian villages but continued to occupy Ramallah, Bethlehem, Jenin and Nablus, and encircled Tulkarm and Qalqilya. Mr. Sharon gave no signs that he planned to lift the siege, citing men still wanted in the area.
news.title: An Arrival, But No Pullout
