news.abstract: Iranian-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon, in solidarity with Palestinians, attack Israeli positions in Golan Heights and Israeli soldiers respond, threatening to open second front; Israeli leaders warn Syria, main power broker in Lebanon, that they hold it responsible for renewed hostilities and that harsh retaliation is possible in Lebanon if attacks continue; residents of Kiryat Shmona, on Israel's northern border, have frayed nerves after two years of calm since withdrawal from Lebanon (M)
news.title: Day by Day, Arab Shells Fray Nerves In the Golan

news.abstract: Detailed portrait of life inside Church of Nativity compound after nine days of Israeli siege emerges in telephone interviews from inside complex with three people: Father Parthenios, Greek Orthodox monk, Rev Amjad Sabbara, pastor of Roman Catholic church in complex and Muhammad al-Madani, Palestinian governor of Bethlehem who is hiding in church; all three men deny that 40 priests and monks and 5 nuns in complex are being held hostage by Palestinian fighters holed up with them, as Israel contends; they warn that food is in very short supply and will not last another day or two; say explosions and gunfire regularly surround church; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Clerics Tell Of Ritual And Danger Under Siege

news.abstract: TOKYO—  For all intents and purposes, Tokyo is an ever-changing theme park whose operating motto is: Scrap and Rebuild. From office building monstrosities to shops, clubs and restaurants, nothing lasts very long before it is torn down to give way to something new.
news.title: The hippest hangouts in Tokyo

news.abstract: Specialist Lillie Morgan, United States Army finance clerk who drowned her small children last September in what she says was attempt to avenge her husband's suspected unfaithfulness, is sentenced by military court to life in prison, Mannheim, Germany (S)
news.title: Soldier Gets Life Sentence For Drowning Her 2 Children

news.abstract: Bush administration finds itself confronted by defiant Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon and by quandary of whether to meet Yasir Arafat just as Arafat's allies claim responsibility for another suicide bombing; in short, eight days into his first real involvement in Mideast conflict, Pres Bush seems bogged down in morass he has tried to avoid for 15 months; photos (News Analysis) (M)
news.title: A Late Entry Quickly Hits Mideast Wall

news.abstract: Miodrag Kovac, Yugoslavia's minister for laor, health and social policy, is found hanged by his own belt in bathroom of Madrid hotel hours after addressing United Nations Assembly on Aging; Kovac reportedly was upset over press criticism; recent reports in Montenegro accused him of financial wrongdoing (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Yugoslavia: Official Found Dead

news.abstract: gang attacks jwes on spor
news.title: Gang Attacks Jews on Sports Field in France

news.abstract: Faisalabad, industrial city deep in interior of Pakistan, has not been high on list of places considered hideouts for Al Qaeda terrorists, until FBI agents and Pakistani police raided house on outskirts and arrested some twenty Arab and other captives, including Abu Zubaydah, highest-ranking Al Qaeda figure captured since Sept 11 attacks; US has confirmed that Zubaydah was seriously injured in shootout, but said little else; Faisalabad does not have turbulent reputation of Pakistani cities that are factories of Islamic extremism; accounts of men who rented home reviewed; photo; map (M)
news.title: In Pakistan's Interior, A Troubling Victory In Hunt for Al Qaeda

news.abstract: Military analysis says Israeli operation in West Bank is sweeping counterinsurgency campaign that, given enough time, could reduce though not end Palestinian terrorist attacks; Israeli troops combing towns and refugee camps have arrested or killed militants terrorist suspects, seized hundreds of weapons, uncovered dozens of bomb-making factories and retrieved explosive belts devised for bombers; all-out conflict with Arabs is considered unlikely: Israel's military, though outnumbered, is qualitatively far superior; photo; map; comparison table (M)
news.title: Limits of Force: Superior Israeli Firepower Isn't Likely to End Terror

news.abstract: Death toll from truck explosion outside ancient synagogue in Djerba, Tunisia, rises to 13, including eight German tourists; authorities agree to allow German officials to join probe of whether incident was accident, and express support for Tunisia's Jewish population (S)
news.title: Toll in Tunisia Blast Rises

news.abstract: Sec Colin Powell says he will meet with Yasir Arafat, after Palestinian leader issues statement condemning terrorist acts against civilians and 'especially' suicide bombing that killed six people in Jerusalem; Arafat's statement, demanded by White House as condition for Powell meeting, also rails at length against Israel; Powell to see Arafat in Ramallah compound where he has been sealed up with about 100 other people by Israeli troops; suicide bomber, identified as Andaleeb Taqtaqah, blew herself up outside Mahane Yehuda market in Jerusalem; photos (M)
news.title: Arafat Condemns Terror; Powell Meeting On

news.abstract: Recent television blackout imposed by Thai government is latest evidence of dwindling hopes for more open press in Southeast Asia, where governments show little patience with press freedom; Malaysia, which has repeatedly hamstrung newspapers, and Bangladesh have banned certain Western magazines with unflattering articles; Indonesia, by contrast, is said to suffer from too much press of inferior quality; about 600 newspapers, many of them tabloid retailers of rumor and innuendo, have opened since fall of Pres Suharto (M)
news.title: Southeast Asia's Press Is Under Pressure

news.abstract: Crude oil prices expected to surge when trading begins on commodity markets on April 15 after weekend lull; oil markets confront possibility of continuing political instability in Venezuela after whiplash turn of events that brought Pres Hugo Chavez back to power following coup on April 11 (S)
news.title: Nervous Markets Fear Surge in the Price of Oil

news.abstract: Osama bin Laden, his deputy and a man believed to have been one of the Sept. 11 hijackers appear on a videotape that has just surfaced.
news.title: Bin Laden Makes Appearance on New Video

news.abstract: Conditions in and around devastated Ramallah headquarters of Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat described; siege has left Arafat and few dozen aides, sympathizers and international peace protestors virtually isolated in few rooms--often without electricity, water or working plumbing; photo (M)
news.title: Inside a Siege, Signs of Life and Loss

news.abstract: Sec of State Colin L Powell meets with Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat in largely destroyed headquarters in Ramallah, Arafat's first meeting with top American official since Israel declared him irrelevant months ago; Arafat tells Powell no cease-fire is possible until Israel ends military operation in West Bank and withdraws from cities and towns it rcently occupied; Powell reportedly delivers blunt message, warning Arafat of need to make changes in interests of peace; later meets with Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon, who proposes international summit on Middle East along lines of 1991 Madrid conference but without participation of Arafat; presses Pres Bush's request for full Israeli withdrawal; photos; map (M)
news.title: No Cease-Fire Until Withdrawal, Arafat Tells Powell

news.abstract: Amnesty International issues harsh evaluation of American policy, accusing US of violating several international laws in treatment of prisoners captured during war in Afghanistan and of failing to live up to its assertions that it is complying with Geneva Convention (M)
news.title: U.S. Treatment of War Captives Is Criticized

news.abstract: Afghans embark on complicated and lengthy process of choosing new leaders, nearly five months after Taliban forces were swept from power; every village in land will be consulted; will put forward one or more representatives to go forward to regional gatherings, which will select 1,500 people to attend loya jirga, or grand council, in Kabul from June 10 through 16; council will formally be convened by former King Mohammed Zahir Shah, set to return to Kabul within days after 29 years in exile (M)
news.title: In Afghan Villages, Elders Begin an Ancient Process to Choose a National Government

news.abstract: Europe RUSSIA: Abuses In Chechnya Cited; YUGOSLAVIA: Progress In Extradition Talks ; BRUSSELS: Nato And Russia Discuss Pact Nato'.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Americas PARAGUAY: Ex-president Convicted Of Corruption; BRAZIL: Candidate Switches Races.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Israeli forces arrest Marwan Barghouti, leader of Yasir Arafat's Fatah movement in biggest catch of its West Bank military offensive; he is accused of planning and financing terrorist attacks while masquerading as politician without military role; Prime Min Ariel Sharon says capture is evidence of value of Israeli mission; says Israel will try Barghouti, who is brought to Jerusalem for questioning; Palestinians insist Barghouti is not military man; warn arrest is likely to provoke more violence; arrest deprives Arafat of trusted lieutenant while further complicating Sec of State Colin Powell's effort to arrange truce after more than 18 months of fighting; arc of Barghouti's career--from Israeli prisoner, to peace advocate, to supporter of conflict to Israeli prisoner again--discussed; once popular with Israeli officials, he is now simply regarded as terrorist; Sharon announces Israeli forces will withdraw within week from Nablus and Jenin, two West Bank cities where fighting has been fiercest, but again defies American demands that Israeli military operation end; says military will remain in Bethlehem and Ramallah until it suceeds in capturing or exiling wanted men trapped in each city; speaks with Pres Bush by telephone; tells him plans for withdrawal from Nablus and Jenin; photos (M)
news.title: ISRAELIS CAPTURE AN ARAFAT DEPUTY IN THE WEST BANK

news.abstract: As Secretary of State Colin L. Powell prepared to end his peace mission, Ariel Sharon made clear that the Israeli dragnet through the West Bank was not over.
news.title: Israel Pursues Military Actions as Powell Prepares to Leave

news.abstract: Banks and state-owned companies in India are closed by one-day strike by estimated 10 million workers protesting sale of government companies and changing laws to make layoffs easier (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: One-Day National Strike

news.abstract: Sec Colin Powell, canny veteran of Washington's bureaucratic battles, concludes Mideast peace venture with comments making clear point that he may be Bush administration's front-line negotiator, but he is far from free-lancer, as some administration snipers back home would imply; photo; Powell's personal approach is unwaveringly calm, upbeat, low-key, good-humored, and unrevealing; Israeli and Palestinian negotiators agree he listens and talks candidly and patiently (M)
news.title: Powell Style: Keep Temperature Down

news.abstract: People living near US air base in western suburb of Tokyo lose final appeal in noise pollution case against US government (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: Neighbors Of U.S. Base Lose Suit

news.abstract: Australian court rules that British American Tobacco did in fact carry out systematic worldwide program of destroying papers that documented health risks of smoking; ruling, first after years of unproven allegations, finds that shredding began in 1985, supervised by then-counsel, at time when American subsidiary faced increasing number of lawsuits; implications for US cases discusssed (M)
news.title: Shredding of Smoking Data Is Ruled Deliberate

news.abstract: Jihad Abdul Rahman, 16, escapes from Church of Nativity in Bethlehem, where some 250 Palestinian gunmen are holed up surrounded by Israeli forces, and tells of meager rations, cold, smell of rotting bodies and gangrenous wounds, and Israeli loudspeakers blaring through sleepless nights; Bethlehem governor Muhammad Madani, inside church, says Yasir Arafat has instructed him to form committee to meet with Israelis; he and monks reached by telephone deny they are held hostage by gunmen; Israelis evacuate two of wounded (M)
news.title: Escapee, 16, Tells of Stench, Cold and Sleepless Nights in Besieged Church

news.abstract: Secretary of State Colin Powell leaves Israel without cease-fire he came for; says no truce could take hold until Israel withdraws from Palestinian-controlled cities and towns its forces have seized; antagonists seem angrier and more fearful of each other, and with less ground for hope that even high-level American intervention could force halt to violence by either side; Powell ends his six-day trip with harsh words for Israel and for Palestinians and their leader Yasir Arafat; some Israeli officials express satisfaction with his trip, saying he helped calm fighting along Israel's northern border; Palestinian officials bitterly assess his mission as failure, blaming Prime Min Ariel Sharon; Arab nations express frustration that US has not put more pressure on Sharon; Pres Hosni Mubarak of Egypt, one of few Arab nations that have been allied with US, cancels meeting with Powell during stopover in Cairo, sending his foreign minister instead; photo (M)
news.title: POWELL ENDS TRIP; SEES NO CEASE-FIRE BEFORE A PULLOUT

news.abstract: Analysis: apparent failure of Secretary of State Colin Powell's mission to Mideast has now pushed American diplomacy into region's most intractable conflict to point where political costs at home are rising and diplomatic costs with Arab world are steep, and where even global antiterror campaign could be in jeopardy; photo (M)
news.title: A Rising Toll for Bush: No Peace, More Blame

news.abstract: Iranian state radio reports execution of Saeed Hanai, who was convicted of strangling 16 women in city of Mashad over two years (M)
news.title: Iran Executes Worker Who Strangled 16 Women Over 2 Years

news.abstract: United Nations moves 905 ethnic minority Vietnamese refugees from two camps just inside Cambodia to Phnom Penh in preparation for their resettlement in United States; Cambodia plans to close camps and seal borders to new asylum seekers, hill tribe members formerly known as Montagnards, who have been fleeing violent land disputes and government crackdown on their unauthorized Protestant Christian groups (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Cambodia: Vietnamese Refugees Leave Camps

news.abstract: President Bush on Wednesday embraced a major American role in rebuilding Afghanistan, calling for an effort he compared to the Marshall Plan.
news.title: Bush Sets Role for U.S. in Afghan Rebuilding

news.abstract: Special Supreme Court tribunal in Athens defers ruling on whether it has jurisdiction to try class-action suit by about 60,000 Greeks demanding compensation from Germany for Nazi atrocities in more than 60 Greek villages between 1941 and 1944 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Greece: Nazi-Era Case Postponed

news.abstract: Grek authorities report arrest of three Turks for smuggling boatload of illegal immigrants seeking to reach Greece, then abandoning wooden fishing boat when it capsized in stormy seas off Naxos; two passengers drowned and more are feared dead (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Greece: 3 Held For Smuggling Migrants

news.abstract: American fighter pilot mistakenly drops 500-pound bomb on group of Canadian soldiers conducting training mission in southern Afghanistan, killing four and wounding eight; Pentagon says accident occurred after pilots of two F-16's saw muzzle flashes on ground below and thought they were under attack; it is not clear whether pilots were given permission to attack or independently dropped bomb in what they believed was self-defense; Canadian military officials say training area is well known to American forces; Pres Bush calls Prime Min Jean Chretien of Canada to express condolences and to pledge full investigation of incident with Canadians; central issue for investigators will be whether pilots of F-16 team sought permission from air controllers to attack (M)
news.title: U.S. Error Kills 4 Canadians in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Jean-Marie Le Pen, 73, is running for president of France for fifth time; victory is not considered within his grasp, but he is crowing with triumph that steadily rising crime and recent wave of anti-Semitic attacks by French Arab youths have mainstream politicians echoing his law-and-order positions and more voters agreeing with his anti-immigrant views; he has tempered some positions, but he still wants 'native French' given priority for jobs and welfare, and he has called for revival of capital punishment and for France to quit European Union; in this election, with so little enthusiasm for front-runners Prime Min Lionel Jospin and Pres Jacques Chirac, anything better than 10 percent could put Le Pen in powerful position in May 5 runoff; photo (M)
news.title: French Never-Say-Die Rightist Grasps at Top Spot a 5th Time

news.abstract: Israelis in Beit El in West Bank are defiant about expanding their settlement, even after Secretary of State Colin L Powell urges reconsideration of settlers' presence in Gaza Strip and West Bank; since Jewish settlers moved onto hill in 1970's, Beit El and nearby Arab neighborhoods have become places of striking contrasts; settlement resembles middle-class American suburb, while Arab zone is comprised of grim neighborhods connected by dirt roads; settlers note that land was barren before they built settlement; policy of Israel's current Government is to refrain from building new settlements while allowing current settlements to grow naturally; Beit El's settlers plan construction as they see fit; photos; map (M)
news.title: Now on the Spot, Builders Of Beit El Vow to Continue

news.abstract: 340 US Navy engineers and Marine Corps guardsare in Philippines to build roads and landing pads and dig wells for Filipino and US troops fighting Abu Sayyaf guerrillas on Basilan island (S)
news.title: U.S. Sends More Troops To Philippines In Rebel Fight

news.abstract: A leader of Al Qaeda now in American custody has told interrogators that terrorists had discussed plans for striking financial institutions in the United States.
news.title: Qaeda Leader in U.S. Custody Provokes Alert

news.abstract: Article reviews two days in which Venezuelan Pres Hugo Chavez was ousted by business and military leaders, and then restored when pro-Chavez crowds demand return and uprising collapses; photos; chronology (M)
news.title: Venezuela's 2 Fateful Days: Leader Is Out, and In Again

news.abstract: New German law sets three-year jail terms for political party officials who try to hide illegal donations (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Getting Tougher On Donations

news.abstract: Truncheon-wielding police officers in Belarus violently break up downtown march protesting living conditions and inadequate salaries; at least 40 demonstrators remain in jail; demonstrators' target is government of Pres Aleksandr Lukashenko, whose Communist-style government controls most aspects of country's laggard economy and permits only limited political opposition; Lukashenko has long been ostracized by most Western governments because of his government's human rights record; two leading political opponents have vanished in recent years(M)
news.title: Police in Belarus Detain 40 As a Protest Ends Violently

news.abstract: Anger and disillusionment in eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt is strong, 12 years after unification of Germany; about 20 percent of adults are jobless, and at least as many others have already moved to west; Communist-era factories have been shut down or reduced to tenth of their original size; disillusionment is expected to produce serious political consequences in upcoming state elections; biggest loser is expected to be Chancellor Gerhard Schroder's Social Democratic Party; biggest winners are likely to be successor to East Germany's Communist Party and center-right Christian Democratic Union; photos (M)
news.title: Germany Hears From Bitter Eastern Voters

news.abstract: British military officials in Kabul warn that Mohammad Zahir Shah, former Afghan king who returned from exile, is under threat of assassination from killers posing as journalists; spokesman for Afghan government says government is aware of several such conspiracies, which he says is work of remaining Taliban and Al Qaeda fighters as well as other 'radical groups'; Afghan officials say they are confident they could protect former king; photo (M)
news.title: British Warn of Plot to Assassinate Former Afghan King

news.abstract: Park Geun Hye, South Korean congresswoman and daughter of late Pres Park Chung Hee, will announce formation of her own political party, with goal of winning presidency herself; her candidacy could split conservative votes, virtually guaranteeing election of Roh Moo Hyun, former human rights lawyer, whom Park dismisses as 'radical'; with voting still eight months away, many analysts are keeping their options open; photos (M)
news.title: Ex-Korean Chief's Daughter Rides Nostalgia Wave

news.abstract: State Dept official William J Burns visits devastated Jenin refugee camp in West Bank and describes what he sees as 'terrible human tragedy'; camp's extensive destruction by Israeli forces has become focus of severe international criticism; Burns speaks of suffering of thousands of innocent Palestinian civilians; he does not criticize Israel, but he also makes no reference to Israel's argument that destruction in Jenin is result of fierce battle in which 23 Israeli soldiers were killed (M)
news.title: U.S. Official at Jenin Sees 'Terrible Human Tragedy'

news.abstract: Europeans of widely varying political persuasions today deplored the rise of Jean Le Pen and the National Front in France.
news.title: Europeans Speak Out Against Rise of Le Pen

news.abstract: Chancellor Gerhard Schroder's governing Social Democrats fall to third place in state elections in eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, delivering jolt to Schroder's political fortunes; this is last major test of voter sentiment before national elections set for Sept 22; it appears to be resounding win for opposition Christian Democrats, with former Communists coming in second; some political commentators note that election focused on local issues, making it difficult to project result as sign of national discontent with ruling Social Democrats (M)
news.title: Conservatives Surge in German State Elections

news.abstract: Article compares and contrasts leadership styles of Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel and Palestian leader Yasir Arafat (M)
news.title: MIDEAST TURMOIL: The Leaders; Personalities, Politics and Style

news.abstract: Israeli forces withdraw to edges of Nablus, and Palestinian fighters there return to streets, slapping posters on walls to celebrate their dead and vowing even fiercer struggle against Israel; this suggests that Israel may find it impossible to sustain its inroads, nor did it negate Palestinians' ability to fight back another day (M)
news.title: MIDEAST TURMOIL: The Battle; A Different Fight, A Different Victory

news.abstract: Analysis: extreme right's strong showing in first round of French presidential election confirms rising law-and-order and anti-immigration sentiments in region and exposes electorate's deep disenchantment with France's tightly knit political elite; recent elections elsewhere in Western Europe have already signaled general turn to right, mirroring traditional pendulum swings of European politics; what analysts are alarmed about is recent shift of extreme rightist parties from periphery to center of political debate; photo (M)
news.title: Domino Effect? New Gain For Far Right in Europe

news.abstract: Parts of Ahmedabad in India's western state of Gujarat are under curfew after renewed Hindu-Muslim violence (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: More Hindu-Muslim Violence

news.abstract: Supreme Court of Pakistan begins hearing petitions by major political parties and Islamic religious groups challenging constitutionality of referendum called for Apr 30 by Pres Pervez Musharraf in move to extend his unelected presidency for five more years (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Pakistan: Challenge To The President

news.title: Argentina's President Suffers Double Blow

news.abstract: Tunisian officials, initially reluctant to tie the blast to Islamic militants, now say that the act was planned and orchestrated by a man with suspected links to several cells.
news.title: Explosion at Synagogue Tied to Jihad; Arrest Made

news.abstract: Kinshasha Journal on mass military trial of 135 suspects that has so far shed no light on who was behind murder of Laurent D Kabila, former president who was gunned down in his palace last year; photos; map (M)
news.title: Kinshasa Journal; Suspects by the Score and, Oh, Such Digressions!

news.abstract: Air Force Brig Gen Stephen T Sargeant and Canadian Brig Gen Marc Dumais will lead inquiry into why Air National Guard F-16 pilot who thought he was under attack mistakenly bombed Canadian troops in Afghanistan last week, killing four of them and wounding eight others (S)
news.title: Investigators Named In Canadian Deaths

news.abstract: Crown Prince Abdullah is expected to tell Pres Bush that strategic relationship between Saudi Arabia and US will be threatened if Bush does not moderate his support for Israel's military policies; two will meet on Apr 25; Saudi family has reportedly discussed using 'oil weapon' against US, or demanding that US leave strategic military bases in region; there is also warning of general drift by Arab leaders toward radical politics that have been building in Arab street; Saudi message contains undeniable brinkmanship intended to put pressure on Bush to take much larger political gamble by imposing peace settlement on Israelis and Palestinians; Abdullah is thought to represent not just Saudi Arabia but also broader voice of Arab world; his delegation's strong sense of alarm and crisis are being heard in other Arab capitals; Abdullah believes Bush has lost credibility by failing to follow through on his demand two weeks ago that Prime Min Ariel Sharon withdraw Israeli troops from West Bank and end sieges of Yasir Arafat's compound in Ramallah and of Church of Nativity in Bethlehem (M)
news.title: Saudi to Warn Bush of Rupture Over Israel Policy

news.abstract: Brig. Gen. Stephen T. Sargeant of the Air Force and Brig. Gen. Marc Dumais of Canada will lead an inquiry into why an Air National Guard pilot mistakenly bombed Canadian troops in Afghanistan last week.
news.title: Investigators Named in Canadian Deaths

news.abstract: Remarks made by President Bush following his meeting with Crown Prince Abdullah of Saudi Arabia on Thursday, as provided by the White House.
news.title: Press Conference Following President's Meeting With Saudi Crown Prince

news.abstract: Israel on Wednesday seemed to retreat from the combative stance it had assumed against a United Nations team set to examine what happened at Jenin Refugee Camp.
news.title: Israel Eases Opposition to Inquiry Into Jenin Attack

news.abstract: North Korea's defense minister, Vice Marshal Kim Il Choi, harshly denounces United States in televised speech, with North Korean leader Kim Jong Il standing by; says North Korean soldiers would respond 'mercilessly' if US encroaches on North Korean land even 'one-thousandth of a millimeter' (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: North Korea: Harsh Warning To U.S.

news.abstract: Pres Olusegun Obasanjo of Nigeria says he will seek second term next year; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Nigeria: Obasanjo To Seek Second Term

news.abstract: United Nations World Food Program reports that southern Africa's worst food shortage in decade is spreading and more than five million people across region may now need help; agency is already feeding 2.6 million people, and millions more are thought to be falling deeper into hunger; Malawi, hardest hit, has declared state of disaster; Zambia and Zimbabwe are in dire trouble also, and Mozambique and Swaziland will be hard pressed to avoid similar shortages; UN agency says 145,000 tons of food, worth $69 million, is needed in coming months, but that only $3 million worth of food has been pledged so far; erratic weather for last few years laid foundations for current crisis (M)
news.title: Hunger in Southern Africa Imperils Lives of Millions

news.abstract: Russia's Federal Security Service says it killed Arab-born Chechen field commander known as Khattab, suspected of links to Al Qaeda, in operation in mid-March; past reports of Khattab's death have proved false; he is accused of torturing and executing Russian prisoners (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Top Chechen Reported Killed

news.abstract: Crown Prince Abdullah of Saudi Arabia tells Pres Bush bluntly that United States must temper its support for Israel or face grave consequences throughout Arab world; Saudi officials at meeting at president's ranch in Texas say Abdullah warned that US would continue to lose credibility in Middle East and create more instability there unless it did more to stop Israel's incursions into Palestinian areas; Adel al-Jubeir, Abdullah's foreign policy adviser, says Prime Min Ariel Sharon wants to drag region 'over a cliff'; American officials offer far more positive account of meetings; Pres Bush says he and crown prince formed 'strong personal bond'; both Bush and Jubeir say crown prince did not threaten in any way to reduce Saudi oil exports to US; Bush, who infuriated Arab world week ago by calling Sharon 'a man of peace,' says he told Abdullah he is counting on Israel to withdraw forces from Palestinian areas, including resolving standoffs in Ramallah and Bethlehem; photo (M)
news.title: SAUDI TELLS BUSH U.S. MUST TEMPER BACKING OF ISRAEL

news.abstract: South Korea Pres Kim Dae Jung apologizes for scandals surrounding his sons and former aides; apology comes on eve of convention to nominate presidential candidate; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: An Apology From The President

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  CORRECTION PUBLISHED IN THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE DATED Saturday, May 25, 2002:
news.title: Overseas Americans : 4 associations to lobby for rights in Washington

news.abstract: PARIS—  An earthquake strikes. A government collapses. A terrorist threat emerges. Relatives try to inform you that a family member is dying. Or you just lose your passport.
news.title: Security precautions : Should you let your government know where you are?

news.abstract: Philippine and American officials say Abu Sayyaf, Muslim extremist group that is holding two Americans hostage in southern Philippines, refuses to hand them over after being paid $300,000 ransom, and has demanded another $200,000; original ransom money was raised and paid by families of hostages, Martin and Gracia Burnham, with acquiescence of Bush administration; Philippine soldiers and American Special Forces are conducting exercises on island of Basilan, where Burnhams are last known to be held, and Philippine officials now say that military activity may have impeded Burnhams' release (M)
news.title: Given $300,000, Abductors Refuse to Free 2 Americans

news.abstract: Regarding "Coping in a strange, new world" (Feb. 16-17):
news.title: Language barriers in Lebanon : Letters to the editor

news.abstract: Pakistaan's Supreme Courtrules upcoming April 30 referendum to extend presidency of Pervez Musharraf is constitutional and can proceed as planned; unanimously rejects three petitions from opposition parties and lawyers' association; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistani Court Backs President On Effort to Extend His Term

news.abstract: Estimated 100,000 demonstrators steam through streets of Paris and other French cities in further protest against strong showing of far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen in first round of presidential balloting; demonstrations draw impromptu alliance of human rights groups and antiracism, student and labor organizations opposed to Le Pen and his anti-immigrant policies and proposals for mass deportations of foreigners without legal residence in France (S)
news.title: At Least 100,000 in France Protest Far Rightist

news.abstract: Doubts arise in Pakistan over commitment of Pres Pervez Musharraf to follow through on pledge made three months ago to crack down on violent Muslim groups and on religious schools that breed them; of nearly 2,000 people arrested in sweep of Islamic radicals, as many as 70 percent have been set free; after five militant groups were banned, members reorganized under new names; reform of religious academies has met with strong resistance, and schools continue to operate much as they always have; while Musharraf has not backed away from major policy reversal of choosing to support US in war against terrorism, direction of his policies are not so clear on most sensitive and entrenched domestic issues; photo (M)
news.title: Musharraf Treading Gently Against Pakistani Militants

news.abstract: Germans struggle to comprehend murderous shooting rampage by 19-year-old Robert Steinhauser, which left 18 students and teachers and himself dead and 10 others wounded at high school in Erfurt, since country has some of toughest gun restrictions in world; police report Steinhauser acquired weapons entirely legally as member of officially accredited sport shooting club; incident underscores that such violence is more feasible than Germans have assumed; Steinhauser was expelled from school earlier in year for forging doctors letters with which he had hoped to delay meeting graduation requirements; photo (M)
news.title: Deep Shock In Germany, Where Guns Are Rare

news.abstract: Group of British tourists pursuing hobby of plane-spotting, peculiarly favorite pasttime in Britain, are convicted in Greek court in Kalamata of obtaining national secrets; eight defendants are sentenced to three years in jail and six others to one-year suspended sentences; reactions in Britain range from incredulity to outrage; member of Parliament decries case as farce; defendants were arrested in November at military air base air show to which they were invited; were originally charged with more serious crime of espionage, which carries 20-year sentence; Greece bans photography of military installations (M)
news.title: Plane-Spotters Found Guilty In Greek Court In Secrets Case

news.abstract: Many Russians are recapturing Lenten traditions, after 70 years in which Bolsheviks destroyed thousands of churches killing or persecuting millions of believers and after decade of wild-east capitalism and noveau-riche flamboyance; even though government officials and private citizens are reverting to fasting and to Lenten diets of meatless and dairy-free meals, ascetic impulse often collides with epicurean and regimen is not always strict; photos (M)
news.title: Moscow Journal; Feast or Fast? Russians Just Can't Give Up Lent

news.abstract: News analysis; Pres Bush's winning of Israeli agreement to end siege of Yasir Arafat's compound in Ramallah may be important step to shore up American credibility with Arab world by repositioning American foreign policy in Middle East, but volatile crisis is far from over and he faces even more difficult challenge of getting warring parties back to negotiating table where expectations for American pressure remain high on both sides; photo (M)
news.title: The Hurdles And the Goal

news.abstract: North Korea welcomes group of visitors from South Korea, whose families were divided by Korean War, but also calls for resignation of South Korea's Foreign Minister Choi Sung Hong for backing Pres Bush's tough stance toward North Korea, which Bush contends is part of 'axis of evil' (M)
news.title: More Reunions Unite Koreans, But Politics Still Intrude

news.abstract: Excerpts from remarks by Pres Bush regarding Israel's acceptance of compromise to end siege of compound of Yasir Arafat in Ramallah on West Bank (S)
news.title: In Bush's Words: Arafat Must 'Thwart' Terrorism

news.abstract: Thousands of Afghan refugees are returning home from Pakistan, where they fled at onset of Soviet invasion in 1979; more than 300,000 have migrated home in two months since UN refugee agency began assisting repatriation; refugee officials believe as many as 1.2 million could also return from Pakistan and Iran; say it could take three years, perhaps longer, before estimated 5 to 6 million in neighboring countries return; those returning home seem to be ingoring naysayers who worry about risk of anarchy if new government in Kabul fails to rein in warlords who currently control much of country, or if Taliban and Al Qaeda regroup for new guerrilla war; map; photos (L)
news.title: Ignoring Risk, Afghan Refugees Rush Home

news.abstract: Argentina passes first day without turmoil on April 29 following swearing-in of new Economy Minister Roberto Lavagna on April 27; banks and stock market are open; pesos are again exchanged legally for dollars; Lavagna persuades Pres Eduardo Duhalde to allow currency to continue floating against dollar and to abandon, at least for moment, plan for fixed exchange rate that analysts warn cannot be maintained (M)
news.title: Back in Business, Argentina Calms Down and the Peso Perks Up

news.abstract: Article on Masonic Supreme Council, largest of Cuba's fraternal organizations whose membership has more than doubled since 1980's to more than 29,000 members after long period of distrust following Communist revolution in 1959, when Masons were seen as threat and treated as clandestine counter-revolutionary sect; government's current official policy links Masons to some of nobler moments of Cuba's past, even though Masons complain privately of infiltration by agents and of veiled warnings about meetings with foreigners, including American diplomats; Jesus Armada Pena, council's sovereign grand commander, comments; photo (M)
news.title: Havana Journal; Masonic Rites, No Less. In Castro's Bailiwick!

news.abstract: President Pervez Musharraf, who seized power in a nonviolent coup in 1999, sought to continue his leadership today in a popular referendum.
news.title: Pakistanis Vote on Extending Musharraf's Term

news.abstract: Young Japanese in quiet technology-driven change are developing hyperagile thumbs, fruit of childhoods spent furiously thumbing hand-held computer games and young adulthoods thumbing out e-mail messages on cellphone key pads; study of cellphone habits of people in eight major world cities finds Japan's 'thumb generation' is most advanced in world; photos (M)
news.title: Youth Let Their Thumbs Do the Talking in Japan

news.abstract: Increasingly likely prospects that Britain and Spain may agree to joint sovereignty over Gibraltar, solidly British since Spanish crown lost it in 1704, fans outrage and deep anxiety among Rock's 30,000 residents, who harbor deep mistrust of Spain; map; photo (M)
news.title: Gibraltar Residents Fight for Identity

news.abstract: Military officials say force of fewer than 1,000 allied troops under United States command sweeping Afghanistan's border with Pakistan has killed four suspected Taliban or Al Qaeda fighters in past two days; say force, working in and out of border area for over week in bid to keep fighters who escaped earlier into Pakistan from regrouping in Afghanistan, has found large arms caches, but few adversaries; force includes American, Australian, British and Afghan fighters; Pakistani intelligence official says major US-led military operation will probably begin in area around Khost in next day (M)
news.title: 4 Militants Die in Clashes With Allies Near Pakistan

news.abstract: British appeals court reverses lower court ruling and upholds government's decision to bar Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan from entering nation; cites his 'notorious opinions' and uneasy state of race and religious relations in Britain; he weighs appeal (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Farrakhan Barred

news.abstract: Vandals ransack London synagogue; attack startles nation that has been largely immune to anti-Jewish attacks (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: London Synagogue Attacked

news.abstract: India's Hindu nationalist-led government, after marathon debate in which it is harshly criticized by opponents and some allies, defeats motion to criticize it for failing to control Hindu mobs who have killed hundreds of Muslims in Gujarat state over past two months; motion is defeated, 276-182; Min George Fernandes holds violence is no different than sectarian riots that occured under Congress Party rule; Congress Party head Sonia Gandhi, often reticent, has forcefully criticized government on issue (S)
news.title: Hindu Party Wins in Critical Vote

news.abstract: Israel again blocks proposed fact-finding mission to probe Apr fighting at Jenin refugee camp, spurring United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan to weigh disbanding investigative team; Israeli officials say they fear biased probe that could possibly expose army to war-crimes trial; Prime Min Ariel Sharon invokes own service as soldier in declaring he will protect troops; holds Israel made extraordinary efforts not to harm innocent people; Palestinian officials charge cover-up; United States, in shift away from its aggressive backing of probe, says it can do nothing if Annan drops probe; US and British officials meet, Ramallah, to work out details for moving six wanted men from Yasir Arafat's beseiged compound into Palestinian prison under international guardianship; Israel withdraws its ground forces from Hebron (M)
news.title: U.N. May Drop Inquiry at Jenin As Israel Resists

news.abstract: Mexican Senate unanimously approves nation's first freedom of information law, requiring government to open records and files to public; law is seen as important step toward ending seven decades of government corruption and abuses shrouded by secrecy (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Freedom Of Information

news.abstract: Senior government officials in Afghanistan suspect that members of former Northern Alliance, which did most of fighting against Taliban, are unloading huge stores of bank notes they printed for themselves during their years in the wilderness; say when warlords of old Northern Alliance cash in their wads of cash for dollars, they get wealthy and country's currency, afghani, takes further plunge; recent collapse of Afghanistan's currency, and skulduggery surrounding it, stands as measure of weakness of country's fledgling government, which is unable to control even supply of its own money; Anwar Ahadi, governor general of central bank, points to murky relationship between what was Northern Alliance and Russian-Swiss company that for years held exclusive rights to print Afghan money; photo (M)
news.title: In Afghan War, Top Exiles Printed Themselves a Fortune

news.abstract: Laksamana Sukardi, close adviser to Pres Megawati Sukarnoputri of Indonesia, says United States should drop restrictions imposed three years ago on assistance to Indonesian military and help restore 'tarnished reputation' of his nation's army; since Sept 11 Washington has repeatedly pressed Indonesia to take firmer action against groups and individuals suspected of having ties to Osama bin Laden and his Al Qaeda terrorism network; Sukardi says this is impossible task if military remains discredited in eyes of public; Indonesian Government wants to resume military training in US for its officers; Sukardi stops short of advocating that US help supply military with weapons (M)
news.title: Indonesian Official Urges U.S. to Resume Military Assistance

news.abstract: Valery Ivanov, newspaper editor in Togliatti, Russia, is killed after publishing articles on corruption in local government and on ties between local criminal groups and auto producer Avtovaz, which is based in city; Ivanov was also general director of local television station whose previous two directors were killed (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Editor Shot To Death

news.abstract: Senior Bush administration official says FBI and CIA analysts have concluded there is no evidence that Mohamed Atta, suspected ringleader of Sept 11 attacks, met with Iraqi intelligence officer before hijackings; reports of meeting came from Czech officials like Prime Min Milos Zeman (S)
news.title: U.S. Drops Last Link of Iraq to 9/11

news.abstract: A Indian MIG-21 fighter jet caught fire today and crashed into a three story bank building in the northwestern city of Jalandhar. Seven people were killed and 14 wounded.
news.title: India Jet Hits Building and Kills 7

news.abstract: Americas MEXICO: More Chances For Women; BRAZIL: Cloners Didn't Use Sonogram.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Ida Milgrom, teacher, economist and musician who helped to lead international campaign to free her son, Soviet dissident Anatoly B. Shcharansky, from prison, dies at age 94; photo (M)
news.title: Ida Milgrom, 94, Dies; Helped Free a Son Held by Soviets

news.abstract: Racial attacks have been on rise in past five years against Moscow's ethnic minorities, in particular Africans, Asians and people from Caucasus; problem is slowly gaining national attention, prompting Pres Vladimir V Putin, in address to nation last month, to warn against rise of fascist groups; attacks often appear to be organized; ambassadors from 37 African countries have signed highly unusual joint appeal to Foreign Ministry asking for more protection after spate of attacks on their families and embassy workers; attackers are young, between ages of 14 and 20, and often those who feel cast adrift in economic collapse and social upheaval that followed fall of Soviet Union; like skinhead groups across Europe, these teenagers turn their anger on people of color; photos (M)
news.title: Moscow Journal; Where 'Living While Black' Means Living in Fear

news.abstract: List of legislators who voted 'No' or did not vote on resolutions of support for Israel in House and Senate (S)
news.title: 'No' Votes And Nonvoters

news.abstract: Israel and Palestinians express cautious support for peace conference announced by Bush administration, as Israeli soldiers launch raid into center of Nablus in which Israeli officer and two Palestinians are killed; in Bethlehem, Palestinian and Israeli negotiators remain deadlocked over siege at Church of the Nativity; much about conference remains unresolved, including its goals and topics of discussion; officials in Washington emphasize that it would be meeting of foreign ministers, not heads of state, in plan that seems intended to sidestep Prime Min Ariel Sharon's refusal to negotiate with Yasir Arafat because of Israel's belief that he sponsors terrorism; photos (M)
news.title: 3 Killed in Raid in Nablus; Peace Conference Idea Wins Initial Support on Both Sides

news.abstract: Barbara Anne Castle, former British Labor cabinet minister and determined socialist, dies at age of 91; photo (M)
news.title: Barbara Castle, British Radical, Is Dead at 91

news.abstract: Kosovo's leader, Ibrahim Rugova, testifies at war crimes trial of Slobodan Milosevic, who as leader of Serbia had Rugova arrested; Rugova, who had led campaign of peaceful resistance against Milosevic's rule in Kosovo, charges that serious war crimes were committed in Kosovo under Milosevic's leadership; Milosevic turns loud and aggressive as he cross-examines Rugova (M)
news.title: Kosovo Leader Confronts Old Foe, Milosevic, at War Crimes Tribunal

news.abstract: Sec of State Colin L Powell and Foreign Min Igor S Ivanov of Russia say they made substantial headway toward negotiating agreement on reducing nuclear weapons that could be signed by Pres Bush and Pres Putin at summit meeting in Russia on May 23; Powell and Ivanov acknowledge that differences remain, but tenor of their remarks leaves little doubt that there is growing optimism on both sides that pact could be hammered out in time for summit meeting (M)
news.title: U.S.-Russia Talks Inch Nuclear Deal Closer

news.abstract: Memorial service is held in Cape Town, South Africa, for Saartjie Baartman, young African woman who was lured to Europe in early 19th century with false promises of fame and fortune, but who died in Paris in 1816, penniless and friendless among people who derided her as circus freak; white scientists intent on proving inferiority of blacks dissected her and displayed her body parts in French museum; after years of wrangling between South Africa and France, her remains are removed from Musee de l'Homme in Paris and flown home; in South Africa, museum officials hope to arrange proper burials for skeletons of other Africans who were defiled in death in name of science; photos (M)
news.title: Mocked in Europe of Old, African Is Embraced at Home at Last

news.abstract: As many as 150 people may have drowned in sinking of double-decker ferry on Meghna River about 35 miles southeast of Dhaka, Bangladesh; 60 passengers are rescued; officials say 300 people may have been on board; photo (M)
news.title: Bangladesh Ferry Sinks in Storm And Scores Are Feared Drowned

news.abstract: Yevgeny Svetlanov, Russian conductor, dies at age 73; photo (M)
news.title: Yevgeny Svetlanov, Gifted Russian Conductor, Dies at 73

news.abstract: Intense American pressure to resolve monthlong standoff between Israelis and Palestinians at Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem causes breakthrough in new talks involving top aides to Yasir Arafat and American and European diplomats; breakthrough follows Arafat's order to Palestinians to give list of those hiding in church to American and European Union diplomats; Israeli officials say 25 wanted men and about 140 civilians are inside complex; have demanded list for weeks; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Is Pressing Hard for End to Church Siege

news.abstract: Left- and right-leaning French newspapers are virtually unanimous in running front-page editorials urging voters to reject far-right candidate, Jean-Marie Le Pen, and to give Pres Jacques Chirac landslide victory in May 5 runoff election for President (M)
news.title: On Eve of Vote, French Papers Rally Voters Against Rightist

news.abstract: Deputy Defense Sec Paul D Wolfowitz warns of dangerous gap between West and Islam, speech, World Affairs Council, Monterrey, Calif; calls for broad American initiative to strengthen ties with moderate Muslim nations and with 'tolerant' people of Muslim world (S)
news.title: Senior Pentagon Official Urges Links With Moderate Muslims

news.abstract: Bush administration officials said today that the court's prosecutors will not be given any information to help them bring cases against any individuals.
news.title: U.S. Says It Will Not Support International Criminal Court

news.abstract: Israeli officials intensify campaign to discredit Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, distributing three compilations of captured Palestinian documents to American officials in Jerusalem that Israelis contend are indisputable proof that he personally approved terror attacks; documents indicate Arafat approved payments to members of Fatah party who later carried out terror attacks, that his security service was aware that some Fatah members were engaging in terrorism and that militant groups Hamas and Islamic Jihad infiltrated parts of Palestinian security apparatus; do not appear to show definitively that Arafat ordered attacks (M)
news.title: Israelis Release More Documents Accusing Arafat of Terror

news.abstract: Sir Peter Shepeard, British architect, planner and landscape designer, dies at age 88; photos (M)
news.title: Sir Peter Shepheard, Architect And Landscape Designer, 88

news.abstract: Nepalese security forces report killing more than 400 Maoist rebels since May 2 in training camps hidden in remote areas, with deaths of only three soldiers; rout of rebels would be worst military blow yet to rebels in their six-year-long insurgency; rebel leader Pushpa Kamal Dahal calls for renewed peace negotiations; Prime Min Sher Bahadur Deuba, who engaged in three rounds of peace talks with Maoists in 2001, rejects overture; says government will not speak with rebels until they lay down arms and surrender (M)
news.title: Nepal Says Over 400 Rebels Are Dead After Several Battles

news.abstract: Pres Kim Dae Jung of South Korea resigns from Millennium Democratic Party in bid to insulate it from corruption allegations surrounding his children and several close aides; resignation follows arrest Kwon Ro Gap, close associate, on charges of bribery and stock manipulation; two of Kim's three sons also face summonses by prosecutors; are suspected of peddling influence in return for bribes (S)
news.title: Korean Leader Quits His Party Over Scandal

news.abstract: Bush administration accuses Cuba of producing small quantities of germs that can be used in biological warfare and says Libya and Syria are also violating international treaties by making unconventional weapons; Under Sec of State John R Bolton, in speech to Heritage Foundation, publicly alludes to conclusions by American intelligence agencies in recent months; Cuban Embassy spokesmen Luis Fernandez denies assertions; accuses administration of trying to extend concern over international terrorism to Cuba to justify hard-line policies at time when US farmers and allies that view Cuba as natural market are advocating loosening of four-decade trade embargo (M)
news.title: Washington Accuses Cuba Of Germ-Warfare Research

news.abstract: Man-in-the News biographical portrait of Jean-Pierre Raffarin, selected by Pres Jacques Chirac as France's new premier; photo (M)
news.title: Man in the News; A Leader to Lean On; Jean-Pierre Raffarin

news.abstract: Pim Fortuyn, maverick right-wing populist and leading candidate in upcoming national elections in Netherlands, is shot and killed by gunman in parking lot of radio station in town of Hilversun, where he had given interview; police arrest unidentified 33-year-old Dutch citizen, who reportedly confesses; murder deeply stuns nation that sees itself as peaceful and egalitarian; raises specter of violence stalking European politics; Prime Wim Kok condemns murder in deeply emotional speech to nation; calls it tragedy not only for nation, but for its democracy; Fortuyn's rise in Dutch politics discussed; former sociology professor wanted to become country's first gay prime minister; carried same strong anti-immigrant message that has propelled resurgent far right to political triumphs elsewhere in Europe; recently stunned Dutch political establishment by winning power in Rotterdam, country's second largest city; public opinion polls predicted he would win one-fifth of vote in May 15 elections, and that his group would have been crucial to formation of next government; map; photo (M)
news.title: Rightist Candidate in Netherlands Is Slain, and the Nation Is Stunned

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac moves quickly to capitalize on landslide re-election victory over rightist Jean-Marie Le Pen; selects center-right Prime Minister Jean-Pierre Raffarin to restore his conservative base and lead his party into legislative elections in June following resignation of Socialist Prime Min Lionel Jospin; move is seen recognition of anger of French voters at Paris-based government elite; Raffarin, affable and little-known former junior minister, is not member of Chirac's party but low-profile senator and head of regional council in western France; he is believed capable of bringing small entrepreneurs who voted for Le Pen back into conservative fold; map; photo (M)
news.title: Chirac's Pick: A Premier Friendly to Small Business

news.abstract: Agreement to end siege of Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem by Israeli forces and release 100 people inside is snagged on angry details; negotiators are deadlocked over how many of Palestinian gunmen inside church will be sent abroad, most likely to Italy, or whether exile will be permanent or temporary; photo (M)
news.title: Deal to End Church Siege Is Snagged on Angry Details

news.abstract: Australians' will to preserve their way of life drives popularity of rigid refugee policy introduced last year; photos; map (M)
news.title: Deep Fears Behind Australia's Immigration Policy

news.abstract: Asia MALAYSIA: A Muslim Leader Criticizes Muslims; North KOREA: Talks On Nuclear Program; BANGLADESH: Ferry Death Toll Passes 200; TAIWAN: Water Rationing For Capital.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Pres Bush asks Bill Clinton to lead US delegation at East Timor's independence celebrations, first time he has given former president role in administration (S)
news.title: Clinton to Represent Bush at Timor Event

news.abstract: Canadian troops and American criminal investigators in Afghanistan's Tora Bora mountains exhume 23 bodies they believe are remains of Al Qaeda fighters, perhaps Osama bin Laden security contingent killed in air strike Dec 15; DNA testing is done before reburial; bin Laden's remains are not found (M)
news.title: Allies Exhume 23 Bodies Thought to Be Qaeda Fighters

news.abstract: Thousands of people, from stolid Dutch burghers to African students and Turkish girls, stand in line for hours in Rotterdam to sign condolence books for murdered political leader Pim Fortuyn; photo (M)
news.title: In Rotterdam, Even a Politician's Foes Pay Respects

news.abstract: Warfare between army and Maoist guerrillas has intensified in last week in Maoist-controlled western Nepal, isolated, mountainous region; rebels, responding to army attack on major base hidden deep in forest, attack army and police post, Gam; Prime Min Sher Bahadur Deuba meets with State Sec Colin L Powell, Washington, seeking military aid; says $20 million proposed by Bush administration is inadequate (M)
news.title: Nepal Battle Intensifying After Attack On Rebels

news.abstract: Seven North Koreans try to barge into consulates in Shenyang, China, in bid for political asylum; two succeed in entering American Consulate and five are interecepted by Chinese guards at Japanese Consulate; 28 North Koreans have gained safe passage to South Korea by forcing their way into Western diplomatic compounds in Beijing in last two months, angering and frustrating Chinese Government; map (M)
news.title: North Koreans Seek Asylum At Consulates In China

news.abstract: London court sentences Declan Rafferty, Fintan O'Farrell and Michael MacDonald, members of renegade Real IRA, to 30 years in jail for trying to buy arms in Slovakia for their program of terror aimed at bringing down Northern Ireland peace plan (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Irish Guerrillas Sentenced

news.abstract: Mexico's federal election board has reopened probe into financing of Pres Vicente Fox's 2000 election campaign at request of two major opposition parties; opposition parties have charged, without hard evidence, that Fox illgeally got foreign contributions (S)
news.title: Mexico Reopens Inquiry

news.abstract: Pentagon and Bush administration officials say Central Intelligence Agency used missile fired from unmanned surveillance drone in unsuccessful bid to kill Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, Hezb-i-Islami militant leader who has vowed to topple Hamid Karzai's interim government in Afghanistan; attack is new tactic in war and shows Bush's determination to support Karzai; American officials cite evidence of Hekmatyar's efforts to bring down Karzai and strike at American and allied troops; Brig Roger Lane, who leads British task force in Afghanistan, says war is all but won against Al Qaeda and Taliban; says offensive operations will be over in matter of weeks, not months (M)
news.title: U.S. Attack On Warlord Aims to Help Interim Leader

news.abstract: Maoist rebel leader Pushpa Kamal Dahal proposes monthlong cease-fire in fighting in Nepal; Prime Min Sher Bahadur Deuba rejects plan, saying Maoists betrayed him last year when they broke off peace talks; Deuba is in United States seeking military aid to help crush insurgency (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Nepal: Rebels' Cease-Fire Rejected

news.abstract: Pres Chen Shui-bian of Taiwan makes unexpected peace overture to Beijing; proposes to send informal delegation from his ruling Democratic Progressive Party to China late this summer; Taiwan and China have had informal contacts for last 10 years, but Chen's party has tended to advocate more independence from China; as result it has had frostier relations with mainland than other Taiwanese political parties; Taipei and Beijing each officially advocate principle that there is one China encompassing both mainland and island of Taiwan, but large faction of Chen's party favors explicit announcement of independence from mainland; there is no immediate reaction from Beijing to Chen's proposal (M)
news.title: Taiwan's Leader Proposes a Delegation as an Overture to China

news.abstract: Asia NEPAL: Rebels' Cease-fire Rejected; South KOREA: Opposition Names Candidate.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: American support for Israel is driving grass-roots effort to punish America by boycotting its consumer products throughout Arab world; word is being spread via Internet, mosque sermons, fliers and even mobile phone messages; purchases of American goods generated by 300 million Arabs form very small part of American exports, but long boycott could retard spread of franchises and other products; boycotts are largely effort of individuals and small groups without government involvement; they reflect growing sentiment that Arabs should distance themselves from United States, and they want their governments to do likewise; photos (M)
news.title: An Anti-American Boycott Is Growing in the Arab World

news.abstract: Salah Ajarma's return home after 39 days in the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem was a bittersweet affair.
news.title: A Bittersweet Homecoming

news.abstract: Nong Duc Manh, head of Vietnam's Communist Party, says says democracy may be getting out of hand; calls for curb on public protests at government buildings; says people should confine complaints to proper government channels; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Vietnam: Too Much Democracy

news.abstract: Uganda's Parliament approves bill easing curbs on political parties; some lawmakers walk out, holding changes do not do enough to end one-party rule; new law lets parties operate but bars them from holding meetings or canvassing for support outside capital (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Uganda: Political Restrictions Eased

news.abstract: Washington Post challenges subpoena served by United Nations war crimes tribunal on former Post reporter Jonathan Randal to testify in case of Radoslav Brdjanin, Bosnian Serb charged with genocide, persecution and deportation of non-Serbs during Bosnian war; wants court to determine circumstances under which journalists must testify; holds journalists working in conflict zones should not be required to testify unless absolutely vital because it could hamper their work and endanger their lives (M)
news.title: Paper Fights Subpoena Of Journalist By U.N. Court

news.abstract: Church of Nativity, Bethlehem, is dirty but apparently undamaged after withdrawal of over 130 Palestinian gunmen, civilians and clergy members following 39-day seige by Israeli army; Israeli troops leave Manger Square; area residents, freed from nearly constant curfew, come to gape at church; some from area's dwindling Christian population come to pray and rejoice in tumult that breaks jealously guarded protocols that divide church's administration between Orthodox and Roman Catholic denominations; photos (M)
news.title: In Church of Nativity, the Refuse of a Siege

news.abstract: Profile of Sheema Kermani, Pakistani dancer whose classical art form is now largely banned in increasingly conservative Muslim Pakistan; she deplores pressure on women to hide their bodies; is one of few dancers who have not retreated into exile or retirement; photo (M)
news.title: A Pakistani Dancer and Her Life Underground

news.abstract: Bush administration officials reportedly brief Congress on what they describe as disturbing intelligence indicating that Russia is preparing to resume nuclear tests, even as Pres Bush prepares to meet with Pres Vladimir V Putin to discuss arms control later this month; among members of Congress who receive briefing, reaction ranges from alarm to skepticism; some wonder if report is tactic to help clear way for US to resume nuclear testing; others are alarmed enough to draft bill that would call for access to Russian nuclear sites and allow work on new generaiton of American nuclear warheads; Russian officials maintain that their nuclear weapons program remains within constraints of Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty signed by Pres Clinton in 1996 but never ratified by Senate; Pres Bush contends it does not adequately protect nation's security interests, although his administration continues to honor test moratorium (M)
news.title: Administration Says Russia Is Preparing Nuclear Tests

news.abstract: Diplomat says eight North Koreans who tried to storm into two foreign consulates in Shenyang, China, are seeking asylum in United States, not in South Korea; this pulls United States into messy international debate; it also puts to test Pres Bush's Feb expression of 'great sympathy and empathy' for North Korean people; other North Koreans who have sought refuge and asylum at United States Embassy in Beijing wanted to go to South Korea, which has policy of accepting North Koreans; request for asylum in US pushes Americans to take explicit stand on politically loaded question: should hundreds of thousands of North Koreans illegally in China be given protected political refugee status under United Nations convenants; map (M)
news.title: North Korean Migrants Pull U.S. Into a Diplomatic Mess

news.abstract: Amb Wendy Chamberlin will leave United States Embassy in Pakistan after nine months to return home to family, saying 'I'm a mother first'; her children are not with her because State Dept says Pakistan is unsafe for all but essential embassy workers; workers throughout embassy, majority of them men, are making same decision as Chamberlin, advising State Dept that they want to leave their assignments early rather then endure continuous separation from spouses and children; photo (M)
news.title: At Embassy in Pakistan, Home Is Next Objective

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook vignettes from United Nations' first General Assembly Special Session on Children, during which children are encouraged to be seen and heard (M)
news.title: Reporter's Notebook; To Be Young and in Negotiations: A U.N. Education

news.abstract: The Likud Party voted tonight in favor of a resolution never to allow the creation of a Palestinian state, defying its leader, Prime Minister Ariel Sharon.
news.title: Rebuffing Sharon, Party Repudiates Palestinian State

news.abstract: China turns enthusiastic attention to public bathrooms, long-neglected aspect of life; is spending millions of dollars to upgrade public restrooms in campaign quietly begun after joining World Trade Organization in 2001; lavish renovations of public restrooms in Beijing with porcelain flush toilets and lockable stalls described; standard toilet in much of rest of country is open pit in concrete floor; photos (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; Where Toilets Are the Pits, a Push for Porcelain

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority's intelligence service head Amin al-Hendi says recent suicide bombing in pool hall in Tel Aviv, Israel, does not appear to be work of Palestinian terrorists, but rather was conducted by Israeli criminals against illegal gambling club; Israel dismisses remarks as baseless and irresponsible; says bombing was conducted by Hamas, radical Islamic group (M)
news.title: Palestinians Sow Confusion And Doubt On Bombing

news.abstract: Former Pres Jimmy Carter begins five-day visit to Cuba with promise from Pres Fidel Castro that he can inspect any of island's biotechnology research facilities; offer made at welcoming ceremony in Havana seeks to blunt State Department allegations that Cuba has developed limited capacity to make biological weapons and shares biotechnology with rogue nations; Castro says Carter is free to meet with whomever he wishes; Carter in welcoming address says he is visiting as friend of Cuban people and looks forward to meeting with Cubans from all walks of life; his arrival in Havana and tour of city described; photo (M)
news.title: Castro Says Carter Can Inspect Biotechnology Centers

news.abstract: Terrorist bombing of outdoor market in Kaspisk, capital of Russian republic of Dagestan, takes heavy toll on children; 17 children died out of 41 fatalities and 30 more children were wounded; authorities say bomb appears to be antipersonnel mine, detonated by remote control; say bombing may be related to guerrilla war in neighboring Chechnya; maps; photo (M)
news.title: A Bombing In Russia: A Massacre Of Children

news.abstract: Streets of Freetown, Sierra Leone, are scenes of lively campaign rallies in last days leading up to country's first elections since brutal civil war in 1999; underscores how much things have changed in West African nation, where only two years ago rebels outsmarted and humiliated UN peacekeeping force, leaving thousands dead on streets; question looms over election over whether country can survive without current umbrella of Western and UN aid; despite governing party's slogan that everything is plentiful, war destroyed nearly everything in country; maps; photo (M)
news.title: For Sierra Leone Ballot, Hope Trumps Despair

news.abstract: Interview with India's Defense Min George Fernandes, who says India has no plans to launch military attack against Pakistan over next few months even if severely provoked; rising tensions between both countries in recent months over issue of Kashmir noted (M)
news.title: Minister Says India Won't Attack Pakistan

news.abstract: Mexico inches toward politics of stalemate as Institutional Revolutionary Party, former governing party, has succeeded in blocking coalition government of Pres Vicente Fox at every opportunity in Congress; Fox is struggling to consolidate political power in capital and throughout Mexico (M)
news.title: Mexico Now Appears to Be Developing the Politics of Stalemate

news.abstract: Former Pres Jimmy Carter says Bush administration officials who briefed him before trip to Cuba never mentioned any concerns about Cuban involvement in developing biological weapons; tours Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology in Havana with Pres Fidel Castro; comments come as Sec of State Colin L Powell is casting doubt on recent assertions by State Dept official John R Bolton that Cuba has developed limited offensive biological warfare research and development effort (S)
news.title: Carter and Powell Cast Doubt on Bioarms in Cuba

news.abstract: Text of remarks by Pres Bush on new nuclear weapons treaty with Russia (S)
news.title: The Words Of Bush On Treaty

news.abstract: Provision of new nuclear arms treaty between US and Russia, to be signed by Pres Bush and Pres Vladimir Putin at Moscow summit, discussed; graphs (M)
news.title: Treaty Offers Pentagon New Flexibility for New Set of Nuclear Priorities

news.abstract: Ethnic Albanian man is sentenced to 15 years in prison for killing elderly Serbian woman in Kosovo, second conviction in recent days in revenge crimes against Serbs in province (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Kosovo: Convictions In Serbs' Killings

news.abstract: Video of beheading of American journalist Daniel Pearl is reportedly shown in Pakistani court in closed trial of Ahmed Omar Sheikh and three others charged with his kidnapping and murder (M)
news.title: Video of Death Of Journalist Is Seen in Court In Pakistan

news.abstract: CANNES—  The Cannes Festival at this flashy little beach resort is striving to revamp its legendary frosty image and stave off grumbles from foreign guests, and the Hollywood contingent — so desired, yet so feared.
news.title: MOVIE CRAZY : Cannes, Hollywood... Bollywood & the world

news.abstract: PARIS:—  Bowing to pressure from credit ratings agencies to reduce debt and improve transparency, Vivendi Universal on Tuesday agreed to the early settlement of a financing arrangement with Deutsche Bank that could have exposed the media company to billions of dollars in off-balance sheet risks.
news.title: Vivendi walks tightrope with balance sheet

news.abstract: Britain, in latest bid to deal with growing numbers of migrants in urban areas, plans to build three centers to house new arrivals whose asylum applications are being processed; community groups and advocacy groups oppose plans (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Segregating Asylum Seekers

news.abstract: PAKISTAN: Crackdown In The Wild Northwest ; CAMBODIA: A Poke At U.N.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain edges closer to outright endorsement of joining Europe's single currency; says it would be 'betrayal of our national interest' if Britons choose to remain apart from new money for political reasons alone; membership in 12-nation euro zone is one of most contentious issues facing Blair; he is seen as being far more supportive of adopting euro than Gordon Brown, chancellor of exchequer; Blair indicates that Britons might be called to pass judgment on euro membership sooner than expected (M)
news.title: Blair Says Merrie Olde England Indeed Needs Shiny New Euro

news.abstract: Prime Min Hun Sen suggests United Nations pulled out of talks with Cambodia on setting up trial of former Khmer Rouge leaders because it wanted to avoid embarrassment; bases his gibe on historical reality that United Nations continued to recognize brutal Communist movement throughout its reign of terror and for decade after; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Cambodia: A Poke At U.N.

news.abstract: Israel's recent military offensive in West Bank causes physical damage estimated at $361 million by international donors who are mobilizing to finance reconstruction; by comparison, first 15 months of Israeli-Palestinian fighting caused estimated $305 million in damage; damage assessment is carried out by World Bank, United Nations agencies, European Union, United States Agency for International Development and officials from various countries, in cooperation with Palestinian Authority (M)
news.title: West Bank Damages Put at $361 Million

news.abstract: Diplomatic dispute between China and Japan escalates over case of North Korean family seeking political asylum in Japanese consulate last week; Chinese police arrested family, including 2-year-old girl, within Japanese compound in Shenyang, prompting angry protests, accusations and news conferences about who should control their fate; crisis threatens careers of several high-level Japanese officials, including foreign minister; dispute originates from disagreement over whether Chinese police should have been in Japanese consular compound (M)
news.title: Japan and China Intensify Dispute Over Korean Asylum Seekers

news.abstract: Nearly 1,000 British commandos were airlifted to eastern Afghanistan today after an Australian patrol came under fire.
news.title: Taliban Killed in New Operation in Afghanistan Mountains

news.abstract: Africa ZIMBABWE: Black Squatters Face Eviction; MALI: Ex-general Appears To Win Election.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Case of Zafran Bibi, Pakistani rape victim, raises outcry, even in Pakistan, because of her sentence of death by stoning, punishment called for by Koranic law but never carried out there before; human rights workers say that in Pakistan, as many as half the women who report rape are charged with adultery; say even if Zafran's case returns to more typical course, she will spend 10 to 15 years in prison as result of her rape; note that men can easily deflect accusation of rape by claiming victim consented; say abuse of women is endemic in Pakistan; photo; map (M)
news.title: In Pakistan, Rape Victims Are the 'Criminals'

news.abstract: Newspaper of Cuba's Communist Party, in highly unusual gesture of openness, publishes uncensored text of former Pres Jimmy Carter's speech in which he bluntly criticized Cuba's government for denying basic freedoms and endorsed referendum to improve rights; referendum campaign itself has been subjected to news blackout in state-run media, even after supporters garnered more than 10,000 signatures on petitions; newspaper Granma devotes five pages to Carter's speech and to his detailed responses to audience members who denounced referendum campaign, known as Project Varela, as foreign creation; Granma does not act on Carter's suggestion that it also print demands of project: for electoral law reform, amnesty for political prisoners, freedom of expression and right to own small businesses (M)
news.title: Party Organ In Cuba Prints Speech By Carter

news.abstract: Berlin Mayor Klaus Wowereit presents citizenship certificate for Marlene Dietrich to her grandson Peter Riva; Dietrich left Germany in 1930 and became United States citizen, criticizing Nazis; she had hostile reception in Berlin in 1960 and vowed not to return; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Making Posthumous Amends

news.abstract: Indian officials say they are considering military action against Pakistan, which they blame for terrorist attacks of May 14 that killed 32 people; also plan punitive diplomatic steps; some in government voice bitter disappointment that US has been unable to persuade Pakistan, ally against terrorism in Afghanistan, to stop sponsoring terrorism against India; photo of demonstration by supporters of Hindu nationlist Bharatiya Janata Party outside Pakistani Embassy in New Delhi (M)
news.title: Still Raw From Recent Attack, India Is Girding Itself for War

news.abstract: Profile of Rafael Barajas, dean of Mexico's large and vigorous corps of political cartoonists; his cartoons, which appear in leftist La Jornada, frequently take aim at Pres Vicente Vox, whom he says is totally incable of living up to changes that he promised; photo (M)
news.title: His Mood Seems Mellow; His Cartoons Are Not

news.abstract: Former Pres Jimmy Carter urges Pres Bush not to provide assistance for dissidents, human rights advocates and independent journalists in Cuba; says dissidents he met with are deeply concerned that such direct help from US would allow Pres Fidel Castro to discredit their efforts; adviser to Carter says many dissidents also favor lifting trade embargo, which Bush wants to tighten (M)
news.title: Carter Urges Bush to Reject Plan to Aid Cuba Dissidents

news.abstract: Mexico will pay debt of billions of gallons of water it owes US under 1944 treaty; much of water has been diverted before reaching Rio Grande by officials in Chihuahua (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Fox Promises Water For U.S.

news.abstract: German court upholds injunction that effectively prohibits news organizations from even hinting that Chancellor Gerhard Schroder colors his hair; Schroder's efforts to suppress such reports is mercilessly lampooned in ads run by cosmetics company for new hair strengthener (S)
