news.title: Chancellor's Hair Color Is Now Ward of the Court

news.abstract: Military planners in Pentagon preparing for possible invasion of Iraq say most complicated problem they face is chance that Pres Saddam Hussein might use chemcial or biological weapons against American forces of their allies; this has prompted discussion of host of pre-emptive options for destroying his stockpiles or limiting his ability to use them; Iraq possessed chemical and probably biological weapons during Persian Gulf war of 1991; it did not use them, possibly because of American threats of retaliation; now that Pres Bush has place himself behind effort to change governments in Iraq, military experts say they must assume that Hussein would use every weapon in his arsenal (M)
news.title: Pentagon's Worry: Iraqi Chemical Arms

news.abstract: Alvaro Uribe, ultraconservative candidate for president in Colombia, has made promise to crack down on leftist rebels; he holds commanding lead in polls and is expected to defeat his nearest rival, Horacio Serpa, when election is held next week; what is uncertain is what effects his policies would have on his country and what they would mean for United States, which has provided nearly $2 billion in mostly military aid since 2000; Uribe says he will break from policies of current president, Andres Pastrana, whose peace talks with rebels collapsed; says he will become 'first soldier of Colombia' in campaign against rebels, promising to double size of army's combat force and police and to organize one million villagers to serve as informants; conflict-weary voters seem to be overlooking fact that Uribe is independent candidate representing far right in centrist country; photo; map (M)
news.title: Rightist's Hard Line Appeals to War-Weary Colombians

news.abstract: India seems to be taking steps needed to go to war with Pakistan; expels Pakistani Amb Ashraf Jehangir Qazi to protest attack by three heavily armed gunmen that it accuses Pakistan of sponsoring; gunmen killed 32 people, including wives and children of Indian Army soldiers; Indian Army, Navy and Air Force chiefs brief Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee on military options for countering what India regards as Pakistan-sponsored terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir, territory claimed by both countries; Indian and Pakistani troops bombard each other with heavy mortar and artillery fire; United States State Dept is expected to work intensely to persuade Pakistan to be more effective in shutting down militant Islamic groups based in Pakistan-held Kashmir (M)
news.title: To the Drums of War, India Expels Pakistan Ambassador

news.abstract: Many European banks and corporations are making English official corporate language as way to leverage international links and enable far-flung affiliates to communicate with headquarters and among themselves; behind choice lies reality that unsettles some Europeans: use of English is mainly determined by unchallenged dominance of United States in industry, commerce and finance; photos (M)
news.title: In Europe, Going Global Means, Alas, English

news.abstract: Riaz Basra, Pakistan's most feared Islamic militant, is brought down by simple villager armed with .22-caliber rifle and few neighbors with old pump-action rifles and handguns; Basra, head of dreaded Sunni extremist group Lashkar-i-Jangvi, led life brimming with murderous action along with legend of miraculous escapes; he met his end in village of Dakota, Pakistan, in shootout with Fida Hussain Ghalvi, who has kept watch every night since Basra killed his brother and other villagers in 1997; groups like Basra's have usually reserved their wrath for fellow Muslims, and have not become well known in West; photos; map (M)
news.title: For Militant, No Glorified End, but Death in the Dust

news.abstract: Growing number of lawmakers from both parties are visiting Cuba on their own and demanding that US open it up to tourism and trade, even as Pres Bush heads to Miami to lay out tougher restrictions on travel to Cuba, and to lend support for government opponents there; will condition any easing of restrictions on adoption of democratic reforms, such as freeing all political prisoners and giving opposition political parties freedom to organize and speak; is committed personally and politically to hard-line policy toward Cuba; pivotal role played by Cuban-Americans in his victory in 2000 presidential election noted (M)
news.title: Bush Faces Pressure From Congress to Alter Cuba Policy

news.abstract: Afghans say five people killed in May 12 raid by US Special Forces on village of Char Chine in Oruzgan province were farmers; American military spokesman says that troops raided compound suspected of being sanctuary for senior members of Taliban and Al Qaeda and that five killed opened fire first; villagers describe raid; map; photos (M)
news.title: Afghans Say 5 Killed in a U.S. Raid Were Farmers

news.abstract: Many Hong Kong merchants and longtime residents are appalled by plans by developers to demolish Stanley Market, island's most famous Chinese street market, to build nine-story hotel and air conditioned shopping mall; while other street markets have already been bulldozed and replaced by malls with little protest, Stanley's merchants and Hong Kong's small community of historic preservationists seem determined to fight latest scheme (M)
news.title: Developers Threaten to Gobble Up a Famous Hong Kong Market

news.abstract: American Special Forces soldier is killed in Afghanistan after unit came under attack while on patrol in eastern mountains where coalition forces have been operating; is identified as Sgt Gene Arden Vance Jr of Morgantown, W Va; photo (S)
news.title: U.S. Soldier Killed in a Firefight in Afghanistan

news.abstract: The exodus of Venezuelans, desparate over deepening political divisions, is the latest chapter in a reversal for a country that was once a magnet for immigrants.
news.title: Chaos Prompts Exodus, Changing a Capital's Face

news.abstract: Afghan warlord Padsha Khan Zadran, still controls large parts of Khost and Pakita Province despite efforts of interim government of Hamid Karzai to oust him; situation has become most glaring example of government's inability to control events outside capital of Kabul; photo (M)
news.title: Afghan Warlord Muddles Interim Government's Plans

news.abstract: Irish voters elect Prime Min Bertie Ahern for second term, at time when disaffected European electorates are turning against incumbent governments; dimensions of victory are huge, with his Fianna Fail party sending traditional foe, Fine Gael, to humiliating defeat and coming within several seats of winning majority in 166-seat Parliament; his presidential-style campaign, in which he traveled 3,000 miles and canvassed all 42 districts, discussed; brief biographical profile; photo (M)
news.title: Charmed by Their Leader, the Irish Ask Him to Stay

news.abstract: US military officials say Sgt Gene Arden Vance Jr, Army Special Forces soldier killed on May 19 in Afghanistan on reconnaissance mission with allied Afghan troops near Pakistan border, died in brief battle in which an Afghan soldier was wounded and one adversary was believed to have been killed; coalition forces press search for attackers (S)
news.title: U.S. Gives More Details Of Clash Where G.I. Died

news.abstract: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon of Israel fired ministers from the rigorously Orthodox Shas Party from his cabinet after they voted against an emergency economic package in Parliament.
news.title: Sharon Ejects Party From Israeli Cabinet

news.abstract: Abdul Ghani Lone, a moderate Kashmiri separatist leader, was assassinated today, a killing that India and Pakistan immediately charged each other with.
news.title: Tensions Mount Over Kashmir as Separatist Leader Is Killed

news.abstract: Rock star Bono and and Treasury Sec Paul H O'Neill visit Accra, Ghana, to start off their two-week fact-finding tour of Africa; pairing of Bono and O'Neill illustrates expanding ideological consensus on need to address poverty, disease, famine and conflict in Africa--as well as remaining gulf between left and right about how best to do it; Bono wants to convince Bush administration that aid to Africa is both moral imperative and good investment of taxpayers' money; O'Neill makes clear that US will be skeptical about providing aid to countries that cannot show how they are improving standards of living; photo of Bono and O'Neill with Pres John A Kufuor; map (M)
news.title: Accra Journal; No Mosh Pit, This, but Some Enthusiasm for Aid

news.abstract: American warplanes bomb group of suspected Qaeda and Taliban fighters as they are setting up mortars within striking distance of airfield at Khost, pivotal hub for allied troops in Afghanistan; Canada announces that it will withdraw its 850 troops in Afghanistan this summer (S)
news.title: American Planes Foil an Attack on an Airfield in Afghanistan

news.abstract: News analysis: Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon's latest bold gamble of kicking ministers of Shas, religious Sephardic party, out of his government was impressive display of brinkmanship, given their importance to his coalition; Sharon acted after Shas voted against his proposed emergency economic package, intended to address budget deficit caused in large measure by military offensive he recently ordered in West Bank; dismissal is likely to bolster his already soaring popularity among Isralies, but also threatens to leave his government with barely enough certain votes in Parliament to stave off new elections; if Sharon becomes embroiled in fight for political survival, international efforts to press for peace would probably be stymied for months; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon's Domestic Battle: A Gamble

news.abstract: Pres Kim Dae Jung calls for moratorium on strikes and political infighting in South Korea through end of World Cup soccer finals on June 30; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Leader Urges Calm For World Cup

news.abstract: Bahrain holds municipal elections in which women participate for first time in nation's history as both candidates and voters, but all 31 women running in field of more than 300 candidates lose; all 50 seats on five councils are won by candidates affilated with Islamic organizatons; voting for a man was turned into religious duty in many neighborhoods; female candidates had difficulty meeting voters in country still largely segregated by sex; photos; map (M)
news.title: In Bahrain, Women Run, Women Vote, Women Lose

news.abstract: Kyrgyzstan Prime Min Kurmanbek Bakiyev and cabinet resign amid growing unrest since death of five demonstrators in clashes with police in March (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Kyrgyzstan: Prime Minister Quits

news.abstract: Britain urges its citizens to leave Pakistan, orders departure of more than 150 personnel from its embassy and closes its consulates; actions are in response to rising threats against Westerners in Pakistan since May 8, when car bomb exploded outside hotel in Karachi, killing 11 French citizens and 3 Pakistanis
news.title: British Leave Pakistan

news.abstract: Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee tells Indian soldiers along tense frontier in Kashmir to prepare for 'decisive battle' against terrorism; uses words powerful enough to rally his troops, threaten Pakistan and scare much of world; India has grim choice: make good on pledge to retaliate forcefully against militant groups based in Pakistani territory, or appear at home and abroad as nation that issues meaningless threats; prevailing expectation is that India will strike punitive blow against militants' training camps in Pakistan-controlled area of disputed Jammu and Kashmir State; overarching fear is that escalating confrontation might unleash nuclear combat; two nations have been exchanging artillery fire across frontier for last five days; Pakistan responds to Vajpayee's latest statement saying it would use 'full force' if attacked; worried diplomats from United States and elsewhere schedule visits to New Delhi and Islamabad; photo; map (M)
news.title: Indian Leader's Threat of War Rattles Pakistan and the U.S.

news.abstract: Iran dismisses US State Department report charging Iran is 'most active state sponsor of terrorism' (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Iran: U.S. Terror Charge Denied

news.abstract: Many Russians are disappointed at indications that Pres Bush will not be discussing economic proposals during his Kremlin meeting with Pres Vladimir V Putin; Russian government announces series of agreements and accords two presidents will sign, but there is no mention of investments, economic incentives or other policy changes that would help stimulate Russian economy (M)
news.title: As Bush Heads for Russia, Hopes for an Investment Plan Fade

news.abstract: Israeli Army is stringing barbed wire around Ramallah on West Bank in hope of preventing Palestinian attacks; international aid workers fear this is part of sweeping new restrictions that will further squeeze Palestinians' already crippled economy and perhaps stoke more violence; aid officials say Israeli Army has outlined plan to create eight zones in West Bank, around each of its major cities; say Palestinians needing to travel would apply for special permit to enter or leave zone, and permits, to be renewed monthly, would be valid only during day; if put into effect plan would amount to substantial tightening of existing Israeli policy; for international aid agencies that move food, medicine or construction material, plan would mean tremendous increase in workers, costs and time spent in transport; photo; map (M)
news.title: Israelis Consider New Limits on West Bank Palestinians

news.abstract: Pakistan prepares to shift troops from border with Afghanistan, where they are hunting for Qaeda and Taliban fighters, to front in Kashmir, where tensions with India are quickly rising; government announcement underscores competing interests between ferreting out terrorist remnants while securing region against possibility of full-blown war between nuclear-armed rivals; India and Pakistan have million troops already massed along their 1,800-mile border; two armies are shelling each other with mounting intensity across dividing line in Kashmir; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld expresses concern, noting that because of conflict, Pakistan has placed forces along Indian borders that could be used to help American soldiers along Afghan border (M)
news.title: Pakistan Prepares to Shift Troops From Afghan Border to Kashmir

news.abstract: France's new agriculture minister, Herve Gaymard, says he will defy European Court of Justice order to lift ban on British beef; ban was imposed in 1996 because of fear of mad cow disease; Britian holds France should be fined (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Still Defiant In Beef Dispute

news.abstract: Security Council extends tenure of international troops in Afghanistan for another six months but choses not to expand their ranks, as Afghanistan's interim government and some senior UN officials had urged (S)
news.title: U.N. Extends Tenure Of Afghan Forces

news.abstract: President Bush and President Vladimir V. Putin signed a treaty today reducing their countries' warheads by two thirds.
news.title: U.S. and Russia Sign Nuclear Weapons Reduction Treaty

news.abstract: Asia South KOREA: Political Truce For Soccer; NEPAL: Political Crisis.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Pakistan risks setting off new crisis with India by beginning series of missile tests; Pakistani government denies any provocative intent, and Indian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman dismisses 'missile antics' that she says are targeted at domestic audience in Pakistan; United States says it is 'disappointed' by Pakistan's decision to test missiles, coming day after Pakistan said it would move troops toward India; State Dept issues warning to Americans to defer travel to India and Pakistan because of risk of war; even with Pakistani decision, tensions appear to have lessened; Indian government officials say they will give Pakistan more time, perhaps few weeks, to demonstrate its commitment to stopping infiltration of armed militants into India's side of Kashmir before undertaking any punitive military strikes; photo; map (M)
news.title: At Tense Time, Pakistan Starts To Test Missiles

news.abstract: BERLIN—  One recent bedtime, five-year-old Alec Kubekov read an English book to his mother, a selection from the "Biff and Chip" series. As his father walked in to say goodnight, Alec began translating the book into Russian. "It was a good translation," said his mother. "He was translating for sense, not word for word."
news.title: Learning curves : Helping children break the language barrier

news.abstract: Federal Bureau of Investigation asks at least two Internet sites to remove video showing questioning and beheading of Daniel Pearl, Wall Street Journal reporter who was kidnapped and murdered in Pakistan; hosts of two sites are said to comply with request, which FBI spokeswoman says was made out of consideration for Pearl's family (S)
news.title: Web Sites Remove Video of Pearl's Death

news.abstract: American officials say military review of battle in eastern Afghanistan in early March that left seven American soldiers dead found intelligence lapses, radio glitches and miscommunication between commanders and commandos; clash came on third day of three-week-long campaign in Shah-i-Kot Valley, and stemmed from attempt to rescue Navy Seal who had fallen out of helicopter; Gen Tommy R Franks, head of allied forces in Afghanistan, defends operation, and attributes any failings to clever fighters from Al Qaeda, unforgiving terrain and 'fog and friction' of war; says no disciplinary action or command changes are being considered as result of that battle; senior Pentagon military officer who conducted review of battle says he sent report on how to improve 'tactics, techniques and procedures' used by military forces involved in fight (M)
news.title: U.S. Review of a Deadly Afghanistan Battle Finds Lapses

news.abstract: South Korean Embassy in Beijing says that three North Koreans sought refuge there, and South Korean government demands that Chinese authorities treat case in 'humanitarian manner' (S)
news.title: 3 North Koreans in Beijing Defect to Seoul

news.abstract: Environmentalists in Switzerland prevail in their campaign to prevent auto racing champion Michael Schumacher from building lavish home in area zoned for agriculture; while most Swiss live in cities, they are greatly attached to concept of rural life, and farmers are heavily subsidized to keep them on the land; land use is strictly regulated (M)
news.title: Swiss Overrule Lavish Home In a Clash Over Rural Values

news.abstract: African leaders, along with some of poverty-fighting advocacy groups that for years have viewed globalization with suspicion if not downright hostility, are increasingly embracing international trade as most powerful tool available for creating jobs, steady incomes, hope and political stability; after concentrating for years on winning relief from crippling debt burdens and lobbying for increases in foreign aid payments, African governments are instead starting to demand reduced tariffs and other changes in trade policies from United States and other rich nations to increase sales of local products; photo of Treasury Sec Paul O'Neill, who is traveling through Africa with Bono, musician (M)
news.title: Seeking Trade, Africans Find Western Barriers

news.abstract: Estimated 12 million Colombians are set to vote for new president, and many, angry about rebel violence, plan to vote for hard-line conservative candidate, Alvara Uribe Velez, who promises to double size of security forces to fight rebels; his main opponent is Horacio Serpa, who is far behind in polls; many Colombians are fed up with regime of Pres Andres Pastrana, who came into office four years ago pledging to negotiate with leftist rebels; photos (M)
news.title: Colombia Voters Are Angry, And Rebels May Pay Price

news.abstract: German officials negotiate with Turkish government to extradite Metin Kaplan, Turk who is serving four-year sentence in Germany for operating terrorist organization and calling for murder of rival; Kaplan is leader of banned terror group known as Caliphate; is wanted in Turkey on charges of involvement in failed 1998 plot to fly airplane filled with explosives into mausoleum of Kemal Ataturk, founder of Turkish republic, in Ankara; Kaplan's organization, which once had 12,000 members in Germany, advocates killing of non-Muslims (M)
news.title: Germany May Extradite Islamic Militant to Turkey

news.abstract: Alvaro Uribe Velez, hardliner, is elected president of Colombia with 53 percent of vote, or more than 20 percentage points ahead of closest rival Horacio Serpa, Liberal Party populist; wins majority needed to avoid runoff; he pledges uncompromising 'hard hand' against insurgents; quickly receives backing of US and congratuations from Amb Anne Patterson; photo (M)
news.title: Hard-Liner Elected in Colombia With a Mandate to Crush Rebels

news.abstract: American intelligence assessmentwarns that full-scale nuclear exchange between India and Pakistan could kill up to 12 million people immediately and injury up to 7 million; even 'more limited' nuclear war would have cataclysmic results, overwhelming hospitals across Asia and requiring vast foreign assistance, particularly from US, to battle radioactive contamination, famine and disease (M)
news.title: 12 Million Could Die at Once in an India-Pakistan Nuclear War

news.abstract: SEOUL:—  Three North Koreans have sought refuge in the South Korean Embassy in Beijing and the South Korean government has demanded that Chinese authorities treat the case "in a humanitarian manner."
news.title: North Koreans defect to embassy in China

news.abstract: Shells from Pakistani positions over mountain fall on Kashmiri border village of Uri, as threat of India-Pakistan war looms over valley; photo; map (M)
news.title: As Shells Fall on Kashmiri Border Village, Residents Fear Outbreak of War

news.abstract: Rome Journal on elaborate setting and security for meeting of NATO and Russian leaders at Practica di Mare military base outside Italian capital; stage sets devised by Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi described; photo (M)
news.title: Rome Journal; A Faux Treaty Room, With Missiles

news.abstract: Pres Pervez Musharraf says in nationwide address that Pakistan does not want conflict with India but will 'respond with full might' if war breaks out; urges India to open dialogue and to move toward normalization of relations; lays full blame for standoff on India; repeats he will not allow Pakistan to be used as staging ground for terror attacks, India's chief complaint against him; denies Islamic militants are crossing into India's side of Kashmir to carry out raids; pledges support for those resisting Indian rule in mostly Muslim region; Indian officials react with anger to address, finding little by way of conciliation; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistan Vows Its 'Full Might' If a War Comes

news.abstract: Excerpts from Pres Bush's Memorial Day speech at American Cemetery in Normandy, France (M)
news.title: Bush's Memorial Words: 'Sacrifice of the Young'

news.abstract: Early results from parliamentary election in Losotho show governing party taking strong lead (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Lesotho: Government Ahead In Vote

news.abstract: Chinese official reports that 300 Uighur Muslims from China's western province of Xinjiang were captured in Afghanistan fighting with Taliban forces and that hundreds more Chinese Muslim separatists remain hidden in Afghanistan and Pakistan (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Muslims In Afghanistan

news.abstract: Colombia's Pres-elect Alvaro Uribe Velez, who won presidency promising to crack down on leftist rebels, strikes conciliatory tone by holding out possibility of negotiating with guerrilla commanders under UN mediation; hopes to set up meeting with Sec Gen Kofi Annan; says negotiations with right-wing paramilitary group, bitter enemy of rebels, are possible--proposition predecessors declined to consider because of widespread rights abuses perpetuated by organization; photos (M)
news.title: Colombian President-Elect Softens Tone on Rebels

news.abstract: NATO formally welcomes Russia as partner but not full-fledged member in organization created 53 years ago to contain Soviet power and expansion; meeting of leaders of 19 member nations in Rome includes Pres Bush and Pres Vladimir Putin; Bush says agreement joins former foes as partners, overcoming 50 years of division and decade of uncertainty; similar sentiments are echoed by Putin, who nevertheless describes agreement as only a beginning, noting that relations between NATO and Russia have historically been far from straightforward; new agreement replaces 1997 accord negotiated during Clinton administration that allowed Russia to participate in discussions only after alliance's members reached agreement on common position; gives Russia for first time immediate role in NATO discussions but not veto power over decisions or vote on expansion of membership; excludes Russia from collective defense pact in which all nation's pledge to come to each other's defense if necessary; photos (M)
news.title: NATO Formally Welcomes Russia as a Partner

news.abstract: Palestinian gunman fires on Israeli settlement near Nablus, killing three young yeshiva students before being shot and killed; Israel dies in road ambush near Ramallah; attacks follow five suicide bombings in less than week; compound evidence that recent major Israeli military offensive did little to blunt Palestinian attacks; Israeli raids in Jenin, Hebron, Beit Jala and Qalqilya in West Bank leads to arrests of 14 Palestinians; Army remains in control of Bethlehem; map; photo (M)
news.title: Arab Rakes Israeli Yeshiva With Gunfire; 3 Students Die

news.abstract: Senior Pakistani intelligence officials say recent terror attacks point to worrisome links between local extremists and fugitive Al Qaeda leaders who are not concentrated along Afghan border, as American officials contend, but have filtered across country into major cities; say imminent battle may be one for Pakistan itself (M)
news.title: Pakistani Intelligence Officials See Qaeda Peril in Their Cities

news.abstract: Stephen Byers, Britain's transport secretary responsible for country's ailing rail and road systems, resigns after turbulent one-year tenure marred by crashes and service disruptions on trains, increased tie-ups on roads and high-profile scandals in his office (M)
news.title: Train Wrecks and Other Headaches: A British Minister Quits

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair today named his work and pensions secretary to the job of running Britain's transportation system.
news.title: New Transport Secretary Named for Britain's Troubled System

news.abstract: Officials in Taiwan say they pinpointed seafloor location of data and cockpit voice recorders from Hong Kong-bound China Airlines Boeing 747 that broke into four pieces in midflight on May 25, apparently killing all 225 people aboard (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Taiwan: 'Black Boxes' From Crash Located

news.abstract: Canary Islands must contend with influx of African migrants who make hazardous journey on small wooden boats to island of Fuerteventura, hoping it will be their first step toward better life; all illegal immigrants except for pregnant women and small children are locked in terminal for full 40 days before being deported; aid workers complain about poor conditions for detainees; photos; map (M)
news.title: Canary Islands Journal; Squalid Dead End for Migrants' Hopes

news.abstract: Italian and German investigators disclose fresh information suggesting that hints of attack involving aircraft and US were more widespread among European law enforcement agencies before Sept 11 than previously suspected; German investigators say communications among Al Qaeda cells has recently picked up; Italian officials note that conversations they intercepted were from summer of 2000, but say they demonstrate that Al Qaeda was organizing something (M)
news.title: Cryptic Tapes From 2000 Hinted at Air Attack in U.S.

news.abstract: United States offers reward of up to $5 million for information leading to arrest of five top leaders of militant Philippine Muslim group Abu Sayyaf; group is holding two American missionaries hostage, Martin and Gracia Burnham; Deputy Defense Sec Paul D Wolfowitz to visit southern Philippines next week to check on progress of rescue operation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Philippines: U.S. Bounty For Militants' Arrest

news.abstract: Pres Vicente Fox's aides say he will not fulfill his pledge to Pres Bush to meet deadline for plan to pay Mexico's enormous water debt to United States; Mexico owes 456 billion gallons under 1944 treaty on dividing waters of Rio Grande; Fox's inability to deliver quickly on his personal pledge to Bush to solve waer crisis raises questions about his ability to govern (M)
news.title: Mexico Misses Deadline for Water-Debt Plan

news.abstract: PERU: Court To Seek Fujimori Extradition; Mexico CITY: Delay On Two-level Highways; MEXICO: All Cyanide Recovered; CUBA: Spy Suspect Arrested.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Pres Bush will send Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld to India and Pakistan in effort to defuse threat of nuclear war between longtime enemies; makes strongest demand yet that Pres Pervez Musharraf of Pakistan crack down on infiltration of terrorists into India, amid growing alarm that five-month-long military buildup has reached new point of crisis; Sec Colin L Powell is sending his deputy, Richard L Armitage, to region next week; Bush has been praising Musharraf for his pledge to clamp down on Islamic extremists who carry out attacks on Indian civilians along line of separation, and newly harsh tone appears aimed at assuaging Indian rage over incursions; Bush also warns remnants of Al Qaeda thought to be gathered in western Pakistan not to exploit India-Pakistan conflict to make trouble along Pakistan's western border (M)
news.title: Bush Presses Pakistan on Kashmir And Orders Rumsfeld to Region

news.abstract: Son is born to Mariane Pearl, widow of Wall Street Journal reporter Daniel Pearl who was kidnapped and killed by Islamic militants in Pakistan four months ago (S)
news.title: Son Is Born to Widow of Reporter Killed in Karachi

news.abstract: Prime Min Jean Chretien freezes dozens of government contracts, reorganizes his cabinet and issues new rules on political donations and conflicts of interest; he is struggling to contain worst ethics controversy to face his Liberal Party in years, involving what opposition calls pattern of government ministers' handing out contracts to friends and companies who donate to party; Globe and Mail, Canada's most influential newspaper, calls for Chretien to resign; he has held office since 1993 and will probably survive crisis, but controversy has already intensified jostling among party politicians likely to use gathering of Liberals in Feb to position themselves as his successor (M)
news.title: Canadian Leader Attacked In a Loud Ethics Brouhaha

news.abstract: Europe RUSSIA: Communist Leader Denounces Summit ; BRITAIN: Guilty Verdict In Foot-and-mouth Case.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Following is the full text from President Bush's commencement address at the United States Military Academy at West Point Saturday, as recorded by The New York Times.
news.title: Text of Bush's Speech at West Point

news.abstract: All nine senior officials at the China Aviation Development Foundation, a quasi-governmental group that owns 71 percent of China Airlines, resigned to take responsibility for the crash last Saturday of a China Airlines Boeing 747 into the Taiwan Strait. all 225 aboard died. Rough seas and powerful currents have prevented the recovery of the aircraft's data and cockpit voice recorders and most of the wreckage.   Keith Bradsher (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Taiwan: Officials Quit After Air Crash

news.abstract: Profile of Umar Farooq, Kashmiri Muslim political and spiritual leader, who seeks political settlement of Kashmir crisis; assumed roles from father, assasinated in 1990, and moderate separatist leader Abdul Ghani Lone, assassinated this May; is possible target of Kashmiri militants backed by Pakistani intelligence agency, who favor violent route to independence; Indian government, unwilling to negotiate Kashmir's status, will not talk to him; photo (M)
news.title: Kashmiri Impelled to Lead by His Father's Death

news.abstract: Parliament overwhelmingly endorsed a looser union between the two remaining republics. Constitutional experts now have to work out the exact structure of the new state, to be called Serbia and Montenegro, which was created under pressure from the European Union to stave off a Montenegrin independence bid and to discourage other Balkan separatists, especially in Kosovo, a province of Serbia. Serbia and Montenegro will be broadly autonomous but share a president, cabinet and army; either can leave the union after three years.   Daniel Simpson (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Yugoslavia: A Nation Reshaped

news.abstract: Lt Gen Dan K McNeill formally assumes command of American-led forces in Afghanistan; says first goal is to put in place more systematic effort to hunt and kill elusive Qaeda and Taliban forces, interview; says he will not use coalition troops to provide nationwide security; photo (M)
news.title: New U.S. Commander At Helm in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Pres Bush delivers toughly worded speech to 1,000 graduates at United States Military Academy that seems aimed at preparing Americans for potential war with Iraq; says cold war doctrines of containment and deterrence are irrelevant in world where only strategy for defeating America's new enemies is to strike them first; says to wait for threats to fully materialize is to wait too long; says enemy's plans must be disrupted and worst threats be confronted before they emerge; he does not mention Iraq by name, but says 'even weak states' could hope to 'strike great nations'; reminds graduates that in their last year at West Point America was attacked by 'ruthless and resourceful enemy'; says they are graduating in time of war; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. MUST ACT FIRST TO BATTLE TERROR, BUSH TELLS CADETS

news.abstract: Yasir Arafat and his top aides are scrambling to address rising Palestinian and international demands for reform of his multiple security forces; but pressure from Bush administration and elsewhere may be having unintended consequences; some top officials whom Israelis regard as possible successors to Yasir Arafat are shying away from security jobs, fearing that such posts could make them appear to be doing Israelis' bidding; Prime Min Ariel Sharon says thorough changes to Palestinian Authority are condition for his return to peace negotiations; Bush administration favors political talks alongside reform; because there has been no public demand for talks by Bush administration, Palestinians fear that even its talk of reform is stalling tactic; photos (M)
news.title: Key Palestinian Security Posts Becoming Harder to Fill

news.abstract: Soldiers on Pakistani side of Ksahmir's disputed frontier wait for assault by Indian Army that they expect could come at any moment; they harbor few illusions about their chances against their more powerful enemy; they are plotting defense and their military leaders are defiant; this reflects belief among Pakistanis that it would be Indians who start war, but that once one started, Pakistanis, however outgunned and outnumbered, would not suffer humiliations visited on them in wars past; world leaders fear that India's overwhelming superiority in conventional forces could prompt desperate Pakistani leadership to use their nuclear weapons to halt attack; photo (M)
news.title: On Kashmir Line, Pakistanis Wait, With Few Illusions

news.abstract: Democracy is slowly, imperfectly, inching across Africa, continent better known for wars, disease, corruption and repression; since 1990, 42 of 48 countries in sub-Saharan Africa have held multiparty elections; in early 1980's, only four countries held multiparty elections on continent dominated by military juntas and autocrats; one dictator, Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire, famously declared that 'democracy is not for Africa'; today, despite common complaints of vote rigging and political intimidation, most Africans have right to choose their leaders at ballot box; over last two years, governing parties in Senegal, Mauritius, Ghana and Mali have peacefully handed power to opposition party rivals; but for many ordinary Africans, tangible benefits of political change remain elusive; so far, democracy has often been followed by period of deteriorating living standards, and many Africans are now freer but poorer than they have been in decades; long economic decline is linked to poor leadership, falling demand for Africa's commodities and reluctance of Western governments to open their markets to African products; foreign aid to Africa, which soared during cold war as Soviet Union and United States competed for allies among continent's dictators, has dropped to its lowest levels; photos; graph (L)
news.title: Africa Creeps Along Path to Democracy

news.abstract: Flora Lewis, New York Times foreign affairs columnist, dies at age 79; photo (M)
news.title: Flora Lewis, Astute Observer of World Affairs for The Times and Others, Dies at 79

news.abstract: Fifteen men and woman are jailed in Oaxaca, Mexico, on suspicion of killing 26 villagers from rural reaches of Oaxaca State in vendetta over land; officials say suspects were residents of nearby villages that have fought people of Santiago Xochiltepec, where victims were from, for many years; maps; phooto (S)
news.title: 16 Arrested in Killings of 26 Over Land Disputes in Mexico

news.abstract: Flora Lewis, New York Times foreign affairs columnist, dies at age 79; photo (M)
news.title: Flora Lewis, 79, Dies; Keen Observer of World Affairs

news.abstract: Focus on October 2001 murder of leading Mexican human rights crusader Digna Ochoa and its implications for Mexico's justice system and Pres Vicente Fox, who has pledged to strengthen rule of law in nation that became democracy with his election in 2000; government investigators are preparing to declare death suicide, citing forensic evidence and trail of correspondence; move sets off alarm among human rights activists in Mexico and abroad, who accuse prosecutors of blaming victim no longer able to defend herself rather investigate soldiers, paramilitary groups and corrupt rural political bosses who were targets of her work; photos (M)
news.title: Rights Lawyer's Odd Death Tests Mexican Justice

news.abstract: SEOUL:—  Sport is able to conjure magic. Here in the capital of South Korea on Friday, Senegal, at its first World Cup, beat the champion of the world and Senegal's former colonial master, France, 1-0. The solitary goal was scored by a big midfielder, Pape Bouba Diop.
news.title: Senegal stuns France, 1-0, as World Cup opens

news.abstract: War is already reality for many Kashmir villagers who live near border with India and have been forced to flee homes because of rising tensions over disputed area; some comment; photo (M)
news.title: War Is Already a Reality For Villagers in Kashmir

news.abstract: Indonesia is taking Malaysia before International Court of Justice over two scenic islands, Sipadan and Litigan, which Indonesia claims; Indonesia claims it was accorded islands by 1891 Anglo-Dutch treaty between region's colonial powers and says Malaysia erred by printing maps showing islands as its territory; map (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: The Hague: Indonesia-Malaysia Island Case

news.abstract: United Nations human rights envoy to Cambodia Peter Leuprecht says number of countries are pressing UN and Cambodia to resume talks on holding international trial for surviving Khmer Rouge leaders; UN recently withdrew from talks saying Cambodian side did not seem serious about reaching agreement; this is first suggestion that talks could resume (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Cambodia: Talks On A Rights Tribunal

news.abstract: Deputy Defense Sec Paul D Wolfowitz arrives, Tabiawan, Philippines, to assess plans for American troops to extend counterterrorism training mission with Philippine military and to become more involved in searching for Gracia and Martin Burnham, Americans held by militant Muslim group Abu Sayyaf; meets with American and Philippine commanders and community leaders on Basilan Island; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Wolfowitz, in Philippines, Looks to a Greater U.S. Role

news.abstract: SWITZERLAND: Bishops Deplore Abortion Vote ; GERMANY: Leader To Boycott Forum ; Northern IRELAND: New Belfast Violence.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Jacques Fauvet, former Le Monde director general, dies at age 87; photo (M)
news.title: Jacques Fauvet, 87, Journalist And Ex-Director of Le Monde

news.abstract: Hong Kong annual candlelight vigil to remember protesters killed by Chinese military in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in 1989 draws sparser crowd than usual this year; poll by group with reputation for impartiality finds that more than half of Hong Kong's population is satisfied with Beijing's rule of China and, separately, with Beijing's handling of Hong Kong affairs (M)
news.title: Hong Kong Passions About Tiananmen Seem to Be Fading

news.abstract: Small amounts of oil caused a big die-off of the algae-eating lizards in the months following a spill.
news.title: Rare Iguanas in Galapagos Are Victims of Oil Spill

news.abstract: Prime Min Helen Clark of New Zealand, former semicolonial ruler of Western Somoa, visits Apia to apologize for New Zealand's negligence in influenza epidemic in 1918, which killed 8,000 islanders, and police suppression in 1929 of independence movement and later banishment of island chiefs; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Pacific: Samoa: New Zealand Regrets Abuses

news.abstract: Kim Hong Gul, the youngest of President Kim Dae Jung's three sons, was indicted today on charges of bribery and influence peddling.
news.title: Son of South Korea's President Indicted

news.abstract: Jean-Marie Le Pen's far-right National Front party is anticipating gains against Socialists and Communists in parliamentary elections in France's north, where unemployment is twice the national average; some Socialists admit they have lost touch with their blue-collar power base; map; photo of Marine Le Pen, Le Pen's daughter, campaigning for National Assembly seat in Lens, onetime coal town (M)
news.title: French Far Right Makes Headway in Battle for Left's Onetime Northern Stronghold

news.abstract: British defense secretary Geoff Hoon reports worrisome increase in Iraq's efforts to shoot down American and British warplanes patrolling two no-flight zones over its territory, after significant lull immediately after Sept 11; declines to say if attempts to shoot down allied warplanes are being matched by any other kind of war footing in Iraq; emphasizes importance of allowing United Nations weapons inspectors back into Iraq with freedom to roam nation; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld has expressed skepticism about ability of international arms monitors to puncture disinformation, decoys and denials from Pres Saddam Hussein (M)
news.title: Iraq Is Said to Step Up Attacks on Allied Jets

news.abstract: MYANMAR: 9 Opposition Members Freed ; CHINA: Death Sentence For Cover-up
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Northern IRELAND: A Sinn Fein Lord Mayor ; IRELAND: A New Opposition Leader ; YUGOSLAVIA: Amnesty For Albanian Rebels ; MACEDONIA: Ex-guerrillas Enter Politics ; Czech REPUBLIC: Ex-mayor To Fight Corruption.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: With Afghanistan's grand council set to convene next week, there has never been a moment with more promise — or long-term danger — for Afghan women.
news.title: Half the Afghans, the Women, Fight to Establish Their Rights

news.abstract: Israeli troops charged into Yasir Arafat's compound today leaving the Palestinian leader's position more shaky than ever.
news.title: A Defiant Arafat Emerges From Compound After Israeli Attack

news.abstract: France's two-stage parliamentary vote starts June 9; when completed, women's share of seats is unlikely to exceed the 55 of 555 seats they gained in last parliamentary election, in 1997, despite law passed in 2000 that called on political parties to ensure that 50 percent of all election candidates be women; politically active women note that France was among last European nations to give women the vote, in 1944; say women who are picked as candidates are frequently sent to contest districts where their parties have little or no chance of success; photo (M)
news.title: French Politics Finds Little Room for Women

news.abstract: Three Afghan women arrive in New York for meetings with American foundations, law firms and Bar Assn of City of New York; they are seeking help because, they say, newly won women's freedoms in Afghanistan are already under threat; say women must take part in writing country's Constitution if they are to achieve protection; three women belong to Afghan Women Lawyers and Professionals Assn, which emerged in Jan from four years underground; group has trained 40 women in basic human rights and wants to send dozens more across Afghanistan to explain to women in towns and rural villages about evolution of political life and how they can work to ensure that developments work to their advantage; Afghanistan's ground council convenes next week and it will select writers of new Constitution (M)
news.title: Half the Afghans, the Women, Fight to Establish Their Rights

news.abstract: Latest suicide bombing and Israeli reprisal raids elicit strong and familiar condemnations from senior Bush administration officials, but they also insist that events will not deter them from discussing new proposals for peace with Pres Hosni Mubarak of Egypt this weekend and Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel when he arrives day later; Bush and his national security adviser Condoleezza Rice are said to be leaning toward notion of outlining parameters or timetable for final peace settlement that would follow lines of proposals under discussion before negotiations broke down; international pressure for presidential response expected to intensify after Bush's meetings with Mubarak and Sharon (M)
news.title: White House Is Working To Nail Down Mideast Plan

news.abstract: Refugee resettlement groups say that because of security concerns, refugee admissions to US since Sept 11 have slowed to trickle, even as number of civilians fleeing war worldwide inches up; says result is refugees languishing in crowded, foul and sometimes unsafe camps overseas; Bush administration set at 70,000 number of refugees it would admit in current fiscal year, which began last Oct 1; so far, fewer than 14,000 have been allowed to enter (M)
news.title: Refugees Languishing in Camps as the U.S. Admits Many Fewer

news.abstract: Germany's Free Democratic Party leader Guido Westerwelle engineers resignation of Jamal Karsli, party politician who compared Israel's tactics in West Bank to 'Nazi methods'; Westerwelle does not fire his deputy Jurgen Mollemann, who had recruited Karsli and who most offended Germany's Jewish Organizations when he said that Jewish leader Michel Friedman inspired anti-Semitism by his behavior; rivals to Free Democrats, party hoping to gain balance of power after Sept 22 national elections, charge Westerwelle and Mollemann with cynical politicking among right wing in Germany by playing anti-Israel and anti-Semitic themes (M)
news.title: Small German Party Tries to Calm Uproar Over Slurs About Jews

news.abstract: Informal grouping of 33 countries from Europe, Latin America and Pacific meet in Paris and urge new measures to prevent spread of chemical and biological weapons (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Accord Against Bioweapons

news.abstract: At least three people die, including attacker, and four more are wounded when two Palestinian gunmen attack heavily guarded Karmei Tzur Jewish settlement in West Bank; attack comes on eve of US visit by Prime Min Ariel Sharon and day after Israeli forces swept into Palestinian-controlled towns in search of wanted militants; Israeli government steps up diplomatic and public relations offensive against Yasir Arafat; charge him with failing to stop terrorist attacks; Arafat urges Bush administration to move quickly toward international peace conference for Middle East (M)
news.title: On Eve of Sharon's U.S. Visit, 2 Settlers Are Killed in Raid

news.abstract: News analysis of death of American missionary Martin Burnham during rescue attempts by Filipino forces after kidnapping by Abu Sayyaf rebels more than year ago; American military experts and lawmakers question whether outcome may have been different if mission involved American soldiers, who trained Filipino rangers but were not allowed to play direct combat role in rescue; incident illustrates limitations on US military might and painful trade-offs required to keep important allies in global campaign against terrorism; photo (M)
news.title: A Painful Consequence Of Political Constraints

news.abstract: Pakistani court bows to public outrage and frees Zafran Bibi, rape victim sentenced to death by stoning for crime of having extramarital relations; she leaves prison in Islamabad with seven-month-old daughter conceived when husband was in prison and described by judge as proof of her crime; was prosecuted after accusing brother-in-law of raping her; human rights groups say as many as half of women who report rape are charged with breaking Islamic law, which forbids any sexual contact outside of marriage; photo (M)
news.title: Sentenced to Death, Rape Victim is Freed by Pakistani Court

news.abstract: First gay pride parade is held in Jerusalem over loud protests from Orthodox Jewish politicians and some demonstrators, who condemn it as celebration of sin; photo (M)
news.title: Gays in Jerusalem Parade Their Pride

news.abstract: Jacques Diouf, head of United Nations Food and Agriculture Orgn, says development experts mesmerized by international trade and high technology must tackle poverty first; says 815 million people go to sleep hungry, and when officials from 183 nations meet in Rome June 10, they should reassess world food situation; his organization estimates that poor countries are falling $30 billion a year short of $180 billion needed to meet targets for cutting hunger that were set at world food summit meeting in 1996 (M)
news.title: U.N. Official Urges Food Aid For the Poor As a Priority

news.abstract: Pres Bush says United States must start working immediately with Israelis and Palestinians toward establishing Palestinian state in Middle East, but that he is not prepared to recommend timetable for state's creation; makes remarks in joint news conference at Camp David with Pres Hosni Mubarak of Egypt, who in his opening statement calls for 'agreed time frame' leading to establishment of state; Bush, who will meet at White House with Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel on June 10, says institutions necessary for emergence of Palestinian state must be built before deadline for state could be set; Bush and Mubarak offer differing views of Yasir Arafat, with Mubarak saying he should be given chance to reform Palestinian Authority, and Bush speaking of need to reach out to newer Palestinian leaders; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Urges Immediate Work on Palestinian State

news.abstract: Swiss police detain Bernard Lasnaud, French arms dealer, at request of Argentine government, whose interest in him arises from scandals involving former Pres Carlos Saul Menem; Argentine officials complain that their repeated requests to United States to detain Lasnaud, who lives in Florida, have been ignored for more than four years; former Justice Dept officials say exceptions to such requests are sometimes made for people who help US government (M)
news.title: Argentina Says U.S. Refused to Detain a Wanted Arms Dealer

news.abstract: The soldiers from Alpha Company have been in Afghanistan for six months, and can now count on one page of the calendar the days before they go home.
news.title: For Company A, War Is Nearly Over but Many G.I.'s See Afghan Mission as Not Quite Completed

news.abstract: Division of 10,000 South Korean troops is placed on alert in and around city of Taegu as South Korean and American athletes prepare to face each other in crucial match in World Cup soccer tournament; American military police offices are expected to patrol stadium on day of match, which many Koreans see as epic encounter in which national pride is at stake; danger of angry reaction by fans to unfavorable calls by referees or scores against Korean team is such that Pres Kim Dae Jung decides not to attend match (M)
news.title: Korean Troops Are on Alert For World Cup

news.abstract: Residents of southern Sudan are adopting new ways of doing business, forced by 20 years of civil war that has devastated economy and left country without banking system or currency; goats are currency of choice in money-scarce Korongo, remote village in Nuba Mountains; map; photo (M)
news.title: Korongo Journal; Amid War, 4-Legged Cash and Dreams of Tourism

news.abstract: Military cooperation between US and India has increased remarkably since September 11 terrorist attacks to level almost unimaginable for most of past three decades; is underscored by burst of army, navy and air force joint exercises, revival of American military sales and blur of high-level visits by generals and admirals; India, for decades champion of nonalignment, seeks warmer ties with US in hopes of gaining access to sophisticated military technology and help in dealing with Pakistan over disputed territory of Kashmir; US hopes deeper military and political ties will give it measure of leverage to prevent war between both countries that could lead to nuclear holocaust and play havoc with hunt for Al Qaeda terrorists in Pakistan; upcoming visit of Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld discussed; photos (M)
news.title: Wider Military Ties With India Offer U.S. Diplomatic Leverage

news.abstract: Outdoor broadcast of World Cup soccer match turns into drunken rampage outside Kremlin after Russian team loses to Japan; hundreds of rioters destroy dozens of autos and scores of storefronts and injure perhaps 100 people; 11 law enforcement officers reportedly are wounded; photo (M)
news.title: 100 Are Hurt As Soccer Loss Leads to Riot In Moscow

news.abstract: Israeli troops and tanks continued the sweep of Ramallah, the de facto Palestinian capital in the West Bank, that began early this morning.
news.title: Pressure on Arafat Builds; Israelis Make More Arrests

news.abstract: Soldiers of US Army's Company A, which operates out of Bagram Air Base in Afghanistan, are returning home after six-month tour of duty; many look forward to reunions with families while others feel their mission is not quite complete; some comment; map; photo (M)
news.title: For Company A, War Is Nearly Over

news.abstract: Defense Secretary Donald H. Rumsfeld arrived in New Delhi today for meetings with senior Indian officials, sounding a hopeful note about the outlook for reduced tensions between Pakistan and India.
news.title: Rumsfeld Sounds Optimistic Note as He Arrives in India for Talks

news.abstract: President Bush will soon give a more specific vision for creation of a Palestinian state, Secretary of State Colin L. Powell said today.
news.title: Powell Says Details of a Palestinian State Will Come Soon

news.abstract: Annual survey by South Africa's Health Ministry suggests number of HIV infections have leveled off at about one-quarter of adult population; epidemiologists estimate 4.74 million people, out of population of 44 million, are currently infected--still largest number of adults of any country in world; graph (M)
news.title: H.I.V. Survey in South Africa Suggests Plateau in Infections

news.abstract: Pres Bush meets with Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon at White House and says time is not ripe for Mideast peace summit since 'no one' has confidence in emerging Palestinian government; comes close to endorsing Sharon's position, echoing his skepticism about conducting political talks with Palestinians until there is significant reform of Palestinian Authority; says Authority under Yasir Arafat is incapable o engaging in political talks administration has assured Arab leaders will be conducted simultaneously with security talks; suggests Arafat's reorganization of Cabinet did not solve problem of finding Palestinian partner; meeting at Camp David 48 hours earlier with Egyptian Pres Hosni Mubarak, who gave opposite advice and pressed for timeline for establishment of Palestinian state, noted; Israeli tanks surround Arafat's compound in Ramallah on West Bank; security forces arrest 27 Palestinians suspected of being militants; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Sees Sharon and Says Time Isn't Ripe for Peace Conference

news.abstract: Secretary General Kofi Annan opened a United Nations conference on hunger by urging a fairer distribution of food supplies and support for farmers. ''While some countries produce more than they need to feed their people,'' he said in Rome, ''others do not, and many of these cannot afford to import enough to make up the gap.'' Most speakers on the first day were African heads of state who called for removal of barriers to farm trade with developed countries and greater access by farmers in poorer nations to land, cheap loans, and technology for producing hardier crops. Mr. Annan, who is from Ghana, said that almost 200 million people in Africa, or 28 percent of the population, are chronically hungry, and that several countries in southern Africa face ''outright famine'' in coming months.   John Tagliabue (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: Annan Opens Food Conference

news.abstract: Manzoorabad Journal on plight of Pakistan's bonded laborers and their families, who get high-interest loans from employers, often brickmakers, and then must labor to pay off ever-mounting debt; photo; map; practice, particularly bonded child labor, is illegal but law is rarely if ever enforced; US human rights report, putting number at several million workers, says strong social ties between employers and public officials at local level undercut law (M)
news.title: Manzoorabad Journal; Bondage's Load: Heavy Bricks, and Crushing Debt

news.abstract: Nine more North Koreans sneak into South Korean diplomatic building in Beijing, bringing number of new asylum seekers to 17(S)
news.title: 9 More North Koreans Seek Asylum in Seoul Embassy in Beijing

news.abstract: Pres Fidel Castro calls for massive marches by Cubans to protest Bush administration's hard-line policies (S)
news.title: Castro Calls March Against Bush's Criticism

news.abstract: Palestinian blows himself up in restaurant in Israeli coastal town of Herzliya, killing 15-year-old girl and wounding eight other people; photo; map; Palestinians report boy and man killed by army gunfire near Jewish settlement in Gaza; army reports three gunmen shot; Arab gunmen in Hebron kill two fellow Palestinians suspected of being informers; Israeli forces carry out fresh sweeps in Ramallah, arresting Abdel Rahim Mallouh, deputy chief of Popular Front for Liberation of Palestine (M)
news.title: Palestinian Suicide Bomber Kills a Girl and Wounds 8

news.abstract: Controversy over speeding up payments to Holocaust victims through Claims Resolution Council further delays disbursement of money from $1.25-billion settlement with Swiss banks over war-era accounts; tribunal supervisor Paul A Volcker explains (S)
news.title: Holocaust Payments by Swiss Delayed Further by New Approach

news.abstract: Egypt arrests Islamic Group co-founder Salah Hashem and another group member; Hashem had been one of main supporters of cease-fire announced by militant group (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: Muslim Leader Arrested

news.abstract: Li Lan, villager in China's Hunan Province who has crusaded against corruption and lawlessness in countryside, is arrested on charge of malicious slander of local officials; photo (M)
news.title: Critic of Corruption in Rural China Is Arrested in a Crackdown

news.abstract: Pakistan officials say several men believed to be American citizens have been taken into custody during past few weeks on suspicion of being linked to Al Qaeda; say most were picked up along with other suspected Al Qaeda and Taliban members in joint American-Pakistani raids in country's remote tribal areas near border with Afghanistan; say they believe that men form disjointed network of disaffected Westerners who converted to Islam and have been drawn to militant causes; one man, who goes by name Ahmed Muhammad or single name Benjamin and claims to be American citizen, is believed to be associate of Jose Padilla, American-born man detained last month on suspicion that he was trying to build radiation dispersal bomb intended for detonation in United States; report they have picked up about 400 suspected members of Al Qaeda and Taliban in sweeps around country since December, about 300 of whom have been turned over to American authorities; say some of men recently detained and believed to be Americans may have studied under radical Islamic cleric Mufti Muhammad Iltimas, to whom John Walker Lindh and Richard C Reid may also have had link; also say they have confirmed that unidentified American convert to Islam was killed while fighting alongside Muslim guerrillas in Kashmir; map (M)
news.title: Pakistan Holds Terror Suspects; Cites U.S. Ties

news.abstract: First day of open debate in loya jirga, or grand council, to select Afghanistan's transitional government, is marked by raucous arguments among 1,551 delegates over wide variety of issues; more than half of agenda is postponed, including selection of head of state; photo (M)
news.title: Voices of Afghan Democracy, Loud and Unclear

news.abstract: Amnesty International representatives will meet with Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam leaders in Sri Lanka for first time to discuss their recruitment of child soldiers and need to let Muslims they have expelled return to north; will discuss with government its alleged failure to effectively prosecute soldiers and policemen who kill or rape civilians (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Sri Lanka: Rights Group To Meet Rebels

news.abstract: Osaka explodes in frenzy when Japan beats Russia for its first ever World Cup soccer victory, scene that was repeated all over Japan; almost no one had predicted that normally subdued populace would be swept up in wild revelry, but Japan's affection for soccer, which began tentatively decade ago, has turned into head-over-heels love affair that reflects deep-seated generational changes; map; photos (Osaka Journal) (M)
news.title: Osaka Journal; Oh-So-Sober Japan, Suddenly Drunk on Soccer

news.abstract: Russian court refuses to halt treason trial of Oleg D Kalugin, former KGB general living in United States; he is accused of disclosing state secrets from Soviet era; has refused to appear in Russia to defend himself (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Treason Trial To Continue

news.abstract: Amnesty International reports 213 people were executed in Egypt in past decade compared with 35 in previous one; scores 21-year-old emergency law, state security courts and military trials for Islamic militants; 67 militants have been executed since 1992 (S)2
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: Number Of Executions Jumps

news.abstract: Correction of June 13 article comparing features of four megapixel digital cameras, which misstated battery life of some models
news.title: Corrections

news.abstract: Correction: two picture credits with Critic's Notebook article about new international piano competition misspelled name of the photographer; she is Dawn Villella
news.title: Corrections

news.abstract: Lower house of German Parliament votes to tighten gun laws; move comes on heels of school massacre on Apr 26 in city of Erfurt, where former student shot and killed 16 people, then himself; upper house is expected to ratify decision (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Gun Law Vote

news.abstract: Irene Njoroge, cosmetologist in Nairobi, Kenya, campaigns against skin-lightening cream, product that has become essential part of many African women's beauty routines, and big business, too; says women are being exploited by irresponsible beauty manufacturers who are cashing in on common perception in Africa that lighter one's skin, wealthier, better educated and more attractive one is; notes that labels on skin-whitening agents fail to disclose potentially harmful, sometimes fatal, effects of creams; her organizaiton, called Beauty Without Danger, conducts neighborhood tours to document extent of problem to Kenyan authorities; photo (M)
news.title: Fighting 'Light Skin' as a Standard of Beauty

news.abstract: Stated mission of 160 American Special Forces soldiers in Philippines is to train Philippine soldiers to fight dwindling band of Abu Sayyaf rebels who have operated on island of Basilan; American forces are playing equally important role in mending roads, drilling wells and clearing airstrip for cargo planes; goal is to improve life for 300,000 residents of island in one of poorest parts of country, and hopefully to help dry up popular support for Abu Sayyaf (M)
news.title: By Aiding Needy Filipinos, G.I.'s Could Help Rout the Rebels

news.abstract: State Department asks Iceland's government why it ordered state airline, Icelandair, to refuse passage to American citizens who appear on list of followers of Falun Gong spiritual movement; Amb Jon Baldvin Hannibalsson of Iceland, in Washington, says his government does not want protests to interfere with visit this week of Pres Jiang Zemin of China, country that has branded Falun Gong as 'evil cult' (M)
news.title: Iceland Bars American Falun Gong Followers

news.abstract: Huge car bomb explodes outside American Consulate in Karachi, Pakistan, killing at least 11 people and wounding at least 26 in most vivid demonstration yet of expanding terror campaign aimed at foreigners and government of Pres Pervez Musharraf; none of those killed are believed to be Americans, but five of those wounded worked inside heavily fortified building; police suspect bomb was set off by remote control and that occupants of car were themselves killed; this is second car-bomb attack in Karachi in less than month; level of destruction and sophistication in bombings may point to links between local militant groups and rogue members of Al Qaeda who have infiltrated Pakistan after being routed from Afghanistan; previously unknown group, Al Qanoon, claims responsibility for bombing, but investigators suspect same militants who went underground after government crackdown have regrouped and taken new name; Pres Bush calls attack work of 'radical killers' and pledges to 'hunt them down, and seek justice'; privately, Bush's aides voice concern that bombings are sign that Musharraf's power is eroding; photos; map (M)
news.title: CAR BOMB EXPLODES OUTSIDE U.S. OFFICE IN A PAKISTANI CITY

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook gives sidelights of Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld's visit to Persian Gulf area, and Asian subcontinent (M)
news.title: Reporter's Notebook; On Tour With Rumsfeld, the Jacket Stays On and the Monkeys Stay Away

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair and his Irish counterpart, Bertie Ahern, order emergency talks with political parties in Northern Ireland over rising violence and deepening political distrust in province (S)
news.title: Ulster Violence Prompts a Call For Crisis Talks

news.abstract: Toronto, Canada's premier city for business and finance, is showing signs of fraying, even while Canada's economy is strong, property values are rising and housing construction is booming for rich and upper middle class; poor have been left behind in otherwise bustling housing market; city officials estimate that 6,000 people are now homeless in Toronto; photos; maps (M)
news.title: Amid Prosperity, Toronto Shows Signs of Fraying

news.abstract: Israel is set to build 225-mile security fence to wall off Palestinians on West Bank from Israel proper; it is a measure of fear that what year ago might have seemed an unlikely idea is now wildly popular among Israelis, though not all of them; settlers and some right-wing Israelis oppose fence, and Palestinians are uniformly against it; photos; map (M)
news.title: On Old Green Line, a Fence and Fears Are Rising

news.abstract: Czech voters reject comeback bid by their contentious former prime minister, Vaclav Klaus, opting apparently for less confrontation in politics and smooth road toward joining European Union; voters choose to keep in power center-left Social Democrats, whose new leader, Vladimir Spidla, campaigned on greatly increased spending and quick accession to European Union; photos (M)
news.title: Czech Voters Block Return of Center-Right Ex-Leader

news.abstract: Pres Bush reportedly directs top national security aides to make doctrine of pre-emptive action against states and terrorist groups trying to develop weapons of mass destruction into foundation of new national security strategy; policy represents significant move away from chesslike military strategies of cold war, dealing more broadly with range of options to prevent nations from obtaining large-scale weapons or sponsoring terrorism; is being fine-tuned to make it clear that US has options beyond armed intervention, such as joint operations with Russia and other powers; potential targets include weak states that have become incubators for terrorist groups; Iraq is clearly first on target list for such action; CIA and Defense Department have stepped up efforts to unseat Saddam Hussein in last effort to avoid necessity of full-scale invasion; photo (M)
news.title: BUSH TO FORMALIZE A DEFENSE POLICY OF HITTING FIRST

news.abstract: A Palestinian suicide bomber blew himself up today in the West Bank area where Israel is building its new security fence, and two other Palestinian fighters were killed.
news.title: Palestinian Blows Himself Up Near Site of West Bank Fence

news.abstract: Padre Pio, Capuchin friar who for 50 years was said to have borne bleeding wounds of Jesus and whose worldwide following blends medieval piety with modern celebrity cult, is canonized at Vatican in solemn Mass celebrated by Pope John Paul II; one of largest crowds in memory packs St Peter's Square; photos (M)
news.title: Vatican City Journal; The Friar, Miraculously, Marches Into Sainthood

news.abstract: Radio Sawa, new radio station established by US government, beams news and music to youth throughout Arab world to counteract anti-American diatribes on Middle East airwaves (M)
news.title: U.S. Messages to Arab Youth, Wrapped in Song

news.abstract: Many Mexicans say biggest law enforcement problem is corrupt police force; efforts to correct problem, declared one of highest priorities by Pres Vicente Fox, is becoming epic struggle; even though government has made significent progress, states and cities report little measurable improvement (M)
news.title: Mexico Begins to Wade Through Morass of Police Corruption

news.abstract: Israeli forces raided the West Bank late Tuesday after a Palestinian suicide bomber launched the worst attack in Jerusalem in six years.
news.title: Israeli Forces Raid West Bank After Suicide Bomber Kills 19

news.abstract: The Bush administration disclosed today that two American citizens of Afghan origin were detained in Pakistan last month.
news.title: Bush Administration Says Two Americans Detained in Pakistan

news.abstract: PAKISTAN: Ready To Match An Indian Pullback; PHILIPPINES: Gunmen Fire At U.S. Troops; CHINA: More North Koreans Seek Asylum; HONG KONG: Falun Gong Members On Trial; INDONESIA: Police Kill Separatist Rebels;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Czech Republic Pres Vaclav Havel asks center-left leader Vladimir Spidla to form government as concern grows that center-left coalition might not be strong enough to push through reforms needed to take country into European Union; Spidla's ruling Social Democrats finished first in June 14 parliamentary elections, taking 30 percent of vote and winning 70 seats in 200-seat lower house (M)
news.title: Center-Left Leader in Prague Is Asked to Form Government

news.abstract: Death of American journalist Larry Lee remains unsolved two-and-a-half years after he was murdered in apartment in Guatemala City, Guatemala; despite increasing pressure from US, his family in Missouri still has no idea who killed him as Guatemalan investigators have barely pressed inquiry, overlooking important evidence and letting trail to suspects go cold; killing is example of justice system in which justice is rarely done; unsolved killings of at least seven other Americans in Guatemala noted; list; photos (M)
news.title: An American's Death Bares Guatemalan Blunders

news.abstract: United States aide Richard S Williamson warns Security Council meeting on renewing mandate of international forces in Bosnia that Americans will not take part in United Nations peacekeeping missions unless council grants them immunity from prosecution by new International Criminal Court; diplomats do not expect US to block extension of Bosnia force, especially since it is essentially NATO operation with UN endorsement; see bid to press council, especially Britain and France, to explicity exempt UN peacekeepers from prosecution before court comes into being July 1; US efforts to deny court jurisdiction over Americans serving abroad has become symbol of what many at UN see as Bush administration challenge to idea of universal legal system (M)
news.title: U.S. Links Peacekeeping to Immunity From New Court

news.abstract: Philippine military reports operation to rescue two Americans and Filipino held by Muslim group Abu Sayyaf was 'meticulously' planned for over six months; American Martin Burnham and Filipino Ediborah Yap died in effort (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Philippines: Report On Hostage Rescue Effort

news.abstract: Saudi Arabia, after denying for months that any Al Qaeda members might be lurking in kingdom, reports arresting some months ago six Saudi and one Sudanese member of terrorist network it believes tried to down United States military aircraft with shoulder-fired missile; reports arresting second group of five Saudis and an Iraqi for hiding Sudanese man, alleged ringleader, and helping him to escape to Sudan, where he was arrested and returned to Saudi Arabia (M)
news.title: Saudi Arabia Arrests 13 Men Tied to Attack on a U.S. Base

news.abstract: Military officials say probe found Air National Guard pilot Major Harry Schmidt, who mistakenly dropped bomb on Canadian soldiers conducting nighttime live-fire exercise in Afghanistan in Apr, and pilot of second plane broke procedures by not taking time to assess threat properly; say Schmidt thought he was under attack from ground when he dropped bomb that killed four Canadians and wounded eight; say warning from radar plane that potential frendlies were in area came seconds too late; say inquiry found second pilot, Maj William Umbach, failed to exercise leadership (M)
news.title: Inquiry on Canadians' Deaths Says U.S. Pilots Broke Rules

news.abstract: THE HAGUE: Delay In Milosevic'S Trial; GERMANY: Convictions In Attack On Foreigners; CZECH REPUBLIC: Agreement On New Government; FRANCE: JuppÉ Rises On Chirac'S Coattails;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Two teenage boys have been arrested and charged with intentionally setting the fire that killed 24 last weekend in an unlicensed Internet cafe.
news.title: 2 Boys Charged With Setting Fatal Fire at a Beijing Internet Cafe

news.abstract: Russia is moving to dismantle collectivization of its farmlands; Parliament's lower house, urged by Pres Vladimir V Putin, has approved preliminary bill to create legal system to buy and sell agricultural lands and is expected to adopt slightly amended version; Communist and Agrarian parties, regional leaders and privatization opponents are threatening to block effort; collectives still run over 90 percent of farms; farmers fear repeat of earlier corrupted privatizations that gave control of former state enterprises to richest oligarchs; map; photo (M)
news.title: Russia Seeking to Dismantle Collective Farms

news.abstract: Asylum seekers are finding Europe has grown deaf to their plight; European Union leaders are set to meet to discuss steps to tighten borders to combat illegal immigration amid rising anti-immigrant sentiment; new Danish laws that make it clear immigrants are no longer welcome in nation once proud of its openness cited; politicians across Europe are under pressure from voters to adopt policies at least as tough as neighbors'; photo (M)
news.title: When Asylum Seekers Knock, Europe Is Deaf

news.abstract: Pres Bush announces $500 million plan to prevent pregnant women from passing AIDS virus to their babies and reduce number of infected babies by 40 percent in dozen African nations and Caribbean; new money, which includes $200 million already set aside by Congress, will provide treatment to million women a year over five years; reaction among advocates for people with AIDS is mixed, with some praising Bush and others holding plan falls short of global needs (M)
news.title: Bush Offers Plan to Help Mothers Avoid Passing H.I.V. to Babies

news.abstract: Second Palestinian suicide bomber strikes Jerusalem, killing six people at bus stop, even as Israel implements policy of taking back West Bank land in retaliation for attacks; Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat condemns both bombings; new bombing apparently spurs series of Israeli military actions, reportedly including helicopter gunship attacks in Gaza Strip and fierce firefight in Qalqilya; Israel, responding to first bombing, moved trailer houses into Jenin, shut city down in curfew and rounded up hundreds of Palestinians; map; photo (M)
news.title: JERUSALEM BLAST KILLS SIX ISRAELIS; ARMY RAIDS START

news.abstract: Noa Alon, 60, and her granddaughter Gal, five, killed on Israeli bus by Palestinian suicide bomber, are buried together; photos; retired teacher had returned to direct year-end kindergarten concert in which Gal performed; child's mother and baby brother were injured in attack that took seven lives (S)
news.title: More Tears in a Land of Mourning

news.abstract: HONG KONG:—  Hong Kong legislators have voted to approve the most sweeping changes to the territory's government structure since China resumed sovereignty over the former British colony five years ago.
news.title: Political appointees to replace 14 senior civil servants : Hong Kong realigns government
