news.abstract: China's villagers are using inexpensive prenatal scans and then abortion in greater numbers than ever to prevent birth of unwanted daughters and ensure they will have sons; recent studies and census data show gap between male and female births has only widened in last decade, giving China largest gender disparity in world; imbalance in some rural areas is staggering 144 boys for every 100 girls born; China's overall figure is 117 to 100, compared with 105 to 100 in US; photo; map; graph; example is southeastern region of Chaoyang, where daughters move away to husband's families, government no longer provides even pretense of old-age or medical care, and people depend on sons (M)
news.title: Desire for Sons Drives Use of Prenatal Scans in China

news.abstract: German Pres Johannes Rau signs immigration law that significantly expands residence permits available to workers from countries outside the European Union, at a time when countries across Continent are moving toward tightening borders (S)
news.title: Germany Eases Restrictions On Workers From Abroad

news.abstract: The man accused of organizing the kidnapping and slaying of Daniel Pearl told a court today that the case against him was a jumble of lies.
news.title: Prosecution Completes Case in Trial of Slain Reporter

news.abstract: World Health Orgn declares Europe free of polio (S)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: Europe Declared Free Of Polio

news.abstract: On moving to Paris, personal safety was the least of my concerns — I considered myself city savvy having lived in London for five years. Had I known that I would be sexually assaulted on a Paris Metro platform, I might have been a little less cavalier.
news.title: Dangerous locations : Security risks often underrated

news.abstract: Ahmed Omar Sheikh, man accused of organizing kidnapping and murder of Wall Street Journal reporter Daniel Pearl in Pakistan, tells court in Karachi that case against him is jumble of lies and faked evidence concocted by government to please United States; says he never met Pearl, was in another city when he was kidnapped and had nothing to do with menacing e-mail messages that threatened reporter's death; Sheikh faces possible death sentence, along with three men who are accused of helping him send e-mail messages; authorities say they have detained six more men with possible connections to case since exhuming body believed to be that of Pearl (M)
news.title: Defendant in Pearl's Death Says Evidence Was Faked

news.abstract: Government of Ireland sends potassium iodide tablets to households across country for use in case Ireland is exposed to radioactive fallout from terror attack or accident at British nuclear reprocessing plant at Sellafield, across Irish Sea (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ireland: Antiradiation Pills For Everyone

news.abstract: YUGOSLAVIA: Ex-Tv Boss Jailed Over Nato Bombing; GERMANY: Antiviolence Measures; RUSSIA: Treason Trial Concludes; IRELAND: Antiradiation Pills For Everyone.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Expo.02, which is set at four lakeside locations in Switzerland, encourages Swiss to see themselves differently and pokes a little fun at some of country's foibles; two-thirds of country's 7.2 million people say they plan to attend (M)
news.title: No Taboos at Swiss Expo, Where Even Money Gets Shredded

news.abstract: Prime Min Jean Chretien of Canada will press other Group of 8 leaders at coming meeting in Kananaskis to forge new strategy to assist Africa; will argue that wealthiest nations should increase their aid budgets for education, agriculture and fresh water, as well as helping to restructure government and legal institutions, combat AIDS and malaria, and encourage foreign investment in Africa; will also argue for dropping of trade barriers to African textiles, footwear and farm products (M)
news.title: Chrétien Is Hoping to Aid Africa by Mobilizing Rich Nations

news.abstract: Severe hunger is sweeping across southern Africa as result of two years of alternating droughts and floods, coupled with mismanagement of food supplies; Malawi, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Lesotho have been declared national disasters, and Mozambique and Swaziland are also struggling; United Nations expects four million people to need emergency aid in next few months as this season's meager harvest runs out; photos; map; graphs (L)
news.title: Meager Harvests in Africa Leave Millions at the Edge of Starvation

news.abstract: United Nations reports that most people in developing nations have now heard of AIDS but that significant number have only limited knowledge of how to avoid it; says most people surveyed in more than three dozen countries believe AIDS cannot strike them and, as a result, are not changing their sexual habits enough to meet threat; says there is relatively low incidence of AIDS in northern Africa, Middle East and parts of Asia with conservative Muslim populations with strong taboos about sexual behavior (M)
news.title: U.N. Finds AIDS Knowledge Still Lags in Stricken Nations

news.abstract: Israeli ground forces move into West Bank village of Dura after Israeli security cabinent endorses plan to seize and hold Palestinian-controlled territory in response to Palestinian attacks that have killed 33 Israelis in past week; army is now holding positions in at least five of eight major Palestinian cities and towns in West Bank; photo; map (M)
news.title: Israeli Military Advances Into More of the West Bank; Plans a 'Crushing' Response

news.abstract: Chile's nominally Socialist government will allow private sector to manage nation's unemployment insurance system, which will rely on market forces (M)
news.title: Chile Will Privatize a New Span of Its Noted Social Safety Net

news.abstract: HONG KONG:—  Lily Cheung, 24, spoke for herself and her boyfriend as they trawled the stores at the Pacific Place shopping mall, wearing skinny fit jeans with loose tops and searching for a bargain in the summer sales.
news.title: Hong Kong fashions, long known for glamour, turn casual

news.abstract: China permits 26 North Korean asylum seekers who have sought refuge in foreign diplomatic compounds in Beijing in last month to leave its territory for South Korea, ending weeks of diplomatic gridlock; is bound by treaty with old ally North Korea to repatriate asylum seekers, but has come under intense pressure by new allies South Korea and US, who vehemently and vocally oppose repatriation (M)
news.title: North Korean Asylum Seekers Leave China

news.abstract: American soldiers in Kunduz, Afghanistan, are on front lines of effort to rebuild country's infrastructure; are working with several other civil affairs teams, local officials and warlords to reconstruct schools, hospitals, roads and water systems ruined by two decades of war; map; photo (M)
news.title: G.I.'s Fight Afghan Devastation With Plaster and Nails

news.abstract: PHNOM PENH:—  When French commandos boarded the Cambodian-registered freighter Winner in international waters in the Atlantic this month amid an exchange of gunfire that wounded one of the 12 crew members, they seized more than a ton of cocaine in a cargo that was registered as scrap iron destined for Bilbao, Spain.
news.title: Cambodia-listed ship was carrying cocaine : Raid at sea highlights flag abuses

news.abstract: Arab world, hoping for detailed American proposal for peace and Palestinian state, finds Pres Bush's speech demanding ouster of Yasir Arafat as Palestinian leader before US can back establishment of Palestinian state short on specific timetable and long on demands for Palestinian reform; few Arabs believe Bush speech went far enough in offering kind of incentives needed to stem risisng violence and death toll on both sides (S)
news.title: President's Speech Is Criticized For Lacking Specific Proposals

news.abstract: Trial of two retired Salvadoran generals in two-decade-old torture case opens in West Palm Beach, Fla, with witness singling out one as participant in brutal 24-day interrogation; Dr Juan Romagoza identifies Gen Carlos Eugenio Vides Casanova as being present during weeks in which he was tortured by members of El Salvador's military; federal civil suit against Vides and Gen Jose Guillermo Garcia, who have lived in USsince 1989, is second they have faced; were cleared of similar charges in October 2000 suit brought by relatives of four American church women who were raped and murdered by Salvadoran military in 1980 (M)
news.title: Victim Links Retired General To Torture in El Salvador War

news.abstract: New Quebec provincial law, which takes effect at end of June, will give gay and lesbian couples same full parental rights and obligations extended to heterosexual couples; is heralded by Canadian gay rights activists as most important advance for their cause since Netherlands in 2001 granted gay couples right to marry; is seen as another sign that rapid social change continues to sweep province that two generations ago was largely directed by Roman Catholic church; its provisions discussed; photo (M)
news.title: With a Quebec Law, Equality for Gay Parents

news.abstract: MILAN—  Highly fragmented, intensely specialized and still largely owned by the same families that started the businesses, Italy's textiles industry remains the most important component in fashion worldwide, supplying top designers with quality materials. But its continuing success may depend on whether it can resist the modern business mantra that says market economics, consolidation and vertical integration are essential to survive in a global marketplace.
news.title: Artisanal roots nurture industry built on integration : It all starts with the best textiles

news.abstract: INDIA: A Warning To Pakistan; INDIA: Support For Embattled Neighbor; HONG KONG: Leader Appoints New Team; KAZAKHSTAN: Law On Political Parties;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Afghanistan's women are determinedly entering traditional male domain of politics, moving quickly out of invisible status under Taliban rule and into visible, activist role; 200 women joined 1,400 male delegates at loya jirga and used that platform to tell Afghanistan that women want peace and reconstruction of their country; still, many outspoken women say they feel strong undertow of resistance to their return to public life and wonder how far women have to go to win equal rights; photos of Dr Sima Samar, elected deputy chairwoman of loya jirga, and Dr Massouda Jalal, first woman to be presidential candidate (M)
news.title: Afghan Women in Political Spotlight

news.abstract: Central Intelligence Agency Director George J Tenet has ordered American intelligence agencies to expand their use of satellite photography provided by private companies, freeing government's own satellites for more specialized and secretive work; order follows complaints from Air Force officials that bureaucratic tangles initially prevented American pilots from using advanced commercial satellite imagery for maps in bombing missions (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Instructs Spy Agencies to Use More Commercial Satellite Photos

news.abstract: Mont Blanc tunnel connecting France and Italy, closed three years ago after truck fire killed 39 people, reopens despite protests by thousands of residents and environmentalists; map (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Mont Blanc Tunnel Reopens

news.abstract: Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad of Malaysia says he will step down on Oct 25, 2003, after two decades in power; statement ends short drama that began when he abruptly announced few days ago that he was resigning, but was then convinced by party leaders to retract his statement; chooses Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, deputy prime minister, as his successor; photo
news.title: Malaysia's Prime Minister to Step Down After 2 Decades

news.abstract: Pres Mohammad Khatami says Iran will accept United States offer of aid for survivors of earthquake in northwestern section of country; offer was made through Switzerland since US and Iran do not have diplomatic relations (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Iran: U.S. Aid Offer Accepted

news.abstract: Bush administration's top trade and agricultural officials respond to rising chorus of foreign criticism of new American farm subsidies, dismissing complaints as unfounded or hypocritical attempts to maintain trade barriers (M)
news.title: U.S. Defends Its Farm Subsidies Against Rising Foreign Criticism

news.abstract: BELGIUM: Sharon War-Crimes Suit Dismissed; THE HAGUE: Skepticism About Milosevic; NORTHERN IRELAND: Effort To Ease Tensions; RUSSIA: Another Step Toward Private Farmland
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Judges trying Slobodan Milosevic on war-crimes charges order thorough medical checkup of Milosevic, whose claims of illness have forced delays in hearings and taken up time allotted to prosecution's case (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: The Hague: Skepticism About Milosevic

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority officially announce plans to hold elections for president and legislative offices in January as part of broad proposal for civic and security reform that stops short of Pres Bush's demand for Yasir Arafat's replacement; one Palestinian minister says Arafat will run again, while others say it is too early to predict who candidates will be; Hussam Khader, Palestinian legislators and one of Arafat's most passionate critics, says Bush's demand for Arafat's removal will keep him in power for years to come; photo (M)
news.title: Palestinian Authority Sets a January Vote

news.abstract: Israeli military keeps up pressure on West Bank, firing thousands of rounds into old British police station in Hebron in standoff with suspected Palestinian militants that has ground on now for two days; 130 people emerge from building, and 13 of them are arrested as terror suspects; Hebron standoff is one of few instances of violent resistance to Israel's new major military operations in West Bank; photo; graph of death toll in violence that began Sept 29, 2000: at least 550 Israelis and 1,600 Palestinians (M)
news.title: Palestinian Resistance at Hebron Offices Thins Out, but Army Standoff Continues

news.abstract: ARGENTINA: Strike After Death Of Protesters; CUBA: Socialism Forever, Assembly Declares;.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: UN issues stinging public criticism of China's lackluster efforts to face its rapidly accelerating epidemic of HIV infection and AIDS, saying country is on 'verge of a catastrophe' and could have largest number of infected people in world in few years; Science article makes same point; China puts number of infections at 800,000-1.5 million at end of 2001, but UN officials say privately there could be as many as 6 million cases already (S)
news.title: U.N. Publicly Chastises China for Inaction on H.I.V. Epidemic

news.abstract: Israeli troops pound Palestinian Authority offices in Hebron for third day, firing heavy machine guns and rockets from helicopters to dislodge 15 gunmen holed up inside; seven Palestinian cities remain shut down for fifth day; two Palestinians killed in clashes; Israeli troops storm Nablus jail used as security headquarters, taking about 20 Palestinians into custody; current action is direct response to attacks that killed 31 Israelis in three days; Israeli prosecutors charge Lebanese-born Israeli, son of Jewish mother and Muslim father, with spying for Hezbollah (S)
news.title: Israeli Forces Hit Palestinian Offices in Hebron in Effort to Dislodge Gunmen

news.abstract: Vowing never to return to capitalism, the National Assembly has voted unanimously that the country's socialist system is ''irrevocable.'' The vote Wednesday night was seen by opposition leaders as an effort to block a dissident movement calling for increased personal and political freedoms. President Fidel Castro also warned that he might cut Cuba's limited relations with the United States if Washington continued to support dissidents and human rights advocates on the island. American diplomats in Havana recently distributed hundreds of short-wave radios able to receive Radio Martí, the anti-Castro station financed by the United States.   David Gonzalez (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Cuba: Socialism Forever, Assembly Declares

news.abstract: China is rapidly strenthening economic presence across Asia, gobbling up foreign investment and chipping away at US position as region's economic engine, while assuring countries that it is offering cooperation, not competition; many countries have rushed to China's embrace, nimbly shifting economic alliances at time when US is making its own way through tentative economic recovery; analysts say China's thrust, more apparent with new WTO membership, begins inescapable process of replacing US as dominant power in Asia; note that China is already economic and political threat to Japan; examples include Indonesia, where Pres Megawati Sukarnoputri has buried age-old hostilities in hopes of getting $9 billion liquid natural gas contract to power industries of southern China; China is also grabbing much of new foreign investment in Asia, leaving once-glittering Thailand, South Korea and Singapore with but crumbs; graphs showing rising Chinese share of ASEAN trade (M)
news.title: China Emerges As Rival to U.S. In Asian Trade

news.abstract: Guatemalan health officials declare national alert against dengue fever after tallying 789 cases, Jan-May; urge people to clean homes to stop breeding mosquitoes that carry potentially fatal disease (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Guatemala: Fears Over Dengue Fever

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, concerned that his party continues to trail in polls behind conservative opponents led by Edmund Stoiber, seeks to associate himself with Germany's unexpectedly good showing in World Cup soccer championships; travels on Japanese Prime Min Junichiro Koizumi's plane from Group of 8 summit meeting in Canada to see Germans play Brazil in final, Yokohama; Germany has also chartered plane to take senior leaders and politicians to game; Stoiber will attend game and return home with team; Schroder is also trying to take initiative on more substantive issues; photo (M)
news.title: German Leader Hopes Soccer Will Lift His Standing in Polls

news.abstract: Canadian news organizations are not known for digging deeply into the closets of politicians to look for skeletons.    So eyebrows were raised earlier this month when The Ottawa Citizen, the capital's most prominent newspaper, published a scathing article accusing Prime Minister Jean Chrétien of unethical conduct in his business dealings. The article appeared the same day the newspaper ran an editorial calling on Mr. Chrétien to resign.
news.title: Canadian Press Freedom Questioned in Publisher's Firing

news.abstract: Police report deaths and injuries from guerrilla activity rose sharply in Northern Ireland in 2001 despite cease-fires by paramilitary groups; say most of 18 killings were by Protestant paramilitary groups, while Catholic and Protestant gangs were equally responsible for over 300 beatings by vigilante enforcers (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Northern Ireland: Sharp Rise In Violence

news.abstract: The presidents of Mexico and Central America today reiterated their commitment to a regional development plan aimed at stimulating their struggling economies as they ended a two-day summit meeting in the southern Mexican state of Yucatán.     The plan, proposed a year ago by President Vicente Fox of Mexico, calls on the leaders to commit public funds and to pursue private financing to build roads, airports, railways and energy installations across a region that is largely cut off from the advances of globalization. Plan Puebla-Panama is named for the new economic bloc that extends from the central Mexican state of Puebla to Panama.
news.title: Talks in Mexico Push Regional Growth

news.abstract: People of Lan Yu, small Taiwanese island, threaten to take drastic action unless government lives up to promise made 12 years ago to remove as many as 20,000 barrels of radioactive debris from Taiwan's nuclear reactor from island; barrels, which are cracking and coming apartment because of chemical reactions inside, are in seaside concrete trenches vulnerable to typhoons, earthquakes and rockslides; island's 3,000 people belong to Tao tribe, descended from Polynesian explorers; photo; map (M)
news.title: Nuclear Dump Disrupts a Peaceful Taiwan Island

news.abstract: Pres Bakili Muluzi of Malawi defends ban on political demonstrations and the issue that prompted them: constitutional amendment to eliminate presidential term limits and allow him to prolong his rule; church leaders, lawyers and university students say Muluzi, whom they revered for ending 30 years of dictatorship and expanding political freedom, has become biggest threat to nation's fledgling democracy; photo; map (M)
news.title: A Surprising Crackdown in Malawi

news.abstract: Pres Bush's decision to condition support for Palestinian state on removal of Yasir Arafat as its leader came late in drafting of policy speech and was influenced by last-minute Israeli intelligence report that Arafat was tied to another transfer of funds to members of Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, which claimed responsibillity for June 19 suicide bombing; Arab leaders and Mideast experts see new position as stalling tactic, putting US policy on hold while Arafat remains defiantly in place; Arab diplomats, who have praised Bush's commitment to Palestinian statehood and who have no illusions about Arafat's flaws, privately fear that months of American disengagement will only incite region's partisans to more violence (M)
news.title: With Time Running Out, Bush Shifted Mideast Policy

news.abstract: The writing of President Bush's speech asking the Palestinians to replace their leadership went through two dozen drafts before Mr. Bush expressed some irritation, saying he was being ''nuanced to death,'' as one adviser put it. Mr. Bush asked for a clear statement of whether Washington's disappointment with Yasir Arafat had grown so deep that the peace effort could not proceed while he held power.
news.title: How Bush Hardened His Tone on Mideast

news.abstract: Graduate Institute of International Studies in Geneva reports that recorded number of small arms around the world rose 16 percent in 2001, to 639 million; says number of such weapons, including handguns and rifles, owned by civilians rose by 25 percent, to 377 million; says US and Russia dominate manufacture of small arms (S)
news.title: Small Arms Proliferating, Study Finds

news.abstract: A Russian passenger airliner collided with a Boeing 757 cargo plane over southern Germany late Monday night, apparently killing everyone aboard both planes.
news.title: Scores Feared Dead as Two Jets Collide Over Southern Germany

news.abstract: Luis Echeverria, Mexico's president from 1970 to 1976, may be called to testify under oath before special commission about role in country's never-acknowledged 'dirty war' from late 1960's and early 1980's in which hundreds of leftists were tortured and killed; his denial of wrongdoing will be tested as special prosecutor begins formal investigation of thousands of newly opened files from country's disbanded secret police; government's own human rights commission says at least 275 people, or perhaps twice that number, died during illegal detention; privately examined secret police files and interviewed hundreds of witnesses and former officials before turning over sealed list containing names of 74 former government officials it holds responsible to Pres Vicente Fox; photos (M)
news.title: Mexico Secrets: Envelope Holds Ghosts of 70's

news.abstract: New International Criminal Court begins operations in The Hague over strong objections from Washington, ready to receive complaints about gross abuses of human rights anywhere in world; created by Treaty of Rome in 1998, court has jurisdiction over war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide; organizers say it is likely to be year before first trial takes place (M)
news.title: Without Fanfare or Cases, International Court Sets Up

news.abstract: US refuses to budge in its demand that American peacekeepers be exempted from new International Criminal Court by vetoing UN Security Council resolution extending peacekeeping mission in Bosnia, but later agrees to three-day extension; display of brinksmanship is sharpest demonstration to date of Bush administration's determination to preclude any possibility that new court, which formally comes into being on July 1, could be used to prosecute American peacekeepers; other members of Security Council, most notably Britain and France, have argued adamantly that court has ample safeguards against politically motivated prosecutions; have refused to allow council to alter rules to satisfy Washington; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Vetoes Bosnia Mission, Then Allows 3-Day Reprieve

news.abstract: Serbia's Ministry of Education closes 11th Belgrade Grammar School, formerly prestigious high school, because of widespread corruption among teachers and staff; former principal Vera Ivkovic, whose anticorruption campaign attracted government's attention, says it will be difficult to clean up nation's education system, neglected for years under Slobodan Milosevic's violent decade in power unless young people can be convinced that money and connections are not only passports to success; photo (M)
news.title: Belgrade Journal; Serbia Expels a School for Teaching Corruption

news.abstract: Pres Jiang Zemin of China delivers tough speech in Hong Kong to mark fifth anniversary of its transfer from British to Chinese rule; urges residents to be more loyal to 'motherland' (S)
news.title: On an Anniversary, Chinese Leader Tells Hong Kong to Be Loyal

news.abstract: Germans believe cost of living has increased ever since mark was replaced by euro, common collective currency of most of European Union, on January 1; embraced currency but were quickly embarrassed as it sank immediately below parity with dollar; few are heartened by fact that euro is again at rough parity; consider rise not function of euro's strength but dollar's weakness; photo (M)
news.title: Berlin Journal; Dear Euro, They Sigh (Not Fondly)

news.abstract: More than 100 million rural Chinese from Nanba area have migrated to cities, with more than half ending up in southern province of Guangdong and forming vast new urban underclass; seldom able to become legal residents, they are blamed for every social ill; many turn to sex trade as financial backstop, with their cheap labor fueling Guangdong's thriving economy, which accounts for half of China's gross domestic product; few reap any benefits, remaining unwanted outsiders for many years in strange and often hostile region; map; photo (M)
news.title: Migrants to Chinese Boom Town Find Hard Lives

news.abstract: Bolivian voters, frustrated with economic turbulence and grinding poverty, are supporting unusually diverse array of politicians in presidential balloting on July 7, shaking up traditional politics in country's most important election in 20 years of democracy; exit surveys give Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada, former president and pro-market reformer, razor-thin edge over Manfred Reyes Villa, populist former mayor of Cochabamba, country's third-largest city; voters also give unexpected support to Evo Morales, leftist leader of coca farmers who favors nationalizing private companies and often criticizes US for its involvement in Bolivian affairs (M)
news.title: Bolivian Congress to Decide Tight Presidential Election

news.abstract: South Korean Pres Kim Dae Jung wins Japanese support for stronger policy on North Korea, and South Korean Defense Min Kim Dong Shin asks American military authorities for permission to strike first if threatened by intruding ships; June 29 clash between North Korean and South Korean patrol boats in Yellow Sea, which left four South Koreans and estimated 30 North Koreans dead discussed; shootout is second worst naval clash between both countries since end of Korean War 50 years ago (M)
news.title: South Korea Wins Support From Japan On Sea Clash

news.abstract: Vandals attack synagogue and memorial to Holocaust victims in Czech Republic spa town of Karlovy Vary (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Czech Republic: Vandals Hit Jewish Sites

news.abstract: Yasir Arafat shakes up security services, removing Jibril Rajoub in West Bank and Ghazi Jibali in Gaza; Rajoub is considered by some Israeli and American officials as among most cooperative Palestinian leaders (S)
news.title: Arafat Replaces 2 Security Chiefs

news.abstract: Steve Fossett prepares to land his balloon in southern Australia after completing first nonstop solo flight around the world without a motor; journey covers 19,400 miles, all in Southern Hemisphere; photo of control crew in St Louis; photos of balloons landing in three of Fossett's five previous failures (M)
news.title: Balloonist, No Quitter, Circles the World Solo on His Sixth Attempt

news.abstract: Robert Waugh, Northumberland farmer whose pigs are thought to have starr
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Foot-And-Mouth Culprit Sentenced

news.abstract: Afghan government expresses dismay at reports that about 140 civilians were killed or wounded in US-led operation in south; Pres Hamid Karzai summons Lt Gen Dan K McNeill; White House expresses condolences, but Pentagon refuses to accept responsibility or explain fully what remains murky situation; officials say that Taliban might have used civilians as shields and that errant bomb from B-52 crashed into uninhabited hillside; gunship in same area attacked six locations after crew reported anti-aircraft fire; foreign minister Abdullah says about 40 people were killed, mostly at wedding in one of four villages hit; US flies four young children to military hospital; photo; troops have been looking for Taliban and Qaeda pockets in Dehrawud area, which includes home village of Mullah Muhammad Omar; US spokesman dismisses idea that firing was celebratory, saying crew felt aircraft was under sustained attack from ground (M)
news.title: Shocked Afghans Criticize U.S. Strike; Toll Is Some 40 Dead and 100 Wounded

news.abstract: INDIA: New Tension Over Kashmir; SOUTH KOREA: After Battle, Phone Deal Is Off.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: US agrees to another extension of United Nations peacekeeping mission in Bosnia without provision placing American peacekeepers beyond reach of new International Criminal Court; Sec Gen Kofi Annan, in letter to Sec of State Colin N Powell, argues that sort of politically motivated prosecution US fears is highly improbable, that Americans are putting entire UN peacekeeping system at risk and that proposed American provision 'flies in the face of treaty law' (M)
news.title: Washington Allows a 12-Day Extension For U.N. Peacekeeping Mission in Bosnia

news.abstract: Talks between two Koreas on opening mobile phone system in North's capital, Pyongyang, are suspended as result of June 29 naval shootout in Yellow Sea for which South blames North (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: After Battle, Phone Deal Is Off

news.abstract: Appeals court of International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda upholds acquittal of Ignace Bagilisema, former mayor of Mabanza, on charges of playing leading role in mass killings of 1994 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Rwanda: Genocide Acquittal Upheld

news.abstract: Once the ball has stopped rolling, and the Brazilians stop partying, we can begin to count the cost and the gains of World Cup 2002.
news.title: Who won the Cup?Korea and Ronaldo

news.abstract: Bush administration's effort to re-establish military ties with Indonesia, which has been curtailed for nearly decade because of its army's widespread human rights violations, has some unexpected support among Indonesians; many who suffered under military in past, and who are still critical of army for its continuing rights abuses, contend that best hope for eventually developing army whose conduct is appropriate for democracy is to send officers to schools in United States (M)
news.title: Some Indonesians Say U.S. Aid Could Promote Army Reforms

news.abstract: The pressure on the Pentagon to plan for a war on Iraq underscores the failure of diplomacy and covert operations to dislodge Saddam Hussein. News analysis, Page A6.
news.title: Pressure to Plan for War

news.abstract: NORTH KOREA: Warm Words Follow Bullets; INDONESIA: Taking Aim At Rebels;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Israel's outgoing army chief of staff said today that only the expulsion or replacement of the Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat might prompt an Israeli withdrawal from West Bank cities.
news.title: Israelis and Palestinians Settle Further Into Their Stalemate

news.abstract: TUNISIA: Trial For Attack Suspect'S Uncle; MALAWI: President Will Need New Job; NIGERIA: Crime-Fighting Aid From U.S.;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Malawi Parliament votes against eliminating term limit preventing Pres Bakili Muluzi from seeking third term; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Malawi: Term Limit Remains In Place

news.abstract: Move by Mexican Pres Vicente Fox to open to public vast archive of secret goverment security documents is providing catharsis to families of victims of 1970's 'dirty war' and sparking investigations of former presidents and cabinet ministers; many relatives of dead and missing remain skeptical that probes will lead to convictions of high-ranking officials; Martha Murillo de Gaxiola, whose 24-year-old son, Oscar, disappeared in February 1978, comments; photo; map (M)
news.title: Files Bare Dark Secrets of Mexico's Dirty War

news.abstract: Charred remains of Brazilian crime reporter Tim Lopes, who disappeared June 2 during undercover investigation into gangs that dominate squatter slums in Rio de Janeiro, are recovered from clandestine cemetery; Lopes reportedly was executed by local drug boss nicknamed Elias the Madman; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | The Americas: Brazil: Journalist's Remains Recovered

news.abstract: Longtime Madagascar leader Didier Ratsiraka flees with family to Seychelles Island as hostile troops close in on last remaining stronghold; Ratsiraka has been battling rival Marc Ravalomanana since bitterly contested December 2001 election; US and France have officially recognized Ravalomanana as president (M)
news.title: Longtime Madagascar Leader Flees as Rival Gains

news.abstract: Former SS officer Friedrich Engel, 93, is convicted in Hamburg of ordering killing of 59 Italian prisoners in May 1944; Judge Rolf Seedorf sentences Engel to seven years in prison but he is released pending results of health tests (M)
news.title: Former Nazi Convicted of Ordering Executions

news.abstract: Hajji Abdul Qadir, Afghan vice president, is assassinated in Kabul, and stability of Hamid Karzai's American-backed government is thrown into question; Qadir and his driver are shot outside his office by gunmen lurking nearby; gunmen escape and police, suspecting conspiracy, detain Qadir's entourage of bodyguards and seal off Kabul's main streets; Qadir, longtime warlord from eastern Afghanistan, was pivotal figure in government, largely because he was one of few Pashtuns to join Karzai in effort to unite country's major ethnic groups; government is dominated by minority Tajiks; photos (M)
news.title: Afghan Official Is Assassinated; Blow to Karzai

news.abstract: Switzerland is resisting pressure from other European governments to ferret out tax cheats, fearing it would frighten capital out of their banks; controversy has become public, with European ministers regularly rebuking Swiss for failing to sign European financial disclosure agreement; accord could fail entirely without Swiss involvement because country's banks control about $27 trillion of world's funds and handle third of all money transferred across European borders; 15-country European Union insists that Switzerland help fight tax evasion--though that is not crime in Switzerland--by disclosing amount of interest paid to nonresidents so they can be taxed accordingly in their home countries (M)
news.title: Europe Calls It Vital Tax Data; Swiss Banks Call It Vitally Secret

news.abstract: United Nations population division will meet in New York to begin exploring global cooperation on issue of immigration statistics; demographers say that past attempts to analyze population movements have been frustrated by govenrment officials who try to inflate or to obscure them; now there is intensifying debate about immigration in Europe and US, partly fueled by fears of terrorists crossing borders; beyond what are perceived as problems of immigration in richer countries, there is mounting evidence of threats to peace and life from migrations, often forced, in poor nations (M)
news.title: U.N. Coaxes Out the Wheres and Whys of Global Immigration

news.abstract: Forceful student movement is replacing Pres Mohammad Khatami as leading engine for political reform in Iran; activists at country's vibrant, overflowing universities say their calls for change are gathering momentum and they are preparing to put delicate issues like renewing relations with United states to public vote for first time; Khatami has twice been elected president but has been stymied in his quest for change by still-powerful conservative clerics and their supporters; unlike him, students are not patient, polite or at all ready to settle for status quo; they are aware of realities outside Iran because of Internet and satellite television; they read about Western democracy and are taught by professors who studied in West; photo (M)
news.title: Iran's Students Step Up Reform Drive

news.abstract: Greek police intensify hunt for members of country's November 17 terror group; discover second huge weapons cache, including anti-tank missiles and explosives in residential apartment block in central Athens; United States Embassy goes on maximum alert to guard against retaliation from group, which is blamed for at least 23 killings, including 1975 assassination of Richard Welch, CIA's station chief in Athens; police win biggest breakthrough in 27 years with arrest last week of foot soldier of terror group during botched bomb attack at port of Pireaus; suspect is said to be providing information to authorities about group (M)
news.title: Greek Police Find Another Arms Cache in 2nd Raid of Week

news.abstract: Parade by Protestant Orange Order in Portadown, Northern Ireland, ends in heated scuffles that injure 27 people, despite predictions by organizers and security forces that annual event would be peaceful for first time in nearly decade; crowds of Orangemen and Protestant supporters dismantle steel barricades blocking them from marching through predominantly Roman Catholic neighborhood and clash with police; photo (M)
news.title: Despite Peace Hopes, 27 Hurt in Ulster Protestant Parade

news.abstract: Article on physical and emotional trauma caused by suicide bombings and long ordeal facing Israelis gravely wounded in attacks; wounds are often severe, but not just physical; more than 4,000 Israelis have been injured since conflict with Palestinians began anew in September 2000, almost 10 times roughly 500 killed; among Palestinians, at least 1,450 have been killed and, according to Palestinian Authority, another 35,700 wounded; Palestinians say they are being injured and killed in larger numbers in course of resisting military occupation; Israelis say more of their own victims are noncombatants, women and children who are often killed or wounded in suicide bombings; in small nation like Israel, wounded produce ripple effect through society that partly explains strong support Israelis give military measures like recent retaking of practically entire West Bank to arrest militants and curb suicide bombings; wounded go on, publicly and painfully, battling wounds often far worse than those seen in nation at peace; recovery, when it comes, is almost always accompanied by ample parts of fear and anger; physical and mental trauma caused by bombings described; photos (L)
news.title: For Israelis Wounded in Bomb Attacks, Recovery Is a Battle

news.abstract: Data from the flight recorders aboard the two jets that collided over Germany last week show that a Swiss air traffic controller inadvertently put the planes on a collision course.
news.title: Controller Sent Jets Into Crash, Flight Data Show

news.abstract: Afghans mourn slain Vice President Hajji Abdul Qadir as officials investigate possibility that he was killed by drug lords double-crossed during Western-backed campaign to destroy country's poppy crop; he was overseeing Western-financed campaign begun in April to destroy fields; Afghan officials have been paying farmers about $500 per acre to destroy poppy plants (M)
news.title: Afghan Killing May Be Linked to Drug Trade

news.abstract: Bush adminstration's stated goal of toppling regime of Iraq Pres Saddam Hussein runs into strong reservations from Iraqi Kurdish leaders, who would be crucial allies in any military campaign; leaders flatly say they will be reluctant to join American military operations that put Kurds at risk of onslaught by Iraqi troops of kind they suffered after Persian Gulf War in 1991; even though American-led military campaign to topple Hussein would probably make Kurds freedom more secure, Kurdish leaders say Washington would be asking them to put all they have gained from decade of autonomy at risk of fresh Iraqi offensive; map (M)
news.title: Kurds, Secure in North Iraq Zone, Are Wary About a U.S. Offensive

news.abstract: Ivan Nikolic, former Yugoslav Army reservist, is sentenced to eight years in prison in Serbia's first war crimes trial for killing two Kosovo Albanian brothers in 1999 during Yugoslavia-NATO conflict (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Yugoslavia: Serb Convicted Of War Crime

news.abstract: Museum of Emory University will reportedly return to Egypt mummy believed to be Ramses I, pharaoh who ruled in 14th century BC (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: Pharaoh Heading Home

news.abstract: WASHINGTON:—  As President George W. Bush prepared a get-tough speech on the scandals buffeting corporate America and two former top executives of WorldCom Inc. refused to answer questions in Congress, investors got another jolt Monday as the drugmaker Merck & Co. revealed that one of its subsidiaries had overstated its revenues by billions of dollars.
news.title: Disclosure by Merck is latest scandal ahead of president's speech : A new jolt as Bush heads to Wall Street

news.abstract: Animal Conservaton for Life accuses Indonesian soldiers of smuggling endangered birds from eastern provinces of Maluku and Papua (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Indonesia: Soldiers Said To Smuggle Rare Birds

news.abstract: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda agrees to hand over some of its cases to national courts in effort to clear backlog and wind up its work by 2008 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Rwanda: Tribunal Tries To Cut Backlog

news.abstract: Senate Foreign Relations Committee plans hearings to question Bush administration officials on Iraq policy; Sen Joseph Biden calls for full public airing of how goal of removing Saddam Hussein from office might be accomplished (S)
news.title: Senate Panel to Ask Bush Aides To Give Details on His Iraq Policy

news.abstract: Bar called Putin in Chelyabinsk, 900 miles east of Moscow, is closed three weeks after it was opened by two college students; photo; Pres Vladimir Putin, who does not seem comfortable with such tributes, apparently was not happy with use of his name (S)
news.title: A Passing Fancy: A Bar Named for Putin

news.abstract: Iranian protesters clash with police at Tehran University and in affluent neighborhood in demonstrations marking third anniversary of violent crackdown on student protests (S)
news.title: Demonstrators, Ignoring a Ban, Clash With Riot Police in Tehran

news.abstract: Polish historians confirm that massacre of Jews in Jedwabne in 1941 was carried out by Poles, not occupying Germans; Radislaw Ignatiew presents conclusions of inquiry into findings of Polish-American historian Jan T Gross, whose book Neighbors told how Poles burned alive as many as 1,600 Jewish Poles; says at least 40 Poles carried out attack; 12 people were convicted in 1949 of aiding Germans (S)
news.title: An Inquiry Confirms a Massacre Of Jews by Poles in World War II

news.abstract: All that is left of Prigorodnoye is three families and the ruins of a kelp processing plant.    The village is a dot on a green stretch of coast on the island of Sakhalin, off Russia's eastern coast. It began losing population several decades ago, but the process accelerated in the last 15 years as economic collapse engulfed Russia.
news.title: Prigorodnoye Journal; Gas May Soon Replace Kelp as Sakhalin's Mainstay

news.abstract: China, in tentative move to re-establish exchanges with United States military, says it will let American military officials come to China to search for bodies of two pilots shot down near China-Korea border during Korean War (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: U.S. Can Search For Downed Pilots

news.abstract: BRITAIN: Big Day For Great Robber; RUSSIA: Another Sign Explodes;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Brazilian Justice Min Miguel Reale Jr resigns to protest solicitor general's ruling against federal intervention to replace crime-ridden government of Espirito Santo State; police director Itanor Carneiro and other senior officials have also resigned to protest decision, which overturned recommendation made by Human Rights Council after lawyers combatting corrupt officials in state were assassinated (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Brazil: Justice Minister Quits

news.abstract: PAKISTAN: Verdict In Pearl Case Due Soon; MALAYSIA: Conviction Upheld; CHINA: U.S. Can Search For Downed Pilots; INDIA: Counting Infiltrators; SOUTH KOREA: Ministers Replaced;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: India says infiltration of Islamic militants from Pakistani into Indian-controlled Kashmir dropped 30 percent between May 27 and June 23, but rose in last week of June (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Counting Infiltrators

news.abstract: Security Council holds several hours of closed-door debate about new American proposal to keep peacekeepers outside reach of International Criminal Court; diplomats say there is fair chance that divisive issue could be resolved soon; without resolution, mandate of Bosnian peacekeeping mission will soon expire, followed by other missions as they come up for renewal; issue has evolved in nasty dispute between United States and some of its closest allies, all of which have embraced new court (M)
news.title: Diplomats Say Court Immunity Solution May Be in Sight

news.abstract: ITALY: New Immigration Law; VATICAN: Contender For The Papacy; RUSSIA: Novelist Faces Pornography Charge; SWITZERLAND: Two Quit In Scandal Over Scandal; BRITAIN: A Break For American Pets;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Moscow investigators, acting on complaint from youth group that backs Pres Vladimir V Putin, charges Vladimir Sorokin with pornography over his 1999 novel Blue Lard, that depicts homosexual act between clones of Stalin and Khrushchev; free-speech advocates express alarm; government official calls charge misguided (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Novelist Faces Pornography Charge

news.abstract: CUBA: Elections, But No Referendum; BOLIVIA: U.S. Warns Against Candidate;.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Cautious debate, prompted by Sept 11 terrorist attacks, is taking place in Saudi Arabia's closed society over intolerance toward non-Muslims and attitudes toward West that are now viewed by some as inspiring unacceptable violence; debate appears to represent significant shift in society whose Wahhabi branch of Islam tends to make such questioning taboo; small group of intellectuals, academics, journalists and religious scholars are quietly suggesting that change is needed, but such positions remain controversial; after scores of religius scholars and academics issued manifesto this spring suggesting that Muslims might find common ground with West, they were subjected to withering denunciations by those who accept Wahhabi notion that Islam thrives on hostility toward infidels; austere teachings of Muhammad bin Abd al-Wahhab have been prevalent in Saudi Arabia for more than two centuries, and ruling Saud dynasty owes its very control over peninsula's once fractious tribes to fact that their ancestors championed his teachings; Saudis in general, and senior princes in particular, reject notion that Wahhabi teachings spawn terrorism; photos (M)
news.title: A Few Saudis Defy a Rigid Islam To Debate Their Own Intolerance

news.abstract: BALKANS MONEY GOING BEGGING ;.
news.title: World Briefing: European Union

news.abstract: UN Security Council, ending unusual wrangle between US and most other members, unanimously adopts resolution effectively giving US peacekeepers year's exemption from prosecution by new International Criminal Court (M)
news.title: U.N. Ends Wrangle Over U.S. Immunity

news.abstract: Children and adults, in interviews, discuss child labor at Los Alamos banana plantation near Puerto Inca, Ecuador; plantation, which employs some 1,300 workers, is owned by Alvaro Noboa, country's richest man and leading presidential candidate; growers and exporters in Ecuador, which supplies 25 percent of bananas exported to US, say product earns them about 30 percent less than decade ago, often prompting to turn blind eye to labor codes; photos; map and chart of child labor in Latin America; photos (M)
news.title: In Ecuador's Banana Fields, Child Labor Is Key to Profits

news.abstract: About 16 people reportedly are injured and dozen others are arrested as hundreds of armed Mexican farmers seize control of government offices in San Salvador Atenco, abduct several local officials and demand that government abandon plans to take land for $2.3-billion international airport (M)
news.title: Mexican Farmers Seize Officials

news.abstract: UN Security Council, ending weeks-long confrontation with intense closed-door negotiations, unanimously adopts resolution that effectively gives American peacekeepers year's exemption from prosecution by new International Criminal Court; also renews mandates of UN peacekeeping missions in Bosnia and Prevlaka, Croatia (M)
news.title: U.S. Peacekeepers Given Year's Immunity From New Court

news.abstract: Handmade grenade slightly wounds 12 people, including 9 European tourists, in Pakistan's North-West Frontier Province; westerners have been targets of several attacks in recent months, with Islamic militants angry about American military operations in Afghanistan; deatils of latest attack are sketchy (M)
news.title: 9 Europeans Among 12 Hurt By Grenade Attack in Pakistan

news.abstract: Pakistan has become laboratory for how American power could be used to combat terror; American law enforcement agencies are working with American military in Pakistan in hunt for Al Qaeda fighers who fled sanctuaries in Afghanistan and hope to revive their group; FBI agents are helping local police in Pakistani cities to break up what senior American intelligence and law enforcement officials regard as depleted but still dangerous network that carried out deadly attacks against Westerners in Karachi and Islamabad in recent weeks; never before have traditionally independent military and law enforcement organizations worked so much in concert; similar, if smaller, American operations appear to be unfolding in Philippines and Yemen; photos; map (L)
news.title: F.B.I. AND MILITARY UNITE IN PAKISTAN TO HUNT AL QAEDA

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of Bangladeshis show outward signs of arsenic poisoning from their drinking water; World Health Orgn calls this largest mass poisoning of population in history; about 35 million Bangladeshis drink arsenic-contaminated water from tube wells that tap into underground aquifers; government, Unicef and various aid groups had encouraged installation of such wells, eager to wean nation from pond water which is often incubator for lethal disease; underground aquifers were never tested for arsenic until hundreds of people fell sick; in 1998, World Bank lent government $32.4 million to test every tube well and to provide safe sources of water; project has been hobbled by unforeseen problems, and most of country's estimated 11 million wells have yet to be tested; trusting Bangladeshi people are now told that water from 'safe' tube wells may be delivering arsenic-induced cancer; photos; maps (L)
news.title: Bangladeshis Sipping Arsenic As Plan for Safe Water Stalls

news.abstract: Former Iraqi military officers who have defected during Saddam Hussein's 23 years in power meet in London to discuss ways of helping to bring him down; they are prompted by Pres Bush's calls for his overthrow; organizers say meeting has aim of sending message to military officers in Iraq, encouraging them to prepare to support American-led effort to oust Hussein; several of former officers claim Iraqi officers corps is rife with hatred for Hussein and could be persuaded to join coup or invading force, provided they are guaranteed future in post-Hussein Iraq; American officials from several agencies attend as observers; surprise guest at meeting is Prince Hassan bin-Talal of Jordan, brother of late King Hussein and heir to his throne until King changed succession in favor his his son, present King Abdullah; Abdullah's government quickly denies reports that American military will be allowed to use Jordan as base for air and ground attacks against Iraq; Prince Hassan claims his presence at meeting is personal; photo (M)
news.title: With Potential in the Air, Iraqi Exiles Meet

news.abstract: Provincial court rules that Ontario government must recognize right of gays and lesbians to marry people of their own gender; ruling comes in response to lawsuit filed by lesbian couple and gay male couple to compel provincial government to register their marriage ceremonies as legally binding
news.title: Court Rules That Ontario Must Recognize Same-Sex Marriages

news.abstract: China's roughly 60 million factory workers, most of whom are still employed by the state, make up the bulk of the urban work force. As the worst of the state-owned enterprises are shut down, many of these people are being thrown out of work. Accustomed to the security of the state economy and concentrated enough to organize, they represent the most volatile slice of the population.    Tang Nianshan and his wife, Tang Airong, have spent most of their lives working in state-owned factories. Ms. Tang, 43, has been working for the same factory since she was 18. It makes enameled tin washbasins. She earns just under 1,000 yuan a month.
news.title: The Factory Worker; A Workplace Shifts As a Society Changes

news.abstract: Death toll from July 13 attack by guerrillas on Kashmir shantytown climbs to 27; Indian officials express outrage, but government avoids accusations while preparing official response; no one has claimed reponsibility (S)
news.title: India Voices Anger at Kashmir Raid That Killed 27

news.abstract: Chen Qun, 28, is one of an estimated 150 million peasants who have left the land to find work in China's swelling cities. Most cities have large populations of these struggling ''outsiders,'' as urban residents call them.    City dwellers regard the migrants with suspicion and regularly blame them for rising crime. The migrants overwhelm railroads and bus lines early each year during an annual migration back to their hometowns for the all-important lunar New Year holiday. But their remittances to their families in the countryside remain the most significant means of distributing the wealth of China's cities and its coastal export belt to the vast, impoverished hinterland.
news.title: The Migrant; Building a New Life In an Unfriendly City

news.abstract: A neo-Nazi gunmen who is accused of trying to kill President Jacques Chirac during Sunday's Bastille Day parade was committed to a psychiatric hospital today.
news.title: Chirac Gunman Committed to Psychiatric Hospital

news.abstract: The Times interviewed people from different walks of life to give a sense of who the Chinese are today.
news.title: China Juggles Conflicting Pressures of Society in Transition

news.abstract: Beijing Journal column on struggle of 20-year old Zhuo Ling, who holds Miss China title, to win approval in country where beauty pageants are officially regarded as subversive; she placed third in Miss Universe contest, which she entered 'unofficially;' photos (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; Here She Comes! (Will China Ever Be the Same?)

news.abstract: Israeli-Palestinian crisis causes flurry of diplomatic maneuvering on eve of high-level meeting in New York City at request of Sec of State Colin L Powell; meeting between representatives from US, UN, European Union and Russia faces central issue of future of Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, long embodiment of Palestinian aspirations who Pres Bush and advisers say cannot lead any future Palestinian state; Israeli Defense Min Benjamin Ben-Eliezer meets with Egyptian Pres Hosni Mubarak in Alexandria; both reportedly arrive at different conclusions about Arafat's future (M)
news.title: Flurry Precedes Mideast Meeting in New York

news.abstract: Focus on controversy surrounding Karahnjukar Hydropower Project planned by Iceland's government to dam glacial river flows in large tract of wilderness and produce hydroelectric power for aluminium smelter planned by Alcoa; smelter will rest on country's wind-swept eastern fjords, with view to creating 2,000 construction jobs and 600 to 1,000 permanent ones in region Icelanders are deserting in droves; outraged environmentalists say country is selling its wild birthright, damaging its eco-tourist image and risking credit rating to benefit $23 billion American conglomerate and to win mere handful of jobs; backers of project say country has profitably taken big risks to attract smelters twice before, that it must keep its rural areas populated and that it will still be able to establish stunning national park, as environmentalists desire; photos; maps (M)
news.title: An Icelandic Battle of Wildlife Versus Voltage

news.abstract: The Irish Republican Army issued a straight, unmitigated apology today for the deaths of civilians killed in its violent efforts to unite Northern Ireland with the Irish Republic.
news.title: I.R.A. Apologizes for Civilian Deaths

news.abstract: British newspaper Guardian's Zimbabwe correspondent Andrew Meldrum is acquitted on charges of publishing false information; he is ordered to leave country within 24 hours; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Zimbabwe: Journalist Ordered Out

news.abstract: With global financial markets on tenterhooks, Alan Greenspan, the chairman of the Federal Reserve Board, delivered a guardedly optimistic outlook Tuesday for the U.S. economy, saying "the fundamentals are in place for a return to sustained healthy growth."
news.title: But Greenspan warns scandals are 'destructive to capitalism' : Fed chief's outlook upbeat

news.abstract: Sec Colin Powell and envoys from UN, European Union and Russia meet in New York and agree on broad goal of creating Palestinian state within three years, but differ sharply on almost everything else, including role of Yasir Arafat and how much to emphasize security as condition for resuming peace talks with Israel; Powell also meets separately with Egyptian and Jordanian ministers; US urges allies to contribute financially through international agencies, not Palestinian Authority, which Israel says siphons off money for terrorism (M)
news.title: Arafat's Role Is in Dispute During Talks in New York

news.abstract: India, under intense domestic pressure following deadly attack in Kashmir, renews call for US to declare Pakistan terrorist state (M)
news.title: India Renews Call for U.S. to Declare Pakistan a Terrorist State

news.abstract: Protesters mostly stay off streets of Asuncion, Paraguay, after declaration of five-day state of emergency to quell demonstrations against economic policies (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Paraguay: Protests Taper Off

news.abstract: Police in Spain arrest three men suspected of being operatives of Al Qaeda, and officials say one of them had five-year-old videotapes with hours of surveillance images of World Trade Center and other United States sites that may have been considered as targets; among sites are Disneyland, Universal Studios, Statue of Liberty, Brooklyn Bridge and Golden Gate Brige; two of men are identified as Muhammad Khair al-Saqq and Ghasoub al-Abrash Ghalyoun (aka Abu Musab); their known links with Al Qaeda operations and contents of tapes described (M)
news.title: Spain Arrests 3 Suspects; Tapes of U.S. Sites Seized

news.abstract: Ontario provincial government says it will not appeal court ruling that province must extend marriage rights to same-xex couples (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Canada: Province Won't Appeal Same-Sex Ruling

news.abstract: Paraguay Pres Luis Gonzalez Macchi lifts state of emergency he decreed on after violent protests against his government's economic policies; rejects demands that he resign, televised speech; links what he calls 'plan of destabilization' to exiled Gen Lino Oviedo and opposition politicians led by Vice Pres Julio Cesar Franco; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Paraguay: Emergency Lifted

news.abstract: Case in which bungling at fertility clinic left white couple with black twins is taken to Britain's highest court; details are being kept secret by court order, leaving it unclear who is suing whom (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Suit In Bungled Embryo Case

news.abstract: Salman Saqib, Fahad Naseem and Shaikh Adil appeal life sentences they face in Pakistan for kidnapping and killing of American reporter Daniel Pearl (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Pakistan: Reporter's Killers File Appeals

news.abstract: European Commission fines France almost $160,000 for every day it continues to refuse to lift ban on British beef; European Union lifted own ban in 1999, after concluding mad cow disease had been wiped out in Britain (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Fine On France Sought In Beef Dispute

news.abstract: Pres Bush reassures skeptical Arab allies that his administration will press forward with efforts to reach peace in Middle East despite continued attacks on Israel and disagreements over role of Yasir Arafat as Palestinian leader; meets at White House with foreign ministers of Egypt, Jordan and Saudi Arabia (M)
news.title: Bush Tells Arab Ministers U.S. Wants Mideast Peace

news.abstract: Argentine government, responding to growing clamor about increase in violent crime after collapse of economy, announces formation of special antikidnapping brigade (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Argentina: Economy Down, Kidnappings Up

news.abstract: Abu Sayyaf, militant group in Philippines, warns in radio broadcast that it will attack Americans and American interests in Philippines (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Philippines: Americans Threatened

news.abstract: Nearly 40 graves are desecrated in Jewish section of Rome's historic Verano Cemetery; vandals smash headstones, topple columns and overturn earth in chilling scene that marks arrival in Italy of wave of anti-Semitic attacks across Europe; Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi scores 'barbarity of anti-Semitism'; photo (M)
news.title: Nearly 40 Jewish Graves Are Desecrated in a Rome Cemetery

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, underdog for re-election in Sept, dismisses defense min Rudolf Scharping after allegations of financial improprieties (M)
news.title: With an Eye On Election, Schröder Fires Defense Chief

news.abstract: Profile of and interview with Maria Asuncion Aramburuzabala, Mexican who, since death of her father, Pablo, has transformed herself from unemployed, divorced daughter of billionaire into billionaire who manages Grupo Modelo, family fortune built on beer; photo (M)
news.title: Daddy's Girl Turns Beer-and-TV Billionaire

news.abstract: Alexandros Yiotopoulos, mathematician suspected of leading Greek guerrilla group November 17, is charged with murders, bomb attacks and bank robberies carried out during 1980's (M)
news.title: Reputed Leader of Greek Guerrillas Is Charged in Murders

news.abstract: US imposes trade sanctions on nine Chinese companies and Indian businessman for allegedly selling goods or technology to Iran, where they were used by country's chemical and conventional weapons programs; Wisconsin Project on Nuclear Arms Control director Gary Milhollin calls sanctions toothless and urges Congress to enact tougher rules (M)
news.title: U.S. to Punish 10 Businesses For Iran Sales

news.abstract: Israeli Army rounds up and threatens to deport 21 male relatives of Palestinian fugitives Nasser Aseida and Ali Ajouri and destroys their houses; Nasser Aseida is said to be Hamas mastermind of ambush on armored bus in which nine Israelis died and Ali Ajouri is believed to be leader of Fatah-affiliated Aksa Martyrs Brigades who sent two suicide bombers to Tel Aviv, where they killed three men; Palestinian officials and Israeli human rights organizations protest possible deportations; photo; map (M)
news.title: Israel Threatens to Deport Relatives of 2 Fugitive Militants

news.abstract: Myanmar's pro-democracy movement, led by Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, calls for opening of both formal talks and private meetings with government (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Myanmar: Opposition Seeks Dialogue

news.abstract: Europe's patchwork of air traffic control systems, major factor in chronic delays in European flights, is now seen as safety threat in wake of July 1 midair collision between Russian passenger jetliner and Boeing 757 cargo plane over southern Germany; among baffling chain of missteps that led to accident was breakdown in communication between Swiss and German controllers; officials are recommending use of emergency phone lines or computer links between air traffic control centers in different countries, and ways of improving communication between pilots and controllers; investigators say German controller tried desperately to call counterpart in Zurich after noticing planes were on collision course, but that line was busy (M)
news.title: Midair Crash Opens Debate On Air Safety Over Europe

news.abstract: American air campaign in Afghanistan, based on use of high-tech weaponry, has produced pattern of mistakes that killed hundreds of Afghan civilians; on-site reviews of 11 locations where air strikes killed as many as 400 civilians suggest American commanders sometimes relied on mistaken information from local Afghans; suggest preference for air strikes instead of riskier ground operations eliminated way of checking accuracy of intelligence; indicate Pentagon's use of overwhelming force meant that even when truly military targets were located, civilians were sometimes killed; map; photos (M)
news.title: Flaws in U.S. Air War Left Hundreds of Civilians Dead

news.abstract: North Korean jetliner makes roundtrip test flight to South Korea, first step in opening regular air links between both countries; map; photo (M)
news.title: Test Flight Advances Plan for Regular Inter-Korean Air Link

news.abstract: British Foreign Sec Jack Straw, in Islamabad, Pakistan, for talks aimed at easing tensions with India over Kashmir, says he is satisfied with discussions so far (S)
news.title: Britain Tries To Ease Enmity Over Kashmir

news.abstract: Hundreds of jobless Palestinians are sneaking into Israel illegally with wives and children to work in fields of Tamara and neighboring Israeli Arab communities, despite border closings that have prevented them from reaching previous jobs in Israel for nearly two years and crippled Palestinian economy; photos; maps (M)
news.title: Desperate Palestinians Sneak Into Israel to Work

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  For years, passengers flying between Asia and North America across the Pacific have had to put up with the inconvenience and tedium of indirect services.
news.title: Longer-range jets win over Asia

news.abstract: Interview with Prime Min Ranil Wickremesinghe, first Sri Lankan leader to visit Washington in nearly two decades; Wickremesinghe holds that American-led campaign against terrorism had helped his government's chances of ending long civil war; says he will ask for increased aid to rebuild nation's economy; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Sri Lankan Says U.S. Drive on Terror Helps Peace Effort

news.abstract: The Bush administration announced today that it will withhold $34 million because some of the programs' funds have gone to agencies that pressure women to have abortions.
news.title: U.S. to Withhold Family-Planning Money From U.N.

news.abstract: High-level defector from Iran's intelligence agency says Iranian government organized and carried out bombing of Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 1994 that killed 85 people and paid former Argentine Pres Carlos Saul Menem $10 million to cover it up; transcript of deposition by Abdolghassem Mesbahi is received by New York Times from Argentine officials frustrated that case remains unsolved; says Menem, president from 1989 to 1999, benefited for years from his ties to Iranian intelligence officials who courted him for his combination of rising political power, Muslim ancestry and connections to Argentina's small but influential Syrian-Lebanese community; allegations in transcript detailed; Menem, through spokesman, rebuts charges; suggests they are politically motivated; has launched new campaign for president despite taint from political corruption scandals; bombing of community center recalled; photos (M)
news.title: Iran Blew Up Jewish Center In Argentina, Defector Says

news.abstract: State Dept experiences difficulty filling hardship posts overseas despite record number of people applying to join Foreign Service as American diplomats shun jobs over security and lifestyle concerns; problem is especially acute in Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, whose strategic importance has surged because of US-led campaign against terrorism; 60 percent of embassies and consulates are designated hardship posts for variety of reasons; from Nigeria to Kazakhstan to China, all considered hardship assignments, American missions report vacancy rate 50 percent higher than in more developed nations; while newly minted diplomats are more eager than ever to serve country and even express interest in hardship assignments, they are quick to state desire to avoid places that might pose risk to families; map (M)
news.title: More Say Yes to Foreign Service, But Not to Hardship Assignments

news.abstract: Arrest of member of Greece's November 17 guerrilla group shatters image of organization which for generation cast itself as infallible cell of intellectuals, or latter-day Robin Hoods punishing rich on behalf of poor; police may have unmasked most of its major figures, including two real estate agents, state bus driver and French-born mathematician; hold group responsible for 23 killings, including four Americans, since 1975 (M)
news.title: Arrests Destroy Noble Image Of Guerrilla Group in Greece

news.abstract: The Justice Dept. announced the indictment today of five suspects in connection with the death of a kidnapped missionary.
news.title: U.S. Indicts 5 in Killing of Missionary in Philippines

news.abstract: Edward Lee Howard, former CIA agent who defected to Soviet Union in mid-1980's after disappearing in New Mexico desert, dies at age 50; photo (M)
news.title: Edward Lee Howard, 50, Spy Who Escaped to Soviet Haven

news.abstract: About 1,000 farmers parading through central Seoul burn copies of secret agreement between South Korea and China that opens way to annual imports of $9 million worth of garlic from China beginning next year (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Garlic Farmers Protest

news.abstract: Jeffrey Archer, millionaire author, former Conservative party deputy party leader and member of House of Lords, loses bids before Court of Appeal to reconsider his conviction for perjury and reduce his four-year sentence; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Court Refuses Archer Appeal

news.abstract: Pres Bush condemns as 'heavy handed' Israeli bombing attack that killed Hamas leader Sheik Salah Shehada and 14 civilians in Gaza; administration says that Israelis knew apartment building hit with one-ton bomb was filled with ordinary Palestinians, including children; Shehada founded military wing of Hamas and was blamed for string of deadly suicide attacks, but scale of damage and televised scenes of infant's body being carried through streets prompt Bush to issue condemnation; photo; Israel says it had no choice and regrets civilian deaths, but military officials, reacting to international criticism, say they did not anticipate extent of collateral damage; top Israeli military envoys met in Washington with Sec Colin Powell and security adviser Condoleezza Rice hours before attack but gave no warning and may not have known (M)
news.title: BUSH DENOUNCES ISRAELI AIRSTRIKE AS 'HEAVY HANDED'

news.abstract: Federal jury in Miami orders two retired Salvadoran generals to pay $54.6 million in damages to three civilians who were tortured by security forces during civil war, more than twenty years ago; finds that Jose Guillermo Garcia and Carlos Eugenio Vides Casanova, who now live in Florida, knew of atrocities and did nothing to prevent them; case was brough under 1992 Torture Victims Protection Act (M)
news.title: Torture Victims In El Salvador Are Awarded $54 Million

news.abstract: International Helsinki Federation for Human Rights charges Russian military conducts deliberate campaign of murder among Chechen civilians, killing between 50 and 80 people a month; says drive seems aimed at young men (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Accusation Of Murder In Chechnya

news.abstract: British Conservative leader Iain Duncan Smith replaces party chairman David Davis with Theresa May, first woman to hold post; is reportedly irked by Davis's resistance to modernizing party; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: A New Look For Tories

news.abstract: IRELAND: 98 Arrests In Immigrant Crackdown; BRITAIN: A New Look For Tories; RUSSIA: Accusation Of Murder In Chechnya; NORTHERN IRELAND: Catholic Quota Upheld;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: ARGENTINA: Menem Acknowledges Swiss Account; PERU: More Charges Against Fujimori; CUBA: Bush Would Veto Easier Travel;.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain denounces persistence of violence in Northern Ireland; calls on province's paramilitary groups to disband and warns that government would become more 'rigorous' in punishing them for violating their ceasefire claims; large-scale organized killing has ended, but there has been upsurge of riots, shootings, gasoline bomb attacks and beatings; government believes some of violence is being coordinated by Irish Republican Army and its counterpart Protestant guerrilla groups, all of whom pledged four years ago to maintain ceasefires and abandon systematic mayhem (M)
news.title: Blair Says Northern Ireland's Militias Must All Disband

news.abstract: Young American Catholics and church leaders gather in Toronto for first World Youth Day since attention to some priests' victimization of children became crisis for American church; those attending event are willing to acknowledge problem, but not inclined to dwell on it; it is posing little distraction to their celebration of Catholicism as force for good and source of peace; weeklong festival, highlighted by presnce of Pope John Paul II, is being seen as time to move on (M)
news.title: Young U.S. Catholics Seeking To Put Scandals in Perspective

news.abstract: United States loses bid to rewrite United Nations plan intended to reinforce 1989 convention against torture; Bush administration fears new plan would lead to demands by monitors to gain access to American prisoners and detainees; US sought to create committee in General Assembly to write new plan more acceptable to Washington, but proposal has been defeated; General Assembly will now consider plan approved by UN's Economic and Social Council (M)
news.title: U.S. Fails in Effort to Block Vote On U.N. Convention on Torture

news.abstract: The European Court of Human Rights ruled today that Maurice Papon was denied a fair trial on charges of war crimes.
news.title: Nazi Collaborator Wins Court Challenge on French Trial

news.abstract: European Union signs $33.8 million agreement to pay for rebuilding main bridge over Danube in Novi Sad, Yugoslavia; it was destroyed in 1999 by NATO bombs during Kosovo war (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Yugoslavia: Danube Bridge To Be Rebuilt

news.abstract: Study under way for United States Agency for International Development is said to be finding that malnutrition among Palestinian children in West Bank and the Gaza Strip has increased substantially during conflict with Israel; preliminary results of study cause alarm within Israeli government and Bush administration, which has been pressuring Israel to alleviate Palestinian suffering; senior Israeli official says study's results could be 'disastrous for Israel'; Israeli government, already anticipating international criticism over conditions among Palestinians, has recently stepped up talks with Palestinian representatives to address needs of those in West Bank; aid workers say few Palestinians can leave their homes to work, and costs and difficulties of transporting goods have become prohibitive; diplomats say Israeli government, concerned about international criticism, has made it easier for international aid groups to distribute food; photo (M)
news.title: In Palestinian Children, Signs of Increasing Malnutrition

news.abstract: Congress reached a tentative pact on a bill to give the White House broader authority to negotiate new trade agreements and increase help for American workers. Page A6.
news.title: Deal on Trade Powers Bill

news.abstract: North Korea issues surprising expression of regret over naval skirmish in Yellow Sea last month in which five South Koreans were killed; calls for cabinet-level talks with South Korea along with steps to revive measures to reconcile two countries; message comes within hours after Pres Kim Dae Jung of South Korea demands apology from North Korea, and day after North warned of more clashes if South Korea and United States insist on their right to block North Korean ships from venturing south of line in Yellow Sea that North Korea has never recognized; analysts say latest message might have been motivated by North Korea's desire for South to ship grain it held back after Yellow Sea skirmish (M)
news.title: North Korea Regrets Naval Clash With Seoul and Seeks Talks
