news.abstract: Israel's Labor Party ministers resign from coalition government over their assertion that Prime Min Ariel Sharon's budget favors Israel's settlers at expense of its poor; break is almost certain to drive Israeli government to right; it is first attempt by moderately leftist party to find political voice and present coherent alternative to Sharon since his crushing victory almost two years ago over his predecessor, Labor candidate Ehud Barak; loss of Labor's 25 seats in 120-seat Parliament leaves Sharon with minority government of 55 seats; he faces three basic options: he can try to govern with his remaining, right-of-center minority, which would leave him vulnerable to possible no-confidence vote; he can try to bring in ultra-right factions that would give him bare majority but also heighten risk that his government would appear extremist; or he can ask Pres Moshe Katsav to dissolve Parliament and call elections within 90 days, nine months ahead of schedule; allies say Sharon is likely to pursue first or second option for now; Defense Min Benjamin Ben-Eliezer, explaining his decision to leave government, says it is time to show Palestinians 'diplomatic horizon'; but most likely result of his departure will be to empower hard-line groups most opposed to dealing with Palestinians; photo; chart (M)
news.title: SHARON COALITION SHATTERS AS LABOR QUITS OVER BUDGET

news.abstract: Senior Chechen leader Akhmed Zakayev is arrested and jailed in Copenhagen on Russian charges that he was involved in Moscow theater siege; seizure signals that Pres Vladimir Putin's vow to apprehend Chechen separatists in American-style, worldwide war on terror is winning friends beyond his borders; Zakayev is in Copenhagen to attend so-called World Chechen Congress, which Russia had urged Denmark to block; conference had drafted statements calling for negotiations to end war in Chechnya; Zakayev's arrest is major coup for Putin; Danish judge orders Zakayev held until Nov 12 because of risk he might flee while question of his extradition to Russia is settled; photo (M)
news.title: Chechen Leader Arrested In Denmark Is a Quarry Of Putin's Terrorist Hunt

news.abstract: The court was informed that the butler had told Queen Elizabeth II he was keeping some of the princess's belongings.
news.title: Theft Charges Dropped Against Diana's Former Butler

news.abstract: British Parliament votes to end centuries-old ritual of late-night sessions and shift workday timetable three hours earlier; sessions will now begin at 11:30 am and run no later than 7:30 pm (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: No More Late Nights For Parliament

news.abstract: Pakistani officials say Al Qaeda members are trying to re-establish their network in Karachi, with support from local people, elaborate secrecy and Internet communication; say story of Ramzi bin al-Shibh's final month of freedom and his chaotic arrest illustrates why it is proving so difficult to eliminate Al Qaeda; say bin al-Shibh, thought to be key planner of Sept 11 terrorist attacks on World Trade Center and Pentagon, lived quietly in Karachi, 10 miles from American Consulate, and spent his days with Qaeda friends, logging on to Internet and at night playing cards; Pakistani officials are convinced that Al Qaeda's operations head Khalid Shaikh Mohammed remains in Karachi, hiding in apartment, just as bin al-Shibh did; Mohammed, one of America's most sought men, is alleged mastermind of Sept 11 attacks; Pakistani officials say bin al-Shibh's arrest disrupted Al Qaeda's network in Karachi but did not eliminate it; yearlong crackdown by Gen Pervez Musharraf has failed to stop Pakistani militants from aiding Qaeda members; photo (L)
news.title: Qaeda Uses Teeming Karachi As New Base, Pakistanis Say

news.abstract: United States troops near Pyongyang, North Korea, accept remains of 11 american servicemen killed in Korean War (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: North Korea: Remains Of Americans Returned

news.abstract: BRITAIN: No More Late Nights For Parliament; AUSTRIA: Leader Of Rightist Party Resigns;
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: The feverish outburst of artistic invention on the Paris scene from 1890 to 1900 is perhaps the most astonishing phenomenon in the recent history of Western culture. Some may marvel that it should have taken so long for an exhibition such as "Les Peintres Graveurs: 1890-1900" to see the light of day.
news.title: EXHIBITION:PARIS : Shedding some light on an era of invention

news.abstract: SRI LANKA: Rebels Protest Leader'S Sentence; SOUTH KOREA: President'S Son Sentenced;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Macedonian Parliament votes in new governing coalition that includes party formed by ethnic Albanian guerrillas; nationalists accuse new prime minister Branko Crvenkovski of bringing 'terrorists' into government by giving ministries to party led by former rebel commander Ali Ahmeti; Crvenkovski says inclusion of party will help stabilize nation; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Macedonia: Government Includes Ex-Rebels

news.abstract: THE HAGUE: Milosevic Ailing Again; MACEDONIA: Government Includes Ex-Rebels; CZECH REPUBLIC: Post-Havel Plans; BELARUS: New Law Restricts Religions; BULGARIA: Missile Destruction For Nato;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Iran's hard-line judiciary closes second research group, Ayandeh Research Group, and arrests two researchers, one of whom is later freed; Hossein Ghazian is still being held (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Iran: Judges Shut Another Research Group

news.abstract: Senior Afghan officials are increasingly concerned that Taliban forces are reorganizing in border areas of Pakistan in preparation for new wave of terrorist attacks on Afghanistan; concerns are heightened by elections in Pakistan in which fundamentalist Islamic parties allied with Taliban gained control of provincial governments along border; assessment is shared by many people in Pentagon and State Department, who are convinced that elements of Pakistani intelligence continue to funnel weapons and money to Taliban units and their allies inside and outside Afghanistan; photo (M)
news.title: Afghans Raise Concern That Taliban Forces Are Reorganizing in Pakistan

news.abstract: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is likely to find his freedom of action circumscribed when he becomes president of Brazil on Jan 1 despite his landslide election victory; his powers are being trimmed by new legislation, and his lack of majority in Congress means initiatives he is proposing may end up being blocked or watered down (M)
news.title: Law and Politics Likely to Curb Power of Brazil's New Leader

news.abstract: Egypt's tourism industry, which accounts for 12 percent of economy and 1 in 7 jobs, is suffering because of Sept 11 attacks, prospect of war in Iraq and violence in Israel and West Bank, as well as economic troubles around the world; visits by Americans have plunged, and fewer visitors are going to historic sites like Luxor; security has been greatly increased since 1997, when Islamic militants massacred 58 tourists and 4 Egyptians at temple in Luxor and virtually shut down tourism; photos; map (M)
news.title: Egypt Shores Up Security, but Tourism Is Shaky

news.abstract: Denmark refuses to extradite Akhmed Zakayev, senior Chechen leader, saying Russian prosecutors have yet to provide evidence that he was involved in terrorist activities; some members of Russia's Parliament call for boycott of Danish goods, while others lead demonstration outside Danish Embassy in Moscow; relations between Denmark and Russia have soured badly since Danish authorities refused to shut down conference of Chechen representatives in Copenhagen after siege of Moscow theater by Chechen guerrillas (M)
news.title: Feud Grows Between Russia and Denmark Over Extradition of Chechen Rebel

news.abstract: Round of international climate talks is held in New Delhi, and focus is on adapting to global warming instead of fighting to limit emissions of gases responsible for it; many environmentalists have long avoided discussing adaptation for fear it would smack of defeatism; shift is partly driven by unusual weather this year and fear that costs of weather-related disasters will rise with global warming; another impetus is rising realization that many significant shifts have already been set in motion by century-long accumulation of warming gases; photos (M)
news.title: Climate Talks Shift Focus to How to Deal With Changes

news.abstract: Former Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu conditionally agrees to become Israel's foreign minister; says he will accept offer by Prime Min Ariel Sharon if government promises to call new elections soon and if he reaches understanding on three major issues; cites exile for Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, which he favors, establishment of Palestinian state, which he opposes, and location of new fence along boundary of West Bank; he would replace Shimon Peres, architect of Oslo accords and supporter of two-state solution to conflict with Palestinians; offer by Sharon is latest move to recruit allies and box in rivals to shore up his minority coalition government now that Labor Party has dropped out; collapse of 19-month-old unity government in budget dispute and political implications of overture to rival Netanyahu discussed; photo (M),
news.title: NETANYAHU AGREES TO A CABINET POST IF A VOTE FOLLOWS

news.abstract: Turkish voters elect former Islamicist Recep Tayyip Erdogan to head new government, expelling ruling coalition led by Prime Min Bulent Ecevit; his Justice and Development Party wins 34.2 percent of vote, compared with 19.4 for closest rival; he quickly seeks to calm fears by emphasizing his support for moderate, secular Turkey, committed to joining European Union and continuing strong relations with US; map (M)
news.title: VOTERS IN TURKEY EXPEL LEADERSHIP

news.abstract: White House rejects North Korean offer to open talks on North's newly disclosed nuclear weapons program, demanding program be dismantled first (S)
news.title: White House Rejects North Korean Offer for Talks

news.abstract: Colombia's new law-and-order Pres Alvaro Uribe moves to pacify Communa 13, district of Medellin that is epitome of urban violence; photo; map; success could become model for other big citieshard hit by 38-year-old civil conflict (M)
news.title: Colombia Takes Aim At Rebels In Its Cities

news.abstract: Police in New Delhi report thwarting terrorist attack on crowded shopping center on eve of Hindu festival; photo; accused are said to be Pakistan-based Islamic militants (S)
news.title: India Reports Killing 2, Stopping Terror Attack

news.abstract: Multinational organization that administers 1994 agreement between United States and North Korea prepares to send shipment of fuel oil to North Korea, despite North's recent admission that it violated pact by operating secret nuclear weapons program; new shipment by agency, Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization, underscores difficulties Bush administration is facing in its efforts to isolate North Korea over its weapons program (M)
news.title: North Korea Is Ready to Get Fuel Shipment Under 1994 Pact That It Violated

news.abstract: Bush administration officials work to put finishing touches on Security Council resolution for tough weapons inspections in Iraq, and major Council nations say they are optimistic that measure will be adopted soon and with broad support (M)
news.title: U.S. Refines Resolution on Iraq as Hopes Rise

news.abstract: South Korean Justice Min Kim Jung Kil and Prosecutor General Lee Myung Jae resign and apologize for murder suspect's death during Seoul police interrogation; relatives of Cho Cheun Hun hold he was tortured to death; civic groups call for full inquiry; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Officials Quit After Suspect's Death

news.abstract: Czech Republic's governing coalition loses majority in Senate, diminishing chance they will decide who succeeds outgoing Pres Vaclav Havel (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Czech Republic: Government Loses Senate Edge

news.abstract: European red squirrel, once common in Moscow's parks, have dwindled down to about 200, and city introduces breeding program to bring them back; photos (M)
news.title: Moscow Journal; Come Home, Little Squirrel: Parks Have Vacancies

news.abstract: American military officials say that in war with Iraq, Air Force would use same missile-firing drones that killed one of Al Qaeda's senior leaders in Yemen to attack Iraqi air defense radars, mobile Scud missile launchers and possibly sensitive targets in Baghdad (M)
news.title: U.S. Would Use Drones To Attack Iraqi Targets

news.abstract: Collapse of court case against Paul Burrell, royal butler accused of stealing hundreds of items belonging to Britain's Princess Diana, has not forestalled disclosure of embarrassing royal secrets; Burrell himself has been fielding offers from British news media, and The Sun has published torrent of revelations said to be based on his 39-page deposition to police (S)
news.title: Royal Secrets Come to Light As Butler's Tale Spills Out

news.abstract: Iran's supreme religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei pardons Abdullah Nouri, veteran cleric who three years ago had been jailed on charges of insulting Islam; Nouri was considered leading reformer at time of his arrest (S)
news.title: Iran Pardons Cleric Who Was Jailed for Insulting Islam

news.abstract: Ho Chi Minh City announces financial investment of over $9 million dollars in equipment and training for firefighters; new initiative follows fire in Vietnamese city department store that killed at least 60 people (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Vietnam: Firefighting Plans After Deadly Blaze

news.abstract: Chung Mong Joon, popular president of national soccer association, creates political party and is named candidate for South Korea's December presidential elections (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: 'Soccer Candidate' Creates Party

news.abstract: Report by American and British investigators reinforces suspicions that Ukraine secretly sold advanced air-defense equipment to Iraq more than two years ago; some Ukrainian legislators express consternation; Pres Leonid D Kuchma denies supplying Iraq with 'any weapons at all' and calls for special commission of Security Council to undertake its own inquiry into allegations; Kuchma is heard to approve proposal to sell advanced radar system to Iraq in recordings of his private conversations that were secretly taped and smuggled to US more than year ago by presidential security guard (M)
news.title: Report of Arms Sale by Ukraine to Iraq Causes Consternation

news.abstract: Report by Open Society Institute, nonprofit organization, states that corruption is rampant in Central and Eastern European countries expecting to join wealthy European Union, and is likely to persist after union expands eastward in 2004 unless EU significantly strengthens its own anticorruption measures; report, based on yearlong study, finds that three-fourths of citizens in candidate states believe that most or all of their public officials are corrupt; says corruption in legislative process is probably biggest problem facing post-Communist countries, along with kickbacks and payoffs in public procurement contracts; one bright spot is Lithuania, which adopted national anticorruption strategy in Jan and which report says could serve as model for other countries; Transparency International, anti-corruption organization, ranks current EU members Italy and Greece as more corrupt than EU applicants Slovenia and Estonia in its current corruption perception index (M)
news.title: Graft in Eastern Europe Is Called Rampant

news.abstract: The Indonesian police said today that they had arrested a man who admitted to planting the car bomb that blew up a Bali nightclub in a terrorist attack last month.
news.title: Indonesian Police Say Suspect Admits Role in Bali Bombing

news.abstract: Number of North Sea cod is believed to be at its lowest level ever, half of what was considered minimum for assured propagation; scientists are warning that unless almost all commmercial fishing in North Sea is banned, cod stocks might soon collapse; cod crisis is one of many facing international community as countries compete for thinning stocks in world's once fish-thick seas; fish are last food source hunted on large scale in wild; United Nations warns that world's 17 main fisheres are being fished at or above sustainable levels; cod, once known as 'beef of the sea,' is world's most popular food fish; photo (M)
news.title: North Sea Cod Crisis Brings Call for Nations to Act

news.abstract: Thrifty Egyptians purchase their holiday treats at wholesale market in Cairo on first day of Ramadan; it is tradition for purveyors to give pet names to their dates, nuts and other delicacies for sale; 'Yasir Arafat' and 'Osama bin Laden' dates are biggest sellers; 'Mass Destruction' moniker given to date imported from Iraq is considered too costly by most shoppers; photo (M)
news.title: Cairo Journal; Saddam's 'Weapons' Costly, 'Bush-Sharon' Cheap

news.abstract: The following is the text of President Bush's remarks on Friday following the U.N. Security Council vote to force the disarmament of Iraq, as distributed by The Associated Press.
news.title: Text of President Bush's Remarks on Security Council Vote

news.abstract: US, backed by 36 other countries, blocks German-French proposal at UN for worldwide ban on cloning to create human beings; insists that ban include all forms of human cloning(S)
news.title: U.S., Pushing for Broader Ban, Blocks U.N. Anti-Cloning Move

news.abstract: Iran's hard-line judiciary sentences outspoken reform activist Hashem Aghajari to death, 8 years in jail, 74 lashes and ten-year ban from teaching for allegedly insulting Prophet Mohammad by saying Muslims should not follow religious leaders 'blindly'; photo (S)
news.title: Iran Sentences Reformist to Death For Insult to Prophet Muhammad

news.abstract: Dutch authorities in Eindhoven report arrest of 22-year-old Moroccan they believe was planning suicide attack (S)
news.title: Dutch Say Arrest Foiled Suicide Strike

news.abstract: Syria, which has long centered foreign policy around its leadership of countries against Israel, fears being isolated in region if pro-US government is installed in Iraq; also fears being next on US list; photo (M)
news.title: Syria Fears Isolation More Than War

news.abstract: THE HAGUE: Effort To Speed Milosevic Trial; SWITZERLAND: Inquiry On Ex-Argentine Leader; NORTHERN IRELAND: Man Released In Spy Case; RUSSIA: More Ill From Tainted Dairy Products;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, Nov. 8 — Following is the White House text of President Bush's remarks today after the Security Council approved the resolution on Iraq:.
news.title: Transcript of Bush's Remarks on the Security Council's Iraq Resolution

news.abstract: Childhood home of Chinese leader Jiang Zemin, Yangzhou, has become shrine of sorts, with visitors arriving daily to view his prosperous origins; Jiang, who transformed Chinese Communism by embracing entrepreneurs and intellectuals, came from cultured middle-class family of doctors, scholars and businessmen; seems ambivalent about new attention from market-driven media and unofficial biographers after being happily lionized for years with propaganda that omitted personal details; map; photos (M)
news.title: Chinese Pilgrims Flock to Jiang Family Home

news.abstract: Chile's Supreme Court rejects bid by Argentine judge to strip former dictator Augusto Pinochet of his official immunity so he can be questioned about 1974 assassination in Buenos Aires of Gen Carlos Prats, his predecessor as Chilean Army commander; finds Pinochet, 86, is mentally incapable of taking part in probe (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Chile: Court Preserves Pinochet's Immunity

news.abstract: Maj Gen Francis Y Mahama, 60, Ghana's ambassador to Russia, says he and driver were attacked by group of young men while walking in Moscow park, latest victims of wave of racist attacks; says festive crowd did nothing to halt attack; attacks on foreigners, especially Africans and Asians, have become increasingly common in recent years in much of Russia, despite official appeals for tolerance; African envoys had earlier appealed to Foreign Ministry to do more to protect embassy employees and other Africans (M)
news.title: Ghana's Envoy to Moscow Hurt in Latest Racial Attack

news.abstract: Hakim Taniwal, former sociology professor, has rousted Afghan warlord in Khost Province with army he raised and trained using local money; his original intent was to use persuasion to oust warlord, Padsha Khan Zadran, but after months of failed negotiations Taniwal concluded that words would not work; he borrowed $125,000 from local businessmen and raised army; he now speaks proudly of how his soldiers trounced Zadran's forces in brief battle in early Sept, sending them scurrying to hills; his triumph shows how much one can get for dollar in Afghanistan these days; former professor's success is bright spot for new national government that he supports as it struggles to pay salaries and begs for foreign aid, particularly from United States; photo (M)
news.title: Afghan Professor Tames a Wild State

news.abstract: Israeli soldiers in Jenin shoot and kill Islamic Jihad leader Iyad Sawalha, accused of masterminding attacks on Israeli buses that killed 31 people; one soldier is killed and second wounded in roadside bombing in Gaza (S)
news.title: Israelis Kill Palestinian Suspected in Attacks, Then Lose a Soldier

news.abstract: Zdenko Tomanovic discusses role as 'virtual lawyer' for Slobodan Milosevic at war crimes trial in The Hague; interview; photo; former Serb leader is conducting own defense, but Tomanovic is legal associate who gathers piles of evidence, more than 150,000 documents and exhibits (M)
news.title: The Hand That Feeds Milosevic's Defense

news.abstract: Argentine politics remains as chaotic as ever, even as battered economy shows signs of finally hitting bottom; fierce dispute between Pres Eduardo Duhalde and former Pres Carlos Menem plunges governing Peronists into crisis threatening election timetable; Peronists cannot even agree when to hold presidential nominating primary; Duhalde's candidate, Carlos Reutemann, has declined to run, so Duhalde wants more time to stitch together coalition; beneficiary is Adolfo Rodriguez Saa, who is running as old-fashioned populist (M)
news.title: In Bitter Race In Argentina, Peronists Trip Each Other

news.abstract: Pres Bush reportedly sets Iraq war plan to begin with air campaign shorter than one in Persian Gulf war and feature quick ground actions to seize footholds and strikes to cut off leadership in Baghdad; plan would mass 200,000-250,000 troops for attack by air, land and sea, commencing with 'rolling start' of substantially fewer troops; calls for quick capture of territory that could be used as bases to funnel troops deeper into country, to ease pressure on nearby staging areas like Saudi Arabia; photo; Bush agrees with Gen Tommy Franks on large troop levels; air campaign would try to cut off Baghdad leadership in hopes of causing government collapse, while trying not to destroy civilian infrastructure; ground operations would likely be woven into opening stages of air war; Bush warns Iraqi generals of war crimes charges if they purposely sacrifice civilians; analysts warn Hussein prepares volunteer martyrs' brigades for suicide bombings and drawing sympathy in region, to show 'real civilian blood on Al Jazeera' (M)
news.title: WAR PLAN FOR IRAQ CALLS FOR BIG FORCE AND QUICK STRIKES

news.abstract: Members of Arab League meeting in Cairo, Egypt, voice collective support for new weapons inspections inside Iraq; want Arab experts on inspection teams; warn UN resolution should not be considered free pass for American military action; restate longstanding Arab position that Iraq must work with UN weapons inspectors; analysts say action suggests most governments in region back seeing Pres Saddam Hussein defanged, yet fear repercussions of another war in region; photos (M)
news.title: IRAQ INSPECTIONS RECEIVE APPROVAL FROM ARAB LEAGUE

news.abstract: Women with HIV fill two wards of former tuberculosis sanitarium in India's southern state of Tamil Nadu; most are wives, or widows, infected yaers ago by their husbands; many have watched their spouses sicken, and die; now their turn has come; number of new patients is so great that hospital has no more beds and offers patients straw mats on floor; Tamil Nadu has been at vanguard of AIDS epidemic in India, country with world's second-highest number of HIV cases; recognizing that India's epidemic is at pivotal point, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation will announce $100 million commitment over 5 to 10 years to combat spread of HIV and AIDS in India; foundation hopes to focus especially on prevention among mobile populations--sex workers, truckers, migrants---who carry virus from state to state; photos (L)
news.title: As AIDS Spreads, India Is Still Struggling for a Workable Strategy

news.abstract: At least one Palestinian gunman attacks kibbutz in northern Israel near border with West Bank, killing five people hours after police report foiling suicide bombing in same area; Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, militant offshoot of Yasir Arafat's Fatah movement, claims responsibility for attack; it comes even as representatives of Fatah and Hamas meet in Cairo to discuss proposed halt to attacks in Israel; photo; map (M)
news.title: A Palestinian Attack Kills 5 on a Northern Kibbutz

news.abstract: Bill Gates announced today that the foundation he and his wife established will give more than $100 million to combat AIDS in India.
news.title: Gates Foundation to Give $100 Million to Fight AIDS in India

news.abstract: Maher Arar, Syrian-born Canadian citizen, has been deported back to Syria by United States authorities on suspicions of belonging to terrorist group; decision is testing American-Canadian relations; American officials claim Arar is member of Al Qaeda, but Canadians say they have no such information; Syrians are questioning him closely, although officially Syrian government has expressed outrage that he was deported to Syria instead of Canada (M)
news.title: Tempers Flare After U.S. Sends a Canadian Citizen Back to Syria on Terror Suspicions

news.abstract: A former Communist Party leader was charged with treason for his suspected role in cutting off access to radio and television as Soviet troops invaded during the so-called Prague Spring in 1968. Karel Hoffman, 78, who later became head of the Czech Communists, was head of the telecommunications office at the time. He is accused of shutting down radio and television broadcasts before the invasion and of refusing to broadcast a condemnation of it from the reformist government.   Ian Fisher (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Czech Republic: Prague Spring Treason Charge

news.abstract: ETHIOPIA: Premier Sees 'Ghastly' Famine'; SOUTH AFRICA: More Whites Sought In Bombings;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Italian government considers what was once unthinkable: clamping down on tobacco users; Health Min Girolamo Sirchia pledges to purify indoor air; Italian Senate has approved antismoking measure forbidding cigar and cigarette smoking in public places; Pres Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has lent his support to measure (M)
news.title: Italy (Gasp!) Starts to Clear The Clouds Of Smokers

news.abstract: The government expelled two Russian diplomats for espionage in a widening diplomatic dispute said to involve spying at a subsidiary of the Ericsson telecommunications company. Press reports in Sweden have said the diplomats, who were not identified, were involved in industrial espionage related to Ericsson's military contracts. Russia's foreign ministry said it would respond appropriately, signaling tit-for-tat expulsions of Swedish diplomats in Moscow.   Steven Lee Myers (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Sweden: Russians Expelled In Spy Case

news.abstract: THE HAGUE: Milosevic Returns To Court; THE NETHERLANDS: Bosnia Inquiry Opens; GERMANY: Opposition Lashes Out At SchrÖDer; SWEDEN: Russians Expelled In Spy Case; CYPRUS: U.N. Peace Plan; POLAND: Low Turnout Prompts Concerns; CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague Spring Treason Charge;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Benjamin Netanyahu vows to expel Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat if he is elected Israel's prime minister, speech to Likud Party convention, Tel Aviv; Prime Min Ariel Sharon casts himself as responsible centrist, winning loudest applause at convention; warns move against Arafat could strain United States ties; Israeli soldiers blow up home of Palestinian leader Muhammad Nayfeh, Shuwaika, West Bank; army says he sent gunman who killed five people at Kibbutz Metzer; Israeli forces backed by dozens of tanks and helicopters reportedly launch predawn raid on Nablus; photos (M)
news.title: Netanyahu Vows to Oust Arafat if Elected

news.abstract: Russia's lower house of parliament rejected two proposals today to create an independent commission to investigate the circumstances surrounding the 57-hour siege of a Moscow theater.
news.title: Commission to Investigate Moscow Siege Is Rejected

news.abstract: Concern mounted about the fate of the trial of Slobodan Milosevic after it was halted again yesterday because of what court officials said was his exhaustion and high blood pressure. The judges at the United Nations war crimes tribunal have called on lawyers to find ways of cutting back the trial schedule and workload even further than they have done. Various proposals are being debated, including imposing a defense counsel on the former Yugoslav president or even releasing him temporarily. The court is expected to hold a hearing to discuss a solution, but for now, proceedings involving Mr. Milosevic are suspended. They had resumed on Monday for the first time since they were stopped on Nov. 1 because of his health problems.   Marlise Simons (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: The Hague: Milosevic Ailing Again

news.abstract: The government said that human remains returned by North Korea that were supposed to be those of a kidnapped Japanese were of the wrong sex and age. The disagreement was the latest setback to efforts by the countries to normalize diplomatic relations after North Korea admitted kidnapping 13 Japanese to work in its spy programs beginning in the late 1970's. Japan said the remains, officially presented as those of a Japanese man abducted in 1980, were probably those of a woman 20 years older. North Korea has said 8 of the 13 abducted people are dead.   Howard W. French (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: Another Setback With North Korea

news.abstract: Iraq said today that it would "deal with" a resolution obliging it to disarm and allow United Nations weapons inspectors to begin work, but it denied that it possessed any prohibited weapons.
news.title: Iraq Accepts United Nations Resolution; Weapons Inspectors Leave for Baghdad on Monday

news.abstract: Young elite of India's high-tech revolution gather in Bangalore to greet Bill Gates on his first visit to India's technology capital, where his example has provided inspiration and where Microsoft is key customer, supplier and partner; photo; map; city, like Seattle before it, has become hub of enormous software services industry and home to thousands of young computer professions (M)
news.title: A Guru, Visiting India, Is Welcomed to Seattle

news.abstract: Experts in voice authenticity says it is not surprising that officials cannot be absolutely certain that audiotape broadcast said to be by Osama bin laden is actually his voice; explain how imposter might imitate voice, which intelligence officials say is 90 percent likely to be bin Laden (M)
news.title: Experts Say a bin Laden Impostor Could Fool a Lot of People

news.abstract: Iraq says it will allow United Nations weapons inspectors to begin work; grudgingly agrees to 'deal with' Security Council resolution obligating it to disarm; nine-page letter, submitted from Iraqi Foreign Min Naji Sabri to Secretary General Kofi Annan, seethes with hostility toward United States and repeatedly denies Pres Bush's assertion that Iraq has weapons of mass destruction; Bush has no specific reaction to letter, saying only there will be 'no negotiations with Saddam Hussein'; further confrontation between Washington and Baghdad is expected; administration officials say they are content for now to wait until Dec 8--deadline for Iraq to submit complete list of its weapons programs--before making issue of violations; Annan urges patience from White House; some Security Council members view war as justified only if Iraq flagrantly violates new inspections regime; gap appears to be growing between those nations and Bush administration; letter from Iraq rages against Americans and British, calling them 'gang of evil'; photo (M)
news.title: IRAQ TELLS THE U.N. ARMS INSPECTIONS WILL BE PERMITTED

news.abstract: German prosecutors say brain of urban guerrilla Ulrike Meinhof, which was removed after her suicide in 1976, will be returned to her family; daughter had filed lawsuit (S)
news.title: Family to Get Brain of German Radical

news.abstract: Jiang Zemin's retirement as China's Communist party chief is confirmed as he triumphantly closes party congress glorifying his 13-year tenure (S)
news.title: China's President Steps Down to Make Way for New Generation

news.abstract: Man in the News profile of Hu Jintao, new leader of China; he is veteran Communist Party insider who never strays from party's prescribed oratory; his past suggests that he values power over vision; photo (M)
news.title: Mystery Man At the Helm Hu Jintao

news.abstract: Tensions over immigration in France burst into open as police raid Catholic church in Calais, taking away in buses nearly 100 Iraqi Kurd and Afghan migrants who had taken refuge there; nine days ago, bowing to pressure from Britain, French government decreed that overcrowded refugee camp set up by Red Cross three years ago in nearby Sangatte would no longer accept new arrivals; goal is to stop thousands of migrants from risking their lives trying to get into Britain by jumping on high-speed trains through Channel Tunnel or as stowaways on ferries; map; photo (M)
news.title: French Police Oust Migrants Who Took Refuge in Church

news.abstract: italian premier names rising appreni
news.title: Italian Premier Names Rising Apprentice as Foreign Minister

news.abstract: Posters of children killed by Israeli Army gunfire cover walls of alleys among bullet-scarred buildings of Palestinian refugee camp in Rafah, Gaza Strip, reminder that two 2-year-olds were shot dead there in three days this week; 8-year-old boy dies of wounds received last month in daily violence in Rafah (M)
news.title: Where the Violence Is Deadly and Daily, a Palestinian Camp Mourns Its Slain Children

news.abstract: Sen Bob Graham, Democrat and chairman of Senate Intelligence Committee, charges that Bush administration has been distracted from fight against terrorism by preparation for possible invasion of Iraq; American intelligence agencies come under renewed attack in Congress for failing to find Osama bin Laden; increasing certainty that he is still alive prompts senior Democratic senators to say effort to dismantle Al Qaeda is failure; Graham says American intelligence agencies must determine extent of terrorist threat at home before any military action is taken in Iraq; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld, in radio interview, underscores concerns that US could face increased dangers of terrorist attacks if Pres Bush orders military action against Iraq; says Pres Saddam Hussein might orchestrate such attacks; administration officials take FBI to task for warning issued on Nov 13 about possible attacks on hospitals, but FBI issues another warning, saying Al Qaeda's highest-priority targets remain within aviation, petroleum and nuclear sectors, as well as significant national landmarks (M)
news.title: Little Headway In Terror War, Democrats Say

news.abstract: British government introduces legislation to allow pubs and bars to stay open 24 hours a day; hopes to put end to binge drinking that occurs when last call for drinks is made at 11 pm (S)
news.title: Pub Beer Is Still Warm, Even 24/7

news.abstract: Twelve Israelis are killed in Hebron on West Bank when Palestinian snipers ambush Jewish settlers walking home from Sabbath prayers and then attack policemen, security guards and soldiers rushing to rescue; gunfight rages for more than three hours as Israeli rescue workers struggle to evacuate wounded; soldiers kill at least three Palestinians whom they identify as killers; Islamic Jihad claims responsibility for attack; Israeli leaders hold Palestinian leadership of Yasir Arafat responsible; photos; map (M)
news.title: 12 ISRAELIS KILLED IN HEBRON AMBUSH NEAR PRAYER SITE

news.abstract: Maan, tribal town in desert in south Jordan, has been sealed off for nearly a week as police and army officials chase down Muhammad Ahmad al-Chalabi, who is known as Abu Sayyaf, small-time Islamic militant accused of heading defiant gang of drug and arms smugglers; operation is of scope rarely seen in Jordan, and people of Maan are angry; photos; map (M)
news.title: Broad Manhunt in Jordan Isolates, and Angers, a Town

news.abstract: LONDON—  As they took their seats in the room where Henry Wyndham, chairman of Sotheby's Europe, was about to dispose of the Beck collection of German Expressionist art on Oct. 8, few professionals felt sure of what would happen. This was the first serious sale of 20th-century paintings in the troubled economic environment of the opening season, followed a day later by another contingent of pictures from the same school. Would it, could it, work?
news.title: ARTS & ANTIQUES: The lure of Expressionism

news.abstract: Condoleezza Rice, Pres Bush's national security adviser, says administration is taking extra precautions to protect nation's most critical facilities from terrorist assaults after FBI warning that Al Qaeda may be planning 'spectacular attacks' with mass casualties in US; rejects criticism from Senate Democrats that Bush's focus on preparations for war against Iraq is distracting him from campaign against terrorism; intelligence officials say senior Qaeda operative has been captured and taken into American custody (M)
news.title: Terror Alert Brings New Steps To Prevent Attacks, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Germans are angry about raft of taxes on individuals and companies that Chancellor Gerhard Schroder has proposed in desperate effort to reduce budget deficit that has breached limit set by European Union; Schroder, who won re-election by reed-thin margin in September after campaign in which he said little about taxes, says dire condition of public finance became clear only after elections; photo; map (M)
news.title: Schröder's Tax Surprise Angers Many Germans

news.abstract: South Africa's foreign minister, Dr Nkosazana Zuma, meets with Zimbabwean counterpart, Stan Mudenge, and afterwards says Western nations should consider ending penalties they imposed on Zimbabwe for intimidating opposition party supporters, judges, journalists and white farmers, and manipulating presidential election; calls on Britain to compensate white farmers who have been forced to give up their farms without compensation; comments draw outrage from supporters of Zimbabwe's opposition party and many political analysts in South Africa (M)
news.title: South Africa Urges the West To Ease Censure of Zimbabwe

news.abstract: Peru Possible, party of Pres Alejandro Toledo, is expected to suffer stinging setback in nationwide elections intended to decentralize Peru's government with creation of 25 new government bodies; Toledo plays down his troubles, explaining that his government has had difficult task of solidifying democracy while satisfying needs during his 16 months in power; latest poll shows his approval rating at 23 percent, up from 11 percent earlier this year; photo; map (M)
news.title: Peruvian Leader's Party Fears Setback in Regional Voting

news.abstract: Abdullah Gul, moderate politician from party with Muslim roots, is named prime minister of Turkey, and he expresses confidence that country's democracy and its Western leanings can thrive under Islamic leadership; affirms Tukey's friendship with US and its membership in NATO (M)
news.title: Turkey Turns To Moderate In Islamic Party As New Premier

news.abstract: Israeli settlers hold services for 12 people killed in ambush in Hebron on Nov 15; victims were five border police soldiers, four regular army soldiers and three civilian security guards from nearby Israeli settlement of Kiryat Arba; Islamic Jihad has claimed responsibility for attack, calling it retaliation for Israel's killing of its local leader in West Bank city of Jenin; Israeli leaders are considering their response; photo (M)
news.title: As Settlers Pray for the Dead, Israel Weighs Retaliation

news.abstract: Organizers of $75,000 annual Booker Prize, Britain's premier literary award, agree to maintain rules that permit only British, Commonwealth and Irish writers to compete; organizers are contemplating introducing second prize--to be awarded less frequently--for lifetime literary achievement, and that could be open to Americans (M)
news.title: Booker Prize Won't Include U.S. Writers

news.abstract: Salaam Abid, portrait painter, has devoted his career to painting Pres Saddam Hussein; he complains that business has been slow since new business opened on sidewalk opposite his gallery in Baghdad, offering lifesize, backlit photographs of Hussein, reproduced on all-weather fabric and mounted on aluminum frames; photographs are new fashion among those eager to have Hussein ever-present in their offices, courtyards and living rooms; Abid is scornful of photographs; photo (M)
news.title: Baghdad Journal; When It Comes to Iraq's Boss, What Is Face Value?

news.abstract: News from Japan about citizens kidnapped by North Korea many years ago enrages relatives of nearly 500 South Koreans who went missing over last quarter century, and are believed to be held against their will in North Korea; South Korean government, unlike Japan, has never made public issue of kidnappings, eager to defuse tensions with its heavily armed neighbor; it has never demanded their return, even as it provided hundreds of millions of dollars in aid to North in recent years; photo (M)e
news.title: Korean Kidnappings: The South's Wound

news.abstract: Knife-wielding man tries to hijack Israeli passenger jet from Tel Aviv minutes before its landing in Istanbul, but he is tackled by air marshals as he tries to force his way into pilots' cabin; nobody on board El Al jet is injured; Turkey's state-run news agency identifies suspect as Tevfik Fukra, 23-year-old Israeli Arab; Turkish police are interrogating him trying to determine motives behind attack; attempted hijacking is unusual for El Al, widely regarded as world's most heavily guarded airline; photo (M)
news.title: Attempted Hijacking Foiled Aboard an Israeli Airliner

news.abstract: Venezuelan troops try to consolidate their hold on 8,000-member police force in Caracas, day after Pres Hugo Chavez's government orders management of department taken away from Mayor Alfredo Pena, staunch opponent of president; tension rises in country and it remains unclear how much of grip Chavez's government has on Police Dept; Pena claims several top-ranking police officials remain loyal to him and to his police chief; photos (M)
news.title: Venezuelan President's Troops Try to Tighten Noose Around Caracas Mayor's Police Forces

news.abstract: The Labor Party chose as its standard-bearer Amram Mitzna, who campaigned on immediate peace negotiations.
news.title: Labor Party in Israel Names Former General as Its Leader

news.abstract: Body of Mir Aimal Kasi, executed in Virginia, is welcomed home by hundreds in Quetta, Pakistan; he was convicted of killing two CIA employees in US in 1993 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Pakistan: Body Of Man Executed In U.S. Is Back

news.abstract: Clean-up crews begin removing sludge from beaches in northwestern Spain fouled when stricken tanker Prestige leaked over 3,000 tons of fuel oil into Atlantic; spill threatens birds, marine life and livelihood of thousands of fishermen in region famous for seafood; calmer weather has allowed tugs to tow tanker, which began to leak again, to area southwest of coast; ship will remain serious environmental threat until its 77,000 tons of fuel oil can be loaded onto another tanker; Spain has refused ship access to any port and seeks to exploit crisis in talks with Britain on future of Gibraltar, British colony claimed by Spain; Britain denies Gibraltar has any link to accident (M)
news.title: Oil From Crippled Ship Fouling Beaches in Spain

news.abstract: United States Sergeant Fernando Nino's court-martial begins in South Korea; stands accused of negligent homicide in death of two local teenage girls; his vehicle struck girls during military exercise (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Trial For G.I. Sergeant

news.abstract: islamic allies in pakistan fail in talks f
news.title: Islamic Allies In Pakistan Fail in Talks For Coalition

news.abstract: Iraqi opposition groups move conference on replacing Saddam Hussein's government from Belgium to London and delay it until mid-Dec amid quarreling and reduced expectations; proposed new date and place emerged only after several groups met with team from State Department, Pentagon and National Security Council, which pressed them to resolve differences and reconsider agenda; opposition leader Sharif Ali bin al-Hussein says up to 400 delegates may be invited to represent wide range of groups; Belgium reportedly blocked conference because opposition's goal of toppling Saddam Hussein is beyond United Nation's goal of disarming him; former Iraqi Gen Nizar al-Khazraji, who defected in 1995, is charged in Denmark with taking part in war crimes for his supposed role in supervising officer who killed Iraqi civilians in 1988 during campaign in which as many as 182,000 Kurds were killed; photo (M)
news.title: Setbacks Dealt to Iraqi Opposition in Europe

news.abstract: Thousands of middle-class Venezuelans opposed to Pres Hugo Chavez and his miliary takeover of Caracas police march peacefully through city demanding force be restored to civilian control; are jeered by Chavez supporters, who are eventually dispersed by National Guard troops to let delegation of 12 mayors and governors deliver statement to National Assembly; Caracas Mayor Alfredo Pena urges Chavez to submit to nonbiding referendum; threatens new national strike; photo (M)
news.title: Venezuelan Marchers Want Police Restored to Civilian Rule

news.abstract: United States Army Sergeant Fernando Nino is acquitted of negligent homicide; stood trial for deaths of two local teenage girls struck by his vehicle during military excercise (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: G.I. Found Not Guilty

news.abstract: Thirty-seven people are arrested in Italy for embezzlement of public works funds allotted to modernize Salerno-Reggio Calabria highway; police suspect Calabrian mob is involved in crime; map (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Charges Of Highway Robbery

news.abstract: Communities along Spain's northern coast gird for widespread oil contamination as crippled tanker Prestige splits in two and sinks over 100 miles offshore; about 2 million gallons of its nearly 20-million-gallon load spills when tanker founders after leaking trail of fuel oil for six days from widening crack in its unlined hull; environmental groups call for accelerating shift to sturdier tanker designs with double hulls; sinking raises questions about Spain's decision to order disabled ship towed offshore, where its load could now threaten broader region; experts say it could take week for newly spilled oil to reach shore; say 90 percent of load that sank with ship is likely to congeal in deep water, but could rise to warmer surface and liquefy again if compartments shatter when hull hits bottom; table of major oil spills; map; photo (M)
news.title: Oil Tanker Splits Apart Off Spain, Threatening Coast

news.abstract: The governments of Britain, Australia, Denmark and several other nations said today that they were strongly considering formal requests from the United States to join a military coalition against Iraq, if weapons inspections fail.    The countries are among more than 50 nations that American diplomats have been contacting this week in foreign capitals and at the NATO summit meeting in Prague to discuss participating either in an invasion or postwar reconstruction effort in Iraq, administration officials said.
news.title: Several Nations Weigh U.S. Request to Join Forces Against Iraq

news.abstract: A young American evangelist was shot dead today at a clinic where she worked as a nurse's assistant in Lebanon.
news.title: American Missionary Is Shot Dead in Lebanon

news.abstract: Pres Bush's speech in Prague on using military force, if needed, to disarm Iraq was less rousing then his Sept speech to United Nations, apparently because NATO is not prepared politically and militarily for fight; Germany remains greatest political obstacle (M)
news.title: A Call to Arms: Bush's Plea on Iraq

news.abstract: South Korean Navy boat fires warning to North Korean patrol which crossed sea border into south; no fire is returned and vessel withdraws to North Korean waters (S)
news.title: World Business Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Shots Fired At Northern Boat

news.abstract: State Department, responding to latest Osama bin Laden audiotape, warns Americans around world may be terrorist targets (S)
news.title: Global Terrorism Warning

news.abstract: Indonesian authorities use ATM records to trace and arrest Imam Samudra, major suspect in Bali nightclub bombing in October; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesians, Tracing A.T.M. Use, Arrest Major Suspect in Bali Bombing

news.abstract: Fierce winds blow oil slicks from shipwrecked tanker Prestige closer to coast of northwest Spain, where viscous black fuel oil has washed up on beaches south of 150 miles of coast already contaminated; map; fishing and tourism are hard hit and local officials are bitterly critical of central government's efforts (M)
news.title: Anger Spreads With Oil Spill Along Imperiled Spanish Coast

news.abstract: Britain's 50,000 firefighters returned to the picket lines on an eight-day strike today after talks broke down.
news.title: British Firefighters Back on Strike as Pay Talks Collapse

news.abstract: Nineteen NATO leaders, meeting in Prague, unite behind Pres Bush and strongly condemn Iraq for failing to meet UN demands to surrender weapons of mass destruction; Germany's continuing opposition to war will likely prevent alliance from formally entering campaign, although many members appear willing to do so on ad hoc basis; leaders agree to establish rapid reaction force that could move swiftly around globe and keep NATO relevant in fight against terrorism; final session hears Latvian Pres Vaira Vike-Freiberga thank leaders for admitting raft of militarily weak nations craving stability that Poland, Hungary and Czech Republic have enjoyed since their admission in 1999; Latvian leader points to her country's long loss of independence and recalls growing up as refugee until she settled in Canada, where she was noted psychologist; photos; map; political split on Iraq is evident as seven nations formally invited into NATO join with aspiring members Albania, Croatia and Macedonia to issue muscular declarations on Iraq; German-American rift preoccupies meeting; Pres Bush and Chancellor Gerhard Schroder twice shake hands and exchange pleasantries but Min Joschka Fischer reiterates opposition to military action (M)
news.title: NATO LEADERS SAY IRAQ MUST DISARM

news.abstract: Latest television reality show in Britain is on-air autopsy performed by German doctor, Gunther von Hagens, with 'almost droning commentary'; scene takes place beneath large copy of Rembrandt's Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp; photos; von Hagens could face prosecution for violating laws dating to 1832 that banned public autopsies to stop body snatching; his current exhibit, Body Worlds, consisting of preserved cross sections of human cadavers, has drawn million visitors to London gallery (M)
news.title: Art or Ghoulishness? Autopsy Is TV Spectacle in Britain

news.abstract: BERLIN—  Holly-Jane Rahlens, a novelist, director and performance artist, has lived in Berlin for 30 years. Her just-published young adult novel, "Prince William, Maximilian Minsky and Me," has received outstanding reviews in Germany, and the nice Jewish girl from Queens has grown into the able chronicler of Jewish life in Berlin.
news.title: AtHomeAbroad: When life in a different culture becomes a time for self-invention

news.abstract: President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia welcomed President Bush to his hometown today, then raised pointed questions about the reliability of two important American allies in the campaign against terrorism, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.    In remarks made at Mr. Bush's side in the majestic setting of Catherine Palace outside St. Petersburg, Mr. Putin also suggested that the disappearance of Osama bin Laden, the leader of Al Qaeda, was a major piece of unfinished business as the Bush administration focused its attention on a possible war in Iraq.
news.title: PUTIN QUESTIONS U.S. TERROR ALLIES

news.abstract: In the last four months, Tatyana and Sergei Akadanovy have been arrested twice, sent to jail for 10 days and fined more than $1,000, an unimaginable sum in impoverished Belarus.    An apartment they help rent has been broken into and vandalized. Mrs. Akadanova has been severely beaten on the steps of their apartment, a fate that separately befell six friends, and the police have issued warnings that the Akadanovys and their friends are all criminals who should be avoided.
news.title: New Belarus Law Codifies Rising Religious Repression

news.abstract: The opposition coalition seeking a referendum on President Hugo Chávez announced that it would mount a nationwide general strike on Dec. 2, or earlier if conditions warrant. It would be the fourth general strike since December in the conflict between Mr. Chavéz and his opponents. The announcement was the latest setback to the talks between the government and the opposition, which are mediated by the Organization of American States.   David Gonzalez (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Venezuela: Opposition Sets Strike Date

news.abstract: Before his arrest, Robert William Pickton kept several menacing signs outside his pig farm, including one that read: ''No Visitors, Agents, Peddlers or Salespeople -- Admittance by Appointment Only!! (No Exceptions).'' Another said, ''This property is protected by: Pit Bull With AIDS.''    The police and prosecutors say he had reason to be cautious. The remains of 18 women have been found on his 15-acre property in a nearby suburb, and investigators say many more may turn up before they are through.
news.title: Mounties Dig Up Body Parts in Serial Killing Case

news.abstract: Six member nations of South American common market called Mercosur approve plan that will allow their 250 million people to live and work in any other member country and be granted same rights as citizens of those nations; Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay are founders and full members; Bolivia and Chile joined later and are associate members; six countries have combined gross product of more than $1 trillion; Mercosur is world's third-largest trade group (M)
news.title: South American Trading Bloc Frees Movement of Its People

news.abstract: Oil from stricken tanker Prestige is threatening aquarium at La Coruna, Spain, which fills its tanks with seawater; fuel oil shed by elderly tanker Prestige along coast of Galicia for six days threatens city of La Coruna as well; aquarium's tanks have not yet been polluted, but omens are not good; two resident seals are stained with oil; aquarium could survive for three days without pumping in any seawater; many of 35,000 fish might survive transfer elsewhere, but not 62 species of invertebrates; photo; map (M)
news.title: Aquarium in Spain Faces Disaster With Oil Spilled From Ship at Its Walls

news.abstract: Israeli military admits that it was shot fired by one of its soldiers that killed senior United Nations official Iain John Hook at agency's compound in Jenin refugee camp in West Bank; Israeli statement claims that Palestinian gunmen had been firing at soldiers from inside small UN compound; this is potentially serious accusation given implication that UN officials sheltered gunmen in some way; charge is likely to increase friction between Israeli government and UN (M)
news.title: Israel Admits One of Its Soldiers Killed U.N. Official in Jenin

news.abstract: Government of Saudi Arabia says wife of Saudi ambassador to Washington gave tens of thousands of dollars in what she believed were charitable gifts to family of Saudi man in San Diego who befriended and assisted two of Sept 11 hijackers; Saudi officials and their American friends say payments from Princess Haifa al-Faisal, wife of Amb Bandar bin Sultan, began four years ago, and they were typical of charitable gifts she provided to Saudis in distress, many of them strangers who asked for help by mail; suggestion that money from Saudi royal family may have been used, if only indirectly, to help hijackers and their friends has created alarm in Riyadh and in Washington (M)
news.title: Saudis Say Cash to Friend Of Hijackers Was Charity

news.abstract: National elections Nov 24 figure to be among closest in Austria's history, as nation's traditional center-left and center-right parties battle for largest plurality and right to name next chancellor; most intriguing political story concerns certain loser: country's self-destructing right-wing Freedom Party and Jorg Haider, its once magnetic but now increasingly marginalized leader; Haider became international pariah during 1990's for praising Hitler's labor policies; political analysts say voters have grown tired of his antics; photo (M)
news.title: Austria Expects Close Election As Far Right Yields to Center

news.abstract: German television broadcasts first German-made film that tries to play country's darkest period for laughs; 90-minute farce 'Goebbels and Geduldig' is about Nazi propaganda minister and Jewish concentration camp inmate who looks identical to him; until not, poking fun at Nazis has been taboo in Germany; critics pan film, saying it is not funny (M)
news.title: German Comedy Lances the Nazis, but 'The Producers' Is Safe

news.abstract: Queen Elizabeth's husband Prince Philip makes public denial of news reports that he sent Princess Diana insulting letters calling her 'harlot' and 'trollop'; report first appeared in one British newspaper and was picked up by every other newspaper in Britain's fiercely competitive press (S)
news.title: Philip Denies Calling Diana Vulgar Names

news.abstract: Top Republicans and Democrats criticized the role of the Saudis in the campaign against terrorism, and suggested that the administration was too timid in confronting them.   Article, Page A13.
news.title: Senators Assail Saudis

news.abstract: Provincial government of British Columbia embarks on one of most expensive engineeering projects in Canada's history, to widen and improve Route 99, treacherous road called Highway of Death in local news media; Vancouver fears that highway's deadly reputation could threaten its bid to host 2010 Winter Olympic games; alpine resort of Whistler, off Route 99, would host many events; photo; map (M)
news.title: Whistler Journal; Repair of British Columbia Road Is Olympic Event

news.abstract: It was one of several clashes today in Nablus, in which a reported seven people were injured by fire from Israeli tanks and guns.
news.title: Israeli Soldiers Fire on Crowd, Killing Boy

news.abstract: US State Dept urges Americans to defer nonessential travel to Nepal because of written threat from Maoist rebels to attack American diplomats (S)
news.title: U.S., Citing Maoist Threats, Warns Against Visits to Nepal

news.abstract: Iran's National Security Council reportedly bars students from further demonstrations backing Hashem Aghajari, pro-reform scholar sentenced to death, after supreme religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei orders review of case; students vow to press their demands through other peaceful means (M)
news.title: Iran Forbids Demonstrations Defending a Reformist Scholar

news.abstract: Tanker carrying liquid petroleum gas continues to burn twenty-four miles from Hong Kong; winds continue to keep fire from flamable cargo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Hong Kong: Tanker Still Burning

news.abstract: America remains as dependent as ever on Saudi Arabia for oil, nearly 12 years after Persian Gulf war when reliance on Saudi supplies prompted calls for US to diversify sources; Saudi Arabia supplies approximately one-sixth of US imports, but has considerable political strength as only producer with spare capacity to replace millions of barrels daily, which could be drained from market by US military action against Iraq; produces approximately eight million barrels per day; officials say it could raise output to 10 million barrels fairly quickly and to 10.5 million within three months; US Energy Department official Guy Caruso says if war halts Iraq's exports of between 1.5 million to 2 million barrels daily, situation would be manageable; says it would be harder to replace steeper decline in exports, which would occur if exports from other Persian Gulf suppliers are reduced by terrorist attacks or by prohibitive insurance premiums on oil tankers; graphs; chart (M)
news.title: U.S. Fails to Curb Its Saudi Oil Habit, Experts Say

news.abstract: Attack on temple in Jammu, India, prompts curfew in Kashmir's winter capital; Indian government blames Pakistan-based militants for assault (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Kashmir: Caution And Blame After Attack

news.abstract: French antiterrorist police arrest six men thought to belong to Islamic militant network that supported Richard C Reid, Briton who admitted trying to blow up American Airlines trans-Atlantic flight last Dec with explosives hidden in his shoes; predawn raid is latest in four waves of arrests in four days, as police remain on high alert to thwart possible attacks by radical Islamic groups; worshippers complain about raid on Islamic center, where Imam Kamel Din was among those detained; photo (M)
news.title: French Link 6 to 'Shoe Bomb' Attempt; 12 Other Militants Seized in Paris Raids

news.abstract: AUSTRIA: Haider Flip-Flops On Resignation; NORTHERN IRELAND: Arrests On Both Sides; DENMARK: Chechen'S Detention Extended; RUSSIA: Return Of A `Sacred' Star; BELARUS: At Least One Friend, Maybe;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: United Nations AIDS program head Dr Peter Piot says women for first time make up about half of adults infected with HIV worldwide, chiefly as result of sexual intercourse with infected men; 19.2 million of 38.6 million adults infected with AIDS virus are women; figures largely reflect epidemic in sub-Saharan Africa, where nearly 1 in 11 adults are infected and women account for 58 percent of infections; similar parity has been reached in Caribbean, North Africa and Mideast; graph of percentage of infected women by region (M)
news.title: Women With H.I.V. Reach Half of Global Cases

news.abstract: House in Jenin refugee camp explodes, killinging suspected high-level Palestinian militants Ala Sabaar and Aimad Nasharta; Palestinian witnesses blame missile fired from Israeli military aircraft; says Israeli tanks and armored vehicles entered West Bank camp just before blast; military official says Army did not fire on house; Israeli military activity in West Bank and Gaza has picked up since suicide attack in Jerusalem; Israeli military releases recording of phone message United Nations aide Iain John Hook reportedly left with Israeli civil officals minutes before he was shot in Jenin by Israeli soldiers; apparently seeks to bolster its claims that Palestinian gunmen had been firing on Israeli troops from inside UN compound; photo (M)
news.title: West Bank Explosion Kills 2 'Most Wanted'

news.abstract: Spanish Prime Min Jose Maria Aznar and French Pres Jacques Chirac, spurred by oil spill from tanker Prestige, set rigourous inspection standards for older single-hulled tankers carrying oil or tar through waters their nations control; empower maritime authorities to inspect ships up to 200 miles out to sea and to expel those not considered seaworthy from 200-mile zone (M)
news.title: After Oil Spill, Spain and France Impose Strict Tanker Inspections

news.abstract: Tamil leader Velupillai Prabhakaran declares rebels will make attempt at secession from Sri Lanka if group is not given autonomy, speech to his guerrilla fighters (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Sri Lanka: Rebel Leader Demands Autonomy

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder says that he will grant United States unrestricted freedom to fly in German airspace, as well as to shuttle troops in and out of American military bases there; reiterates, however, that Germany will not take part in war against Iraq; also says Germany would supply Israel with German-made armored vehicles and Patriot antimissile system to protect it from Iraqi chemical, biological or nuclear attack (M)
news.title: 'Clear as Glass' Against War With Iraq, Germans Still Agree to Aid U.S. and Israel

news.abstract: Entrepreneur and Chinese national Yang Bin is arrested by Chinese authorities and charged with bribery and fraud; also faces regional charges in Shenyang for illegally occupying farmland; charges have stopped him from assuming duties as head of new North Korean zone near China that was devised to attract foreign investors; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Tycoon Charged With Corruption

news.abstract: Three suicide car bombers killed themselves and 12 others at an Israeli-owned hotel in Mombasa, Kenya. Missiles fired at an Israeli airliner missed their target.
news.title: In Kenya, 3 Suicide Bombers Attack Hotel Owned by Israelis; Missiles Fired at Passenger Jet

news.abstract: Proposed bans on cod and haddock catches are to be debated by European Union fisheries ministers; European Fisheries Commissioner Franz Fischler supports cuts to preserve industry while protecting stocks; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Belgium: Fishing Ban Considered

news.abstract: Nigerian Pres Olusegun Obasanjo visits Kaduna in wake of clashes between Muslims and Christians; visits riot victims; religious strife, which has erupted with some regularity in region, is not likely to end with decision to move Miss World beauty contest from Abuja to London; map; photos (M)
news.title: Fiery Zealotry Leaves Nigeria in Ashes Again

news.abstract: Question of whether Israelis attacked in Kenya and while voting in Israel, surely victims of at least two different organizations, are victims of same worldwide terror drive goes to heart of Bush administration's widening fight against terrorism and Israel's focused conflict with Palestinians; United States and Israel have drawn ever closer since Sept 11 attacks, but differ over whether treating two conflicts as one and same would help or hinder in resolving either fight; Israelis see Kenya attacks, in which Israelis have fallen victims to terrorism with global reach, showing fallacy of Bush criticism of Israeli efforts against Palestinian terrorism that are similar to US antiterrorist efforts (M)
news.title: Fight Against Terror: Two Conflicts or One?

news.abstract: Spanish police hold seven people suspected to be members of far-left group Grapo, which has been labeled terrorist organization by US and European Union (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Spain: Leftists Accused Of Terrorism Arrested

news.abstract: Venezuela's Supreme Court apparently blocks move by Electoral Council to hold nonbiding referendum on whether Pres Hugo Chavez should resign; finds council needed at least 4-1 majority to act, rather than simple majority it mustered; Chavez's government rejects council move (M)2
news.title: Venezuela Court Blocks Order for Nonbinding Vote on President

news.abstract: Two men and two women in Northern Ireland are charged with 1999 funding of IRA guns and ammunition smuggled from US (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Northern Ireland: Four Charged In Gun Plot

news.abstract: International Monetary Fund, in unusually blunt confidential report, documents disappearance of almost $1 billion from Angola's treasury in 2001; cites widespread corruption; Angoloan officials reportedly are furious about report, which was completed in Mar and widely circulated among donor nations and multilateral organizations; need IMF support to raise funds from donor nations they say are needed to rebuild war-ravaged infrastructure (M)
news.title: I.M.F. Skewers Corruption in Angola

news.abstract: Japan's Foreign Minister Yoriko Kawaguchi reports that ministry has disciplined 39 officials who doctored expense reports defrauding government of almost $4 million dollars; Vice Minister Yukio Takeuchi and Deputy Vice Minister Shinichi Kitajima are censured; last year 328 officials were similarly exposed and punished (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: Financial Scandal Uncovered

news.abstract: Disrupting terrorist attacks is becoming even more daunting as terrorist increasingly attack 'soft' targets like Israeli-owned Mombasa, Kenya, resort; at issue is deciding where to focus security and intelligence resources if enemy is able to strike almost anywhere; intelligence officials around world say they have become much more aggressive in collecting and distributing intelligence tips, even about unlikely threats; Australian officials say they got reports two weeks ago about threat in Mombasa, leading them to urge citizens not to go there; say all such data is automatically passed to United States; American officials say they were unaware of any credible and specific data that could have predicted attacks on hotel and on Israeli plane (M)
news.title: Wide Reach Of Terrorism

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, who has long promised economic reforms, faces questions about whether he has courage and political capital to tackle woes with his popularity falling and economy tipping toward second recession in year; pressure to address problems is coming from within Germany and from nation's European Union partners; labor unions and other vested interests that form base of Schoder's support have stymied reform and upcoming elections in two states make it hard for Schroder or opposition to propose unpopular measures; graph; photo (M)
news.title: Does Schröder Have Political Capital to Reform Economy?

news.abstract: Question of succession to Cambodia's throne, once taboo, has recently become subject of debate and speculation, prodded by King Norodom Sihanouk himself, who is 80 and ailing; hundreds of descendants of any of three past kings are eligible under 1993 Constitution; supporters of Prime Min Hun Sen control Throne Council, which will choose next king; Hun Sen has blocked bill clarifying succession process, but cannot simply ignore wishes of popular king; Prince Norodom Sihamoni, one of king's many sons, has emerged as strong possibility, even though he spends much of his time in Paris and has taken little interest in royal affairs; photo (M)
news.title: Shuffling 'Heirs' to Cambodia Throne

news.abstract: US military officials say Americans and Philippines may soon start new military training operation against Muslim extremists in southern Philippines; it would involve 300 to 400 American troops, including many on jungle combat patrols in risky hunt for Abu Sayyaf guerrilla force; group was target of training mission carried out by American forces on island of Basilan earlier in year, but only one leader, Abu Sayyaf, was killed in that mission, and group's other leaders have regrouped in Sulu Province, principally on Jolo Island; photo; map (M)
news.title: U.S. and Philippines May Start New Training Mission

news.abstract: Amber miners of Simojovel, Mexico, earn very little for their backbreaking and dangerous work: salary of no more than $2 or $3 a day, plus as little as $2.50 a week for amber that they might hack from earth; they work hand-hewn, hundred-foot tunnels without benefit of safety standards, rules and regulations; Simojovel has one of world's few known mother lodes of amber, and its amber is reputed to be best; photos; map (M)
news.title: A Friend in India to All the World

news.abstract: A P J Abdul Kalam, India's Muslim president, pays visit to Sri Sathya Sai Baba, Hindu holy man at ashram in Puttaparthy, who preaches unusual mixture of faiths and encourages nonviolence; photo; map (M)
news.title: Indonesian Human Rights Court Acquits 4 in East Timor Killings

news.abstract: American officials find it hard to stop flow of money from wealthy Saudis and Saudi-financed charities to people and groups deemed by US to be supporting terrorist attacks around the world; report sponsored by Council on Foreign Relations in November said Saudi Arabia was largest source of financing for Al Qaeda and blamed both American and Saudi governments for not being tough enough; some 300 Saudi charities dispense as much as $4 billion a year (M)
news.title: Saudi Arabia Is Called Slow in Helping Stem the Flow of Cash to Militants

news.abstract: Investigators probing attacks on Israeli targets in Mombasa, Kenya, study evidence that East Africa has served as both useful base and target for Al Qaeda terror network for nearly decade; photo; Kenyan official Julius Sunkuli, cordinating probe with US and Israel, says Qaeda cannot be ruled out, although police have few leads into bombing of hotel and attempted missile attack on Israeli airliner; hotel attack killed ten Kenyans and 3 Israelis; police release American woman and her Spanish husband who apparently were trying to leave city because they were frightened; 6 Pakistanis and 4 Somalis are being questioned; Qaeda operations are especially difficult to track through Africa's porous borders (M)
news.title: After Attack, Kenya Traces Qaeda's Trail in East Africa

news.abstract: Bali's tourism-based economy has collapsed in wake of Oct terrorist attack on disco; return of foreign visitors is only starting again; economists do not expect early recovery; say quick progress in arresting attack suspects could spur foreign governments to drop travel warnings; photos (M)
news.title: Bali's Broken Economy: As Fragile as an Eggshell

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  While most major Asian technology companies evolved from a skilled manufacturing base, Hong Kong's largest conglomerate, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd., has taken a telecom road less traveled.
news.title: BIZTECH: Hutchison's uphill struggle for 3G glory

news.abstract: Orthodox priests in Greece are pressing for change in priestly dress code; some want permission to shed outer robe when not performing formal church service; others want permission to wear casual garb on streets; some even want beard requirement eased; many Greek Orthodox priests outside Greece dress much like Roman Catholic priests, with no complaints from superiors; photo (M)
news.title: Athens Journal; The Priests in Black Yearn for Unorthodox Attire

news.abstract: Britain released a dossier today on what it called the systematic rape, torture and executions of Iraqis by Saddam Hussein.
news.title: Britain Accuses Hussein of Systematic Torture and Killing

news.abstract: United Nations weapons inspectors and Iraqi officials, with only 13 of 1,000 suspected weapons sites checked so far, have already set pattern of tension and intrigue that is barely covered over with polite humor and vows of mutual interest; both inspectors and Iraqis have entered process knowing that war would be likely if inspections flounder or uncover new pattern of Iraqi deceit, and that generation of iron-fisted rule under Pres Saddam Hussein is hanging in balance; inspectors' grinding task is burdened by knowledge that hawks in Bush administration have scant faith in their ability to strip Iraq of its weapons of mass destruction after evasion and intransigence with which Iraqis met earlier generation of UN inspectors in 1990's; some in current UN inspection team suspect that Washington hard-liners might prefer them to fail, to clear path to military showdown; inspectors are caught between Americans and Iraqis, each pushing in different direction, as they set about task of huge technical and logistical complexity; photos (L)
news.title: U.N. Team Gets to Work, Wary of Both Iraq and U.S.

news.abstract: United States Amb to Japan Howard H Baker Jr says Washington could respond with surprising speed to engage with North Korea if that country takes verifiable steps to dismantle its nuclear weapons program; says Pres Bush has made clear that he does not want conflict with North Korea (S)
news.title: Offering an Incentive to Disarm

news.abstract: Russia expels two Swedish diplomats in reprisal for earlier expulsion of Russian diplomats from Stockholm; controversy stems from claim that Russians were participating in industrial espionage while in Sweden (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Swedish Diplomats Expelled

news.abstract: CIA investigates informant's accusation that Iraq obtained particularly virulent strain of smallpox from Russian scientist; American officials say several American scientists were told in August that Iraq might have obtained mysterious strain from Nelja N Maltseva, virologist who worked for more than 30 years at Research Institute for Viral Preparations in Moscow before her death two years ago; photo (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Hunts Iraq Tie to Soviet Smallpox

news.abstract: Dora Bakoyanni, first woman to be elected mayor of Athens, Greece, is one of most popular politicians in country with dismal record of representation by women in government; her dramatic life story has repeatedly intersected with darker chapters of Greece's recent past; her father, Constantine Mitsotakis, was prominent politician who was arrested in 1967 when military junta seized control of country; he then fled country with his family, returning in 1973 to be arrested again; he was released next year when junta fell; her husband, Pavlos Bakoyanni, an opponent of junta, was gunned down in 1989 by Nov 17 Group, which aimed its attacks at prominent public officials in Greece in effort to destabilize country; photo (M)
news.title: New Athens Mayor Embodies a New Greece
